en: Cook, hey cook! Cook, hey cook!
en_old: Cook, hey cook! Cook, hey cook!

brh: بس کنا مار اما ایراغ داسکان تیار اف بس کنا مار داسہ تیار مریکک بورچی انداخستاوار کرٹ کٹ گٹ کنا دم درینگا اسل بمپکک اما نی تینٹ تیار کریسو نہ نہ کنا مار کنے بورچی خانہ غان خورس بریکک اما
en: Just a moment, my son, but the food isn't ready yet. Just a moment, my son, it's getting ready now. The cook... [garbled]... I got tired, it isn't coming at all. But you could make it yourself. No, no, my son, I'm scared of the kitchen, but...
en_old: Just a moment, my son, but the food isn't ready yet. Just, my son, it's getting ready now. The cook put something in... my breath got stuck, it isn't coming at all. But you could have made it yourself. No, no, my son, I'm a little scared of the kitchen, but...

brh: ما کنا خیال پئی کہ ہموڑے جن ارے، اما جن داڑے تو بفک، نہ کنا مسڑ داڑے ہچ جن من افک، دا شعیب کے پاننگٹی ئے شعیب کنا مار انتئے دنو ہیت کننگٹیس، ایڑے خلیفپہ، اما ابا ہادے، کنا مسڑ
en: Well, I thought there was a jinn there, but a jinn doesn't come here. No, my daughter, there's no jinn here at all. It's Shoaib who's saying this. Shoaib, my son, why are you saying things like that? Don't scare your sister. But Dad, that one... my daughter.
en_old: Well, I thought there was a jinn there, but a jinn doesn't come here. No, my daughter, there's no jinn here at all. This is what Shoaib is saying. Shoaib, my son, why are you saying things like that? Don't scare your sister. But Dad, it's that... my daughter...

brh: ایڑ ابا نا بورچی خانہ نا تہٹی نانے بھاز وڑ نا کسر دیٹ ہنتے۔
en: Sister, inside Dad's kitchen, for us, [there are] many kinds of paths...
en_old: Brother, so many kinds of things have been seen inside Dad's kitchen.

brh: چوکیدار او چوکیدار ہا انت سے کنا بارا دے کڑین سمائی نا بارا
en: Watchman, hey watchman! Yes, what is it? [Tell] me about this... about the [ghost?]...
en_old: Watchman, hey watchman! What is it? Tell me about this... about the ghost.

brh: نی امر سما اف؟ نی دا ریسٹ ہاؤس نا چوکیدار ئس ئے دا ریسٹ ہاؤس نا چوکیدار اٹ، نا باوہ نا چوکیدار افٹ۔ ہن تے دا باوے پٹ۔
en: How do you not know? You're the watchman of this rest house. I'm the watchman of this rest house, not your father's watchman. Go and ask your father about it.
en_old: How do you not know? You're the watchman of this rest house. I'm the watchman of this rest house, not your father's watchman. Go ask your father about it.

brh: اما ئے کاوا بئے وریوے، ہاوے نورتہ کیر ہنگینا، خیال کیس ایرین پین، انتئے ایرین
en: But I'm going... [garbled]... going... be careful, [it's] something else... why...?
en_old: But he brought the cooking pot, and then he was going over there. You were thinking it was something else. Why something else?

brh: او جنارے او خلوکے جن منف ابائے ننا دا کین نی ہرتا کنا مار ابائے تینا توار کرک اوہو
en: Oh, there's a jinn! Oh, it's going to hit [me]! There's no jinn. Dad, this one of ours... where are you? My son is calling his dad. Oh ho!
en_old: Hey, there's a jinn! Hey, it's going to hit me! There's no jinn. Dad, this one of ours... where are you? My son, Dad is calling you. Oh ho!

brh: اینو چکل نا زیات افک؟ ہو صبح نا دنو ہچو گڑاس کنتنوٹ۔
en: Isn't there a lot of [it] today? Yes, I haven't eaten anything like this since morning.
en_old: Isn't there much fog today? Yes, we didn't see anything like this in the morning.

brh: زیات بننگٹی ڈاکٹرے ناسے دا ہرا ڈاکٹر ئس ارے کہ ایتنے نشان ایتو اسہ تس ارے اونا خو شکل مئے نوس کا خنتنوٹ کہ
en: Lots [of people] are coming to the doctor... What kind of doctor is this, who has shown himself only once? I haven't even seen his face properly...
en_old: Too many are coming to the doctor... What kind of doctor is this who showed us one sign? We didn't even see his face properly, that...

brh: ہمار اوسی خبر اف ہرا وخت بریک ہرا وخت کائیک ہچ سما تفت۔ شاری نسی ایڈ ڈاکٹر آک بازو
en: We have no news of him at all, when he comes or when he goes; we have no idea at all. In the city, doctors are many...
en_old: We don't know about him at all, when he comes and when he goes, we had no idea. In the city, the doctors are many...

brh: دا ہس طاقت نن ایرا دے کے نن کانتنے نشان تس دا ہس طاقت مسکتو نن تنے مالو نشان تس نن تنے نن او
en: This much power... Two days ago we... showed you a sign. If there had been this much power, we would have shown ourselves earlier... we... ourselves... we... oh.
en_old: This much strength... the day we came, we showed you a sign. If there had been this much strength, we would have shown you a sign earlier. We... you... we...

brh: دے دا دے امر گدریفنے او نن ایماتو انتئے سرکار اوفتے پیسے تفک او سرکار نا تنخواہ نا اراڑے پرواہ کے تانکے نن کوننگا غریب آتے چوٹ
en: How will this day be got through? And we... because the government doesn't give them money, and he hardly cares about the government salary, until we poor people... [unclear]...
en_old: How will we get through the day? And we... because the government doesn't give them money, and who cares about the government's salary? Until... we are called the poor ones...

brh: ہندن دانہ کتک تفوک مرے ہندن تموک مرے تانکہ تانکہ دا ہاکتنے دا ہندن تفوک سلوک ذلیل
en: Let him stay tied up like this, let him lie fallen like this, until... until he says yes, let him stay like this, tied up, motionless and humiliated.
en_old: Just like this, let him be tied up, let him be left lying there, so that this one dies like this, tied up, disgraced.

brh: باسٹ ئے ٹھو بندہ غاسے، بائے تینا نی پاش ہس بہ کپر، اسل بائے تینا ملپ، ایلو، ایلے تا کہ بائے تینا ملپ
en: He's a tough man. He won't let anything out of his mouth; he won't open his mouth at all. The other one... leave him, so that he doesn't open his mouth.
en_old: Brother, he is a very good man. Don't reveal your own brother; don't let your own brother down at all. The other one, leave him, so that he doesn't let his brother down.

brh: آخر بایتنے ملکتہ، ہنداڑے تفوک مرے تمبوک مرے، او ہا، اینو آن پد تانا دیرم بندے مئے رختم بندے
en: In the end he didn't open his mouth. Let him be tied up right here, let him lie fallen here. And yes, from today on his water is cut off, and his food is cut off too.
en_old: In the end he came to the country. Let him be tied up right here, let him lie there. Oh yes, from today on his water is cut off, his bread is cut off.

brh: سمجھارے؟ میجر صاحب ئے تفاوت آتے گولیس نا بواچی کیو لاخرونا داتے دنزو کسو یفک داتے
en: Do you understand? Major sahib, ... instead of a bullet, I will make these weak; these won't be killed so quickly.
en_old: Do you understand? The major sahib will put a gun to these differences... these won't be let go like this...

brh: آستہ آستہ ئے خوراکا غب غب کمزور کروئیے، ہندن دادے کمزور کروئیے تو کہ بلا درخت ٹھکاکے تن۔ میر صاحب ئے تو دائے حیرانٹ۔
en: Slowly, slowly he must be weakened through his food, bit by bit; he must be weakened like this, so that he comes crashing down like a big tree. Mir sahib, I am really amazed at this.
en_old: Slowly, slowly, starve him of food and weaken him; weaken him like this so that the tree gets cut down. As for Mir Sahib, he is amazed at this.

brh: کہ دا ننا خلاف گواہی ء مریک، ضرور ننا دشمن تا سر ء تتو ننگا تے حوصلہ تک، اور ننا خلاف۔ او گلو، نی راست پاریس۔
en: If this one becomes a witness against us, he will surely embolden our enemies, and against us. O Gulu, you spoke the truth.
en_old: Since this is a testimony against us, he has surely encouraged our enemies' heads, and against us. Oh Gul, you spoke the truth.

brh: دا ولنگا پنجگتا ہن حیثیت اسے کہ میر نا مورا بشمرے میر صاحب اینو داڑان ضرور معلوم کیوہ کہ ننا دشمن دیر اسے۔ ہاؤ
en: Does this one have such standing that he could stand up in front of the Mir? Mir sahib, today I will surely find out from him who our enemy is. Yes.
en_old: Has this wretch got the standing to stand up before the Mir? Mir Sahib, today I will surely find out from him who our enemy is. Yes.

brh: نی داڑان زو ملوک ئس
en: You'll be set loose from here quickly.
en_old: You got free of here quickly.

brh: باورچی او باورچی باورچی او باورچی ہنم ئس کنا اما اما ایراغ داسکان تیو
en: Cook, O cook! Cook, O cook! ... My mother, mother, isn't the food ready yet?
en_old: Cook, oh cook! Cook, oh cook! You son of... my mother, mother, the food is still not ready.

brh: بس کنا مار دا سے تیار مریکک بورچی انداخس توار کریک کہ گٹ کنا دم درنگا اسل بمبکک اما نی تینٹ تیار کریسو نہ نہ کنا مار کنے بورچی خانہ غان خوری سے بریکک اما
en: Just a moment, my son, it's being made ready right now. I've called out to the cook so much that my throat... I'm completely out of breath. Mother, did you make it yourself? No, no, my son, a dish was coming to me from the kitchen, dear.
en_old: Just as my son was getting ready, the cook shouted so much that my breath was completely taken away. Mother, did you prepare it yourself? No, no, my son, he brought food for me from the kitchen, mother.

brh: کنا خیال پی کنا موڑ جن ارے۔ اماں جن داڑتو بفک۔ نہ کنا مسڑ داڑے ہچ جن من افک۔ دا شیپ کہ پا ننگٹیء۔ شیپ کنا مار اینتے دون ایت کہ ننگٹوس ایڑے خلیف پی اماں
en: I think there's a jinn around me. Mother, jinn don't come here. No, my daughter, there's no jinn or anything here at all. This..., my son, why do you go on like this... Don't frighten us like that, dear.
en_old: I think my daughter-in-law is fine. Mother, she is not coming here. No, my daughter is not well here at all. This sheep is... the sheep, my son, why are you...

brh: بارادے کنا مسڑ ابا نا بورچی نا رندا ٹینانی بھاز واری کرے دے چنتئے
en: ... my daughter, father's cook... after him... many times...
en_old: When my daughter, about father's cook, cried a lot and so on...

brh: او چوکیدار! او چوکیدار! ہا، انت اسے؟ کنا باراٹی۔ کنے انت سما ہی نا باراٹی کہ؟ نی امر سما اف؟ نی دروشت اوس نا چوکیدار ئس
en: O watchman! O watchman! Yes, what is it? About my father. What would I know about your father? How can you not know? You are the watchman of this rest house.
en_old: Oh watchman! Oh watchman! Yes, what is it? About me? What do I know about you? How do you not know? You were the watchman of the whole...

brh: ئے دا ریسٹ ہاؤس نا چوکیدار اٹ، نا باوہ نا چوکیدار افٹ، اینتے دا باوائے پٹ، اما ئے کاوہ باہی ہریوے
en: I am the watchman of this rest house, I'm not your father's watchman. Why? Search for this father of yours. Mother, I'll go and look outside.
en_old: I am the watchman of this rest house, I am not your father's watchman. Why should I look for your father? Mother, ... go and look.

brh: او نرتہ ہنگنا خیال کیس ایرن پیس انتئے ایرن جن ارے او خلوک جن من اف ابا نا ننداکے نی نرتہ کنا مار ابا تینٹ
en: Oh, are you thinking of running away? Don't go in there. Why? There's a jinn there, and it's not a harmful jinn or anything. Father's... you ran off, my son; father himself...
en_old: Did you think of running away? Don't go, why? Iran is fine, it's not a bad place. Father's sitting place... you run away, my son, father himself...

brh: توار کرک ئے نو
en: He's calling out, you know.
en_old: He is calling, you know.

brh: جکہ نا زیات افک، ہو، سوبنائی، تنے چہ گلاس کن تنٹ، افف، زیات بننگٹی، ڈاکٹر ایناسے، داڑے ارا ڈاکٹر ئس ارے کے
en: Isn't your cough any worse? Yes. Since this morning... I gave you a few glasses... No, it's getting worse. A doctor... is there any doctor here?
en_old: Not much of the place... yes, ... give you a few glasses... it's getting worse, a doctor came... is there a doctor here?

brh: ایتنے نشان ئتو اسٹو سرے، اونا خو شکلی مئے نو اسکا خنتنوٹ کے ہمار اوسی، خبر اف ہرا وختہ بریک، ہرا وختہ کائیک
en: There's just a sign of him, but I haven't even seen his face to this day, though he lives right there. Who knows what time he comes and what time he goes.
en_old: There was a sign of him, but I haven't even seen his face yet, though he's around. Who knows when he comes and when he goes.

brh: شاری نا سے ایڑے ڈاکٹر آک بازو؟ داخس طاقت ننے ارادہ کے نن کان تینے
en: Are there many doctors there in the city? Do we have the strength to go there ourselves?
en_old: Are there many doctors there in the city? How much strength and resolve do we have for ourselves?

brh: شارت دا ہستاکت مسکتو نن تینے مالو نشاستس نن تینا ننودے داڑے امر گدرپین او نن مالو انتئے
en: If there had been this hospital in the city, we would have known ourselves... how would we get through our nights and days here, and why would we...
en_old: If this had happened, we would have known ourselves how we will spend our days here, and why we...

brh: سرکار اوفتے پیسہ تیفک؟ او سرکار نا تنخواہ نا ہراڑے پرواہ کیک۔ تانکہ نن کونگا غریباتی چونٹی تونو اوفتا دیگ گدری پسی۔ داسہ گڑا ہمک کیو انت کیو؟
en: Doesn't the government give them money? And where does he care about a government salary? Unless they fleece us poor people, their pots won't keep boiling. So now what do I do, what do I do?
en_old: Does the government give them money? And who cares about the government's salary? As long as we feed the poor, their pots keep cooking. So now what do I do, what do I do?

brh: ستے تنے نی لدائی تتے نی دن کرک کہ ہمو بلوچینگا دوائی تے مچ ایلار تے اوفتے مچ آرام ملیک بش مئے اینک جوان دا ستے
en: ... you gave him the medicine. You do it like this: those Baloch remedies, they all take them, they all get relief and get back on their feet. This is good like this.
en_old: ...you gave the medicine, you do it like this: those Baloch remedies, they all get relief, they get well. This is good.

brh: نی ارانگینا اسس؟ دا
en: Where were you? This...
en_old: Where were you? This...

brh: بورچی نی تبار کنے کنا سوٹ، بلیڑے کسے سے خناٹ۔ جیون دیر اسس کہ؟ خبر اف دیر اسس، ئے بورچی خانہ نا خیرے اناٹ، دانگی گوراٹ تو۔
en: Cook, get my suit ready for me. Listen, I saw someone over there. Then who was it? I don't know who it was. I was by the kitchen, I looked this way, and...
en_old: Cook, tell me, my suit... I saw someone there. Was it water? I don't know, it was water. I was coming out of the kitchen, near here.

brh: خبرہ فرنگا ہبمس اینی فارغ اٹ کہ دا کوبین ورا سے جن استولم اوہو کاڈے جن من ہرا ہبمس تو گرا ڈیرس ہکا ہندا توئی تے کہ او ڈیرس
en: ... now I'm free, so this ... a kind of ... jinn ... oh, ... a jinn or anything, which ... then a lot ... right there ... that oh, a lot.
en_old: ...I'm free now... this... jinn... oh, the jinn that... then a lot...

brh: دا شعیب ارادے؟ شعیب تو نا رندٹ ٹرائی کرے ٹک۔ شعیب کنا رندٹ ٹرائی کریس؟ انتئے الستاء؟ نی کہ وری کریس کنا خاطر نا رندٹ ٹرائی کرت۔ داسہ اینو تک۔
en: Is this Shoaib? Shoaib tried to come after you. Shoaib, you tried to come after me? Why...? Since you were worried for my sake, he tried to follow. Now today...
en_old: Is this Shoaib? Shoaib tried to follow you. Shoaib tried to follow me? Why...? You... he tried to follow for my sake. Now today...

brh: ئے خلوئی چنا
en: I have to hit it, child.
en_old: Hit it, child.

brh: ابا ابا چوکیدار بورچی ہراڑے کیورے جی صاحب انمس شعیب ہراڑے کنے خبر اف
en: Father, father! Watchman! Cook! Where are you? Yes, sir, what happened? Where is Shoaib? I don't know.
en_old: Father, father! Watchman, cook, where are you? Yes, sir. Where is Shoaib? I don't know.

brh: ئے بورچی خانے ٹی اسوٹ۔ صاحب کنا خیال پئے ئے کتو وار بس۔ کانپورٹ تا۔ دا سبی نا چل درویش نا قصہ ئے افوہ۔
en: I was in the kitchen. Sir, I think he came once... This is the story of the forty dervishes of Sibi, isn't it?
en_old: I was in the kitchen. Sir, I think it came once... This is the story of the forty dervishes of Sibi, isn't it?

brh: چڑے باٹی نن دا کسے، اندا کسے بینیفٹ بینیفٹ ئے تنگ بسوٹ، امر کہ مرے آئی، اینو دا کسے بینیو، اوہو ئے تو چلتن لمشہ نا دیوانہ مسونس، آخر دیر پارے ننے چے
en: ... we, this story, that story, telling and telling, I got fed up. However it may be, today let me hear this story. Oh, you've gone crazy over Chiltan...; in the end, who told us...?
en_old: ...we this person, that person, benefit, benefit, I got fed up. How could it be... today this person... oh, you've gone crazy over Chiltan... in the end, what did the water tell us?

brh: دا چل درویشاک، بھلا تو تومر جنگ کریر۔ پاریر کہ درویشاتے تون علم نا طاقت اسس، اور علم باز بھلو طاقت اسے۔
en: These forty dervishes then fought a great war. They said that the dervishes had the power of knowledge, and knowledge is a very great power.
en_old: These forty dervishes fought a great war. They said that the dervishes had the power of knowledge, and knowledge is a very great power.

brh: علم اٹ جتا خست آ ختارے، ہو کنا مار، علم آن بلو طاقت اسل اف، علم نا روشنائی آن تار
en: They won with knowledge ... Yes, my son, there is no power at all greater than knowledge; from the light of knowledge, dark- ...
en_old: With knowledge they defeated the enemy in a different way. Yes, my son, there is truly no power greater than knowledge; it is the light of knowledge, remember.

brh: مر مرے مر مریک، ئے ہم، ئے ہم دا طاقت ء ضرور حاصل کیوے۔ انت پاریس کنا مار؟ ہچ نہ باوا، ہم چاکو۔
en: Come what may, I too, I too will surely gain this power. What did you say, my son? Nothing, father, just so.
en_old: Whatever happens, I too, I too will surely gain this power. What did you say, my son? Nothing, father, I'll see too.

brh: گلو جی میر صاحب اینو چنا کسوئے
en: Gullu! Yes, Mir Sahib, today the children ... (unclear).
en_old: Gullu ji, Mir Sahib, today the children are studying.

brh: ئے نو اسکا داڑے کسے اسکول اینتنے بغیر کنا اجازت آن دا چنا کما اسکول اینانو ہما اسکول اینانو
en: Until today nobody here has ever gone to school. Without my permission these children have gone to school? Gone to that school?
en_old: Now who here has opened a school without my permission? Who brought these children to school, to which school?

brh: چناک، ماسٹر جاگہ جاگہ غا ہننگے، ارا ارا ٹی پاننگے کہ تینا چناک کے اسکول آ راہی کبو۔ اور مخلوق ہم تینا چناک کے اسکول آ راہی کننگٹی ئے میر صاحب۔ حیف، حیف! ننے اسکان اسے ماسٹر ئس داڑے ہرا دے گرفت او۔
en: The children: the master is going from place to place, telling people in house after house, 'Send your children to school.' And the people too are sending their children to school, Mir Sahib. Alas, alas! A single master here, getting a grip this far, right up to us!
en_old: The children... the master is going from place to place, telling people in every house to send their children to school. And people are also sending their children to school, Mir Sahib. Shame, shame! We had never had a master here who would get hold of this.

brh: او دا ہنو اسکا تولوک ئے ضرور دا نراں در تا طاقت نا سر ئے کہ دا داڑے بے ہم توسونے۔ باز افسوس نی تسی۔ نی ہم کنے افسوس ئے او نی ہم کنے افسوس ئے ماسٹر تولوک ئے خوانفنگٹ چناک کے اور نمے ووٹ نا سمک ہم پک۔ واہ یار!
en: And this one is still sitting here to this day; surely there is some power behind him, that he has settled here so carefree. What a great pity about you! I am disappointed in you too, and in you too. The master sits teaching the children, and he won't even give you a vote. Wow, man!
en_old: He has come and is sitting here; surely there is some power behind him that he has come here fearlessly. It's very sad of you. You, too, I'm disappointed in you; and you too, I'm disappointed in you. The master sits teaching the children, and he won't even give you a vote. Wow, man!

brh: واہ باز افسوس نا ہیت اسے میر جلال خان نا طاقت اینو مدس کہ دادے ایشانتے تنورے ہندا خاطر دا ہرامٹ تولوکے نم کنا خاص انگا بندہ آکورے ماسٹر بدا ہم تولوکے میر صاحب اگہ نما
en: Wow, it is a matter of great regret: has Mir Jalal Khan's power come to this today, that these people ... him? That is why this one sits here at ease. You are my special men. The master is still sitting there too, Mir Sahib; if your ...
en_old: Wow, it is a very sad thing that Mir Jalal Khan's power today is such that these people don't listen to him. That's why the one sitting here, you are my special men. A master is also sitting. Mir Sahib, if your...

brh: گم رے! تو نن اینو دانا کلے قصہ ء تمام کینہ۔ نہ نہ گلو نہ، جذبات آن نہ، عقل آن کار حل عقل آن۔ دشمن آ ہندن وار ئس کر۔
en: Come on, man! Then today we'll finish off his whole story. No, no, Gullu, no, not with emotion; the job gets done with reason, with reason. Deal the enemy such a blow
en_old: Get lost! Then today we will finish his whole story. No, no, Gullu, no, not with emotions; work is solved with reason, with reason. Strike the enemy in such a way

brh: تا کہ او نا فرشتہ غاک ہم خبر تمیر کہ اور تو انتس مس گلو کنا ایت نا بومانی نا ڈورینا یو بابو کنتو
en: that even his angels come to know what has happened to him. Gullu, ... my word ... (unclear) ... with me.
en_old: that even his angels won't know what happened to him. Gullu, ... my ... (partly unintelligible)

brh: ہیلو، ہاں انسپکٹر صاحب، اوڑے کریرے، جیا اونا سر مسونو۔
en: Hello, yes, Inspector Sahib. Did you do it there? Yes, they have got to him.
en_old: Hello, yes Inspector Sahib, have you done it there? Yes, it has been taken care of.

brh: شام کننگن نما انتظار مننگٹیٹی جی جی اچھا خڑک رے ہا ٹھیک ہی ٹھیک ٹھیک مہربانی
en: We'll be waiting for you in the evening. Yes, yes, alright, it's near, man. Yes, fine, fine, fine, thank you.
en_old: We are waiting for you this evening. Yes, yes, alright, okay, yes fine, fine, fine, thank you.

brh: اوڑا اوفتے ئنا ہم براہوئی ادب نا زبان نا حوالہ اٹ اوڑا اوفتے تورا سے مچ ہرس کرین اسہ ادارہ ئس پلار ہرا نا پی تخر براہوئی پبلیکیشن سہی فرید احمد ئنا نا ڈاکٹر صاحب انت اسہ سرپرست ئس اسہ کہ سائیں جوڑ ئس کاریم کرین
en: There, they too, with regard to Brahui literature and language, there we gathered them all together and set up an institution whose name they made Brahui Publication, right. Farid Ahmad's ... Doctor Sahib, well, was a patron, and we did quite good work.
en_old: There, regarding them and in relation to Brahui literature and language, they gathered together and established an institution named Brahui Publication, ... Farid Ahmad's ... Doctor Sahib was a patron, and they did a lot of work together.

brh: آن اللہ اختارنی واختار لی اصحابی، او انساناک، او شیخ عبدالقادر جیلانی رحمتہ اللہ علیہ پیرانی پیر رحمتہ اللہ علیہ تولوک ئے بغداد ٹی، خلیفہ آپونا تولوک او غور ٹی
en: 'Inna Allaha ikhtarani wa-khtara li ashabi' (Allah chose me and chose my Companions for me). O people, Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him), the Pir of Pirs (may Allah have mercy on him), is sitting in Baghdad, and his khalifas are sitting attentively.
en_old: Indeed Allah chose me and chose for me my companions. O people, Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him), the Pir of Pirs, was sitting in Baghdad, and your caliph was sitting there in Ghor.

brh: اسٹ ئس بس خلیفہ اسونا اولو خلیفہ ئس پارے حضرت اگر نن اللہ نا نبی نا دور آ مروست، اللہ نا نبی ء تینا خنتٹ خنوسٹ امر جوان ئس کنے ایت سمجھو ہبنی گٹے۔
en: One of them came, a khalifa of his, a senior khalifa, and said: Hazrat, if we had been in the era of the Prophet of Allah and had seen the Prophet of Allah with our own eyes, how good it would have been! ... (unclear)
en_old: Once, there was a caliph; the first caliph said: 'Hazrat, if we had been in the time of the Prophet of Allah, and seen the Prophet of Allah with our own eyes, how good it would have been.' Explain the matter to me...

brh: شوبہ سمجھاتی لگے نی نی الس سدھ نا او سرسری تے ہتہ کے لگے نی ئے اللہ نا نبی شیخ عبدالقادر جیلانی رحمتہ اللہ علیہ او نا خلیفہ پارے حضرت نن اللہ نا نبی نا دورہ مرو
en: ... (unclear) ... the Prophet of Allah. Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him): his khalifa said, 'Hazrat, if we had been in the era of the Prophet of Allah ...'
en_old: Explain it... you... (partly unintelligible) the Prophet of Allah... Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him), his caliph said: 'Hazrat, if we had been in the time of the Prophet of Allah...'

brh: امر جوانس تینا خنتیٹ اللہ نا نبی ء خنانا او نا رندا نماز خوانانا آ او نا ایتا تے بنگونا امر جوانس شیخ عبدالقادر غنیۃ الطالبین ٹی دا واقعہ ء
en: How good it would have been! We would have seen the Prophet of Allah with our own eyes, prayed behind him, and heard his words. How good! Sheikh Abdul Qadir relates this incident in Ghunyat al-Talibin.
en_old: How fortunate was the one who saw the Prophet of Allah with his own eyes, prayed behind him and heard his words. How fortunate... Shaykh Abdul Qadir, in Ghunyat al-Talibin, [narrates] this incident.

brh: شیخ عبدالقادر جیلانی رحمۃ اللہ علیہ فرمائفے او کمبخت اگر نی اللہ نا نبی نا دور آ مروستس نی ابوجہل آن بدتر مروستس دا کل تولوک آ حیران حضرت انتھی دست کریس
en: Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'O wretch, if you had been in the era of the Prophet of Allah, you would have been worse than Abu Jahl.' All those sitting there were astonished: 'Hazrat, why did you say this?'
en_old: Shaykh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'O wretch, if you had lived in the time of the Prophet of Allah, you would have been worse than Abu Jahl.' Everyone sitting there was astonished: 'Hazrat, why did you say that?'

brh: دا خلیفہ دا عالم دادے پاننگ اٹی کہ اگر تو اللہ نا نبی نا دورہ بیتیتہ تو ابو جھل نا چم کنڈہ غا بیتیتہ پر حضرت انتئے
en: This khalifa, this scholar: he is telling him that if you had been in the era of the Prophet of Allah, you would have been on Abu Jahl's side. 'But Hazrat, why?'
en_old: This caliph, this scholar, is saying that if you had been in the era of the Prophet of Allah, you would have been on Abu Jahl's side. But Hazrat, why?

brh: وضاحت کرک شیخ عبدالقادر جیلانی رحمۃ اللہ علیہ فرمائفے اللہ نا نبی چودہ سو سال مست فرمائفے نی آن اللہ اختاری واختار لی اصحابی او انساناک اللہ کنے تمام نبی تیا
en: He explains: Sheikh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him) said that fourteen hundred years ago the Prophet of Allah said, 'Inna Allaha ikhtarani wa-khtara li ashabi': O people, Allah [chose] me from among all the prophets ...
en_old: He explains: Shaykh Abdul Qadir Jilani (may Allah have mercy on him) said that the Prophet of Allah said fourteen hundred years ago, 'Allah chose me and chose my Companions for me.' Those people... Allah [chose] me over all the prophets...

brh: چانٹی کرے نی کشانے واختار لی اصحابی تمام انسان تا تیان چانٹی کرے نی کنا صحابہ غاتے کشانے او تو چانٹی مسنو فا اگر نی وروسس مسوسو
en: He selected me, He picked me out; 'wa-khtara li ashabi': from among all human beings He selected, He picked out my Companions. And so they are the chosen ones; so if you had come ... had been ...
en_old: He chose: you were selected, 'wakhtar li ashabi'. From all mankind He chose; He selected my Companions. They were the chosen ones, so if you had been there...

brh: نبی علیہ السلام فرمائفے او کنا امتی او پدنا بروکاک اگر نم احد مشنا کچا صدقہ کیرے احد مدینہ ٹی مش سے چھے کلو میٹر اونا لمبائی ئے
en: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'O my ummah, O you who come later, if you give charity the size of Mount Uhud ...' Uhud is a mountain in Medina; its length is six kilometres.
en_old: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: 'O my followers, those who come after, if you give charity equal to Mount Uhud...' Uhud is a mountain in Medina, about six kilometres long.

brh: واللہ او مش اسے، اللہ نا نبی فرمائفے او پد نا ئے و نی، نن نم کلاک، اگر احد مش نا کچہ صدقہ کیر، گڑا صحابہ غا کسے مٹس غلہ نا صدقہ کیر، دا نا ثواب احد آن زیادہ ئے
en: By God, it is a mountain. The Prophet of Allah said: 'O later ones, I and you, we, you, all of us: if you give charity the size of Mount Uhud, and then one of the Companions gives a handful of grain in charity, his reward is greater than Uhud.'
en_old: By Allah, it is a mountain. The Prophet of Allah said: 'O those who come after, and you, all of you: if you gave charity equal to Mount Uhud, and one of the Companions gave a handful of grain in charity, its reward would be greater than Uhud.'

brh: او کینرا سے مسٹ تو ئیو رسالہ سے نا اجرائی کرے سجا سے او پاپا دے لیٹر بھلو خواریاٹ ہمے دوریاٹ پوسٹ افس نا انتس دا ہمے التاتے ٹو تے تینا
en: And when ... (unclear) ..., then he launched a ... magazine, ... and a letter to Papa, with great hardship, from that distance, through the post office or something ... these same ... his own ...
en_old: When he was... he launched a new magazine... and the father [sent] a letter with great difficulty from that distance, through the post office... these... his own...

brh: صحابہ دا دے پارے اللہ نا نبی پیرنگائے پارے او پیرنگا نا ایرا درخت داڑے ارے پارے ہا اللہ نا نبی ارے نبی علیہ الصلوۃ والسلام پارے
en: The Companions told him this. The Prophet of Allah said to the old man: 'O old man, are your two trees here?' He said: 'Yes, O Prophet of Allah, they are.' The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said ...
en_old: The Companions said that day: 'O Prophet of Allah, the old man...' He said: 'Is the old man's tree here?' They said: 'Yes, O Prophet of Allah, it is.' The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said...

brh: دا نوجوان کوش کن مسلمان مسونے دادے ارادے رختے پیرنگائے حضرت دے فرات اللہ نا نبی پائے دے فرات اللہ نا نبی فرما
en: This young man has recently become a Muslim, and he has an intention in mind ... To the old man, Hazrat ... the Prophet of Allah says ..., the Prophet of Allah sa[id] ...
en_old: This young man had recently become a Muslim. He had this intention... the old man... Hazrat said, the Prophet of Allah said...

brh: او ماما پیرنگا، دافتہ قیمت ال، لیکن ایت تا، پارے اللہ نا نبی قیمت ہم دے پر، الپر، قیمت کٹم تے نا درختاتے دے پر، اللہ نا نبی مسٹمی کوئیتء کننگٹ او پیرنگا
en: 'O uncle, old man, take their price, but give them [to him].' He said: 'O Prophet of Allah, I won't give them even for a price, I won't take it; for a price ... I won't give the trees.' The Prophet of Allah was trying for the third time with the old man.
en_old: 'O uncle, old man, take their price, but give [the trees].' He said: 'O Prophet of Allah, give the price too... take the price... the trees...' The Prophet of Allah tried three times with the old man.

brh: او بن کنا ایتے اگر نی دا ارادہ تختے دا نوجوانی ایتیس ئے محمد جنت ٹی اللہ غان ہلی وی ارادہ تختے ہیتے وی سبحان اللہ دا سو پیرنگا سمجھپنگٹے
en: 'Listen to my word: if you make up your mind to give these to this young man, I, Muhammad, will take one for you from Allah in Paradise ... make the intention, I will bring it ...' Glory be to God, this old man does not understand.
en_old: He said: 'Listen to my word: if you intend to give these to this young man, Muhammad [promises you a tree] in Paradise from Allah...' Subhanallah, this old man does not understand.

brh: پینگا سمجھ پینگا تے کہ جنتا اللہ نا نبی کنے دا درخت تے تک دو اللہ نا نبی تینا زبان اٹ کنے پاننگ اٹے نی جنتی اوس
en: He doesn't understand, doesn't understand that in Paradise ... The Prophet of Allah asks me for these trees; the Prophet of Allah is telling me with his own tongue, 'You are of the people of Paradise.'
en_old: The old man does not understand that... in Paradise. 'O Prophet of Allah, give me these trees...' 'The Prophet of Allah is telling me with his own tongue that you are among the people of Paradise.'

brh: اللہ نا نبی تینا زبان اٹ کنے پاننگ اٹی ء نی جنتی ئس لیکن پیر انگا پائک پاتے ہادے
en: 'The Prophet of Allah is telling me with his own tongue, You are a dweller of Paradise,' but the old man says ...
en_old: 'The Prophet of Allah is telling me with his own tongue that you are a dweller of Paradise,' but the old man says...

brh: تینا مشورہ غا ٹھیک ئے اگر نی بنفتوس ئے نیان غصہ مریو۔ جوان بابا غصہ کپہ بنفہ وانی۔
en: Your advice is all well and good, but if you don't tell (the story), I'll get angry with you. — Alright, baba, don't be angry, I'll tell it.
en_old: Your advice is right; if you don't listen, I'll be angry with you. Okay, father, don't be angry, I'm listening.

brh: شعیب شعیب شعیب شعیب انو بس شعیب شعیب خنت مل
en: Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib... (unclear)... Shoaib, Shoaib, open your eyes!
en_old: Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib... today just... Shoaib, Shoaib, look...

brh: دیر ئس ہٹ بو زکا زو دیر ئس ہٹ بو شعیب شعیب مل خنتے شعیب خنتے مل خنتے مل ہن مس شعیب صاب دادے شعیب شعیب
en: Bring some water, quick, fast, bring some water! Shoaib, Shoaib, open your eyes! Shoaib, open your eyes, open your eyes! What happened? Shoaib sahib, (look at) him... Shoaib, Shoaib!
en_old: Bring some water, quickly bring some water! Shoaib, Shoaib... did you see? Shoaib, look... Shoaib sahib, this one... Shoaib, Shoaib!

brh: ابا ابا ہمبس ہمبس کنا مار ابا خبرو فیر کسس کنالنگ کے بس ولئی تما شوٹ دانا ویمے نی نی اتینن خلارتے عجب و بندغسس
en: Father, father... (unclear)... my son... Father, ... someone... by God, (he) fell... (unclear)... You, you... (unclear)... what a strange person you are!
en_old: Father, father, that, that, my son, father... what is this... you, you... what a strange person.

brh: او جوان ئے گڑا صاحب ریسٹ ہاؤس نا کھیرانٹ ہموڑے ڈکو ایتے نی کمبو بش مبو
en: Oh, it's fine. Then, sir, at the rest house... over there... (unclear)... you (all)... get up!
en_old: Oh, good. Then, sir, at the rest house... there... don't you... be well.

brh: شاباش حق علم ہنر
en: Well done! Truth, knowledge, skill.
en_old: Well done! Truth, knowledge, skill.

brh: بابا جی چل درویش آتا قصہ بینف دا دیر اسرے
en: Grandpa, tell (me) the story of the forty dervishes — who were they?
en_old: Grandpa, tell me the story of the forty dervishes. Who were they?

brh: کنا مار نی ہم چل درویش تا قصہ نا دیوانہ مسوس آ؟ آخر مار کسے دا قصہ؟ باوا جی
en: My son, have you too gone crazy over the story of the forty dervishes? After all, son, who (told you) this story? — Grandpa...
en_old: My son, have you also gone crazy over the story of the forty dervishes? After all, son, who [told] this story? Father.

brh: کنا ئے ہر شام کنے دا قصہ ء بنفک ولے اینو تسکان پورا متنے۔ قصہ ء بنفیو انے ولے سواری چادن نا لاتھ کنے ٹی شولنگٹی انچو پورا کتے۔ جی۔
en: My (grandpa) tells me this story every evening, but to this day it has never been finished. He'll start telling the story, but... (unclear)... and so it never gets finished. Yes.
en_old: My grandfather tells me this story every evening, but to this day it has never been finished. You start telling the story, but sleep takes over before it's complete. Yes.

brh: باوا جی نم چاکمبو قصہ ء بنف۔ تو بن کنا مار۔
en: Grandpa, drink your tea and tell the story. — So listen, my son.
en_old: Grandpa, tell me the whole story. All right, listen, my son.

brh: دا مودی نا ہیتے کہ چار ما کنڈ آن تارماسکہ چلتن نا مش آن خاخر
en: This is a tale of the time when there was darkness on all four sides, and from the Chiltan mountain, fire...
en_old: This is the story of a time when there was darkness on all four sides, and fire from Chiltan mountain...

brh: بس بیستمک، بلا قضا تسر، اور چلتن نا مشہ تینے قبضہ ئ کرے سر، کنا وارثی وقتس، چل درویشف
en: Then... demons and calamities came, and took Chiltan mountain into their possession. In the time of my forebears, the forty dervishes...
en_old: Then disaster came, calamities fell, and took hold of Chiltan mountain. In the time of my ancestors, the forty dervishes...

brh: دا بشتمار سفر کریسا کریسا کریسا چلتن نا مشان گترینگیسا اندا چلتن نا خورک آ بسو
en: These (men) travelled and travelled and travelled, and passing over the Chiltan mountains they came near this Chiltan.
en_old: Travelling on and on and on, they passed through the Chiltan mountains and came to this spring of Chiltan.

brh: دا درویشاک پیون آ لبیس اٹی کاٹم آ نالیس نٹ اسکا نا سورم پور نور آ چہرہ اوفتہ چہرہ غاک
en: These dervishes were dressed in white from head to foot, with faces full of light — their faces...
en_old: These dervishes were dressed in white, with something on their heads, and their faces shone with light.

brh: نورم بارسر ہر وخت کہ او چلتن نا مش آ سرمسر تو اوفتہ دا فیصلہ مس کہ نن دا
en: (their faces) were like light. And when they reached Chiltan mountain, they decided that we (would)...
en_old: The radiant ones came, and when they reached Chiltan mountain, they decided that we would...

brh: ننے انت ہم وشننے نیامٹی گدریفین۔ او مبلاتی دا عید اسل خوش بتو۔ اوف دا عیدے برداشت کتو۔ مچ آ نن اوفتا نیامٹی مقابلہ مس۔
en: ...whatever happens to us, we will spend (our days) in the midst (of it). And the demons did not like this at all. They could not tolerate this. All night long there was a battle between them.
en_old: We didn't like anything that went on between them. And they were never happy about this Eid. They couldn't stand this Eid. All of us ended up in a contest among them.

brh: اسے گونڈان تارماس ایلو گونڈان روشنائی۔ پار کہ ہمو نن چلتن نا مش آن اسے ہندن و خاخر ئس پیش تما کہ
en: Darkness from one side, light from the other. They say that that night such a fire appeared from Chiltan mountain that...
en_old: Darkness on one side, light on the other. They say that from Chiltan mountain there appeared such a fire that...

brh: خلکنا ڈغار و شنگار سیاہ جوڑ مسر، مون نا سنگار، مچ آ نن دا ڈغار جولانٹ گھونگک، گڑ گڑ تاسک
en: The people's land and (surroundings) turned black, (pitch) black; all night long this earth was rocking like a swing, rumbling and roaring.
en_old: The people's land turned black... all of us... this land was shaking and rumbling.

brh: سہبت کہ مخلوق بش مس خناٹ کہ چلتن نا مش نا خاخر ختم مسنے او چلتن نا مش آ پیون پیون برف ئے
en: In the morning, when the people got up, they saw that the fire on Chiltan mountain had gone out, and on Chiltan mountain there was pure white snow.
en_old: In the morning, when people woke up, they saw that the fire on Chiltan mountain had gone out and Chiltan mountain was covered in pure white snow.

brh: ولے دا چل درویش آتا ہنمس؟ کنا مار خلق والا کو دا کماشاک پارہ کہ ہمو
en: But what became of these forty dervishes? — My son, the village folk, these elders, say that they...
en_old: But where did these forty dervishes go? My son, people, these elders, say that they...

brh: او دیان اینو اسکان ولدا دا چل درویشے کس خنتو۔ باباجی دا چل درویشاک بلا تو تومر جنگ کریر۔ پارہ کہ درویشاتی تون علم نا طاقت اسے۔
en: And from that day until today, no one has seen these forty dervishes again. — Grandpa, how did these forty dervishes fight the demons? — They say the dervishes had the power of knowledge.
en_old: And from that day to this, no one has seen these forty dervishes again. Grandpa, these forty dervishes must have fought a great battle. They say the dervishes had the power of knowledge.

brh: اور علم باز بلو طاقت اسے۔ انت؟ علم ٹی داخس طاقت ارے؟ ہاؤ کنا مار، علم آن بلو طاقت اسل اف۔
en: And knowledge is a very great power. — What? Is there that much power in knowledge? — Yes, my son, there is no power at all greater than knowledge.
en_old: And knowledge is a very great power. What? Is there that much power in knowledge? Yes, my son, there is no greater power than knowledge.

brh: علم نا روشنائی آن تارمئی مر مریک۔ ہمو علم نا طاقت ء ضرور حاصل کیرے۔
en: Through the light of knowledge, darkness is driven away. — I will surely gain that power of knowledge.
en_old: The light of knowledge ends darkness. I will definitely gain that power of knowledge.

brh: انت پاریس کنا مار؟ ہچ نہ بابا، ہمو چاکوم۔
en: What did you say, my son? — Nothing, baba, just... (drink) that tea.
en_old: What did you say, my son? Nothing, grandpa, I'll do that.

brh: حق اللہ حق
en: The Truth! God is the Truth!
en_old: Truth, God is truth.

brh: گلو جی میر صاحب اینو چناک اسکولے ہناسرنت جی او میر صاحب اینو اسکا دے
en: Gullu! — Yes, Mir sahib, today the children had gone to school, sir. Oh, Mir sahib, up until today...
en_old: Gulu ji, Mir sahib, the children went to school today, and Mir sahib, until today...

brh: داڑے کس ئس اسکول ہنتنے بغیر کنا اجازت آن دا چناک امر اسکول ہینانو امر اسکول ہینانو چناک ماسٹر جاگہ جاگہ ایننگے ارا ارا ٹی پاننگے کہ تینا چناک اسکول ارائی کبو اور مخلوق ہم تینا چناک اسکول ارائی کننگٹی بینے
en: No one here has ever gone to school without my permission! How have these children gone to school, how have they gone to school? — The teacher is going from place to place, telling people in every house, 'Send your children to school,' and the people too are sending their children to school.
en_old: Here no one goes to school without my permission. How did these children go to school, how did they go to school? The children, the teacher is going from place to place, house to house, telling people to send their children to school, and people are also starting to send their children to school.

brh: صاحب! حفی حفی! دا اینو اسکان ہسے ماسٹرز داڑے ہرا دے گریفتاؤ۔ خدا اینو اسکا تولو کے؟ ضرور دانا رندٹ طاقت ئس ارے کہ دا داڑے بے غم توسونے۔ باز افسوس نئے تسے۔ نی ہم کنے افسوس ئے
en: Sahib! Alas, alas! Up to now, not a single teacher has lasted two days here. God, and he's still sitting here to this day? There must surely be some power behind him, that he has stayed here without a care. It's a great pity. You too — I'm disappointed in you.
en_old: Sir! Shame, shame! Until today, the teachers who came here, I caught them. God, he's still sitting here until today? There must surely be some power behind him that he has stayed here without fear. Very sorry, you too. You too, I'm sorry.

brh: او نی ہم کنے افسوس ء ماسٹر تولوک ء خوانفنگ ء چناتے او نما ووٹ نا سم کمپک واہ یار واہ باز افسوس نا ہیت اسے میر جلال خان نا طاقت اینو داسکان دادے شانتی تننگٹی ء ہندا خاطر دا ہرا مہڑ تولوک ء
en: Oh, you too — I'm disappointed in you. The teacher sits there teaching the children and doesn't care about your vote. Wow, man, wow! It's a very regrettable thing. Mir Jalal Khan's power is what keeps him at ease to this day; that's why this fellow is still sitting there.
en_old: Oh, you too, I'm sorry. The teacher is sitting and teaching the children, and they don't care about your vote. Wow, my friend, wow, it's a very sad thing. Mir Jalal Khan's power is still giving him peace today; that's why this man is still sitting here.

brh: نوم کنا خاص انگا بندہ غاک او رے ماسٹر پدا ہم تولوک ئے میر صاحب اگے نما حکم مرے تو نن اینو دانا کل قصہ ء تمام نا نا گلو نا جذبات آن نہ عقل آن کاریم حل عقل آن
en: You are my special men, and still the teacher is sitting there! — Mir sahib, if it's your order, we'll finish off his whole story today. — No, no, Gullu, not out of emotion — handle the matter with reason, with reason.
en_old: My special men, the teacher is still sitting there. Mir Sahib, if it's your order, we'll finish his whole story today... Not with emotion, work with reason, solve it with reason.

brh: حضرت عمر رضی اللہ تعالی عنہ فرمائے کہ اسہ دے اسہ پسٹ اللہ نا نبی مسجد نبوی ٹی تولوک ئس ئے ہناٹ وٹی ئے پاریٹ ئے اللہ نا نبی حضرت عمر پارے کہ ئے پاریٹ ئے اللہ نا نبی خیر ئے او۔
en: Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said that one day, one afternoon, the Prophet of Allah was sitting in the Prophet's Mosque. I went to him and said, 'O Prophet of Allah' — Hazrat Umar said that I said, 'O Prophet of Allah, is all well?'
en_old: Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said that one day, in the afternoon, the Prophet of Allah was sitting in the Prophet's Mosque. I went and said: 'O Prophet of Allah...' Hazrat Umar said: 'I said, O Prophet of Allah, is all well?'

brh: ہنگٹس نی تکلیف ئس پارے نانا ایچو تکلیف ئس جبرائیل امین بس نی دا سے پیغام ئس سونے جبرائیل امین بس نی دا سے پیغام ئس سونے ہنتس
en: Is there some trouble for you? He said, 'No, no, there is no trouble at all: Gabriel the Trustworthy came, he brought you a message; Gabriel the Trustworthy came, he brought you a message...'
en_old: Then, when you spoke of a hardship, how great a hardship... Gabriel the Trustworthy came, he came to you with a message; Gabriel the Trustworthy came, he came to you with a message, then...

brh: پیغام ء بسنے، ئے اللہ نا نبی پیغام انت ء، اللہ نا نبی فرمائفے او عمر، جبرئیل اللہ نا پیغام ء بسنے، دا کنا محبوب پاک نا امت نا پیر انگا کہ اونا ریشٹی پیر انگا پٹ ء
en: 'A message has come.' 'O Prophet of Allah, what is the message?' The Prophet of Allah said, 'O Umar, Gabriel has come with Allah's message: this old man of the ummah of My pure Beloved, in whose beard the hair has grown old (white)...'
en_old: 'A message has come.' 'O Prophet of Allah, what is the message?' The Prophet of Allah said: 'O Umar, Gabriel has brought Allah's message: this old man of My beloved's ummah, whose beard is white...'

brh: او تینا دوئی تن برز کیک کنا رب نا مونا کنا اللہ ئے شرم بریک پیرنگا نا دعائے قبول کپو منا شرم کیت کہ پیرین وتی دستا برز کن منا آیا دعا قبول
en: '...he raises his hands before my Lord. My Allah feels ashamed not to accept the old man's prayer.' [In Balochi:] 'I feel ashamed that an old man raises his hands to me and his prayer is not accepted.'
en_old: He raises his hands before my Lord. My Allah feels ashamed not to accept the old man's prayer: 'I feel ashamed that an old man raises his hands and I do not accept his prayer.'

brh: ہمو جڑ تے خار تقریبا معنی ہفدہ پرچہ دانا جاری کرے ہفدہ او کہ بھلو اسہ تاریخ ئس اسہ انتس محفوظ ئے اگر ہمو باید ئے کہ ہمو ہفدہ انت بو
en: That ... (unclear) ... about, I mean, seventeen issues of it he published, seventeen, which is a great history, something preserved. If those are needed, those seventeen, whatever they were...
en_old: Those... he published about seventeen issues of it, seventeen. That is a great piece of history, something preserved. If those are needed, what those seventeen were...

brh: حضرت عمر پارے حضرت دا تو جوان ہوئی تسے نا امت نا پیرنگا نا دا مقام اللہ نا نبی فرمائفے او عمر دا وچہ غان او خپرا او غنگٹ دا وچہ غان اللہ ئے تو شرم بریک لیکن دا پیرنگا ئے شرم بفک
en: Hazrat Umar said, 'Hazrat, this is good indeed: the old man of your ummah has this rank.' The Prophet of Allah said, 'O Umar, from this time ... (unclear) ..., from this time Allah indeed feels ashamed, but this old man does not feel ashamed.'
en_old: Hazrat Umar said: 'Hazrat, this is a great honour for an old man of your ummah.' The Prophet of Allah said: 'O Umar, from the time that [his hair turned white]... Allah feels ashamed, but this old man does not feel ashamed.'

brh: اللہ ء تو دا پیرنگا نا پٹ آ تیان شنبہ ریک لکھنگا پیرنگا اللہ نا بغاوت ء کیک نن ہم تو ہمو زور اٹ تینا ریشہ تے مٹ کینہ
en: Allah feels ashamed before this old man's hairs, but the old man rebels against Allah. And we, too, with that same force, change our beards.
en_old: Allah feels ashamed before this old man's white hair, yet the old man rebels against Allah. And we too use that same force to change our beards.

brh: اندو پلو دا، ئے مفتی ئس نا پٹ خیال کیرے پئی دا فتوی تیننگا ٹینا ئے او نصیب ئس پا او، تیننگا پٹے و ڈکھے نا، انتئے؟
en: In the same way, look at a mufti's hair: he is giving this fatwa, and ... a fortune ..., yet he hides his own hair and ... — why?
en_old: In the same way, consider a mufti: this fatwa is for himself, and that fortune... for himself... why?

brh: ئے خنڑ کنے دا ورنائے اور اراڑ کین کہ رنگ کنے دا ترتاؤ پی رنگے کنے بلوکیاں پی رنگے کنے انچو نی نہ آنڑ مریو تے کرنٹے معلوم کہ مناظر اچ کہ کرنٹ سے
en: [Largely unintelligible:] ... see, this youth of mine, and where ... color (dye) me, ... color me ... color me, so that you would not ... it is known that ... a current ...
en_old: Look, this youth of mine and... the color... my... the color of my... how much you... you know that the scene... the current...

brh: اللہ نا نبی فرمائفے او پیرنگا نی دا ہیرا درخت ء او پیرنگا دا ہیرا درخت ء جنت اٹی ئے اللہ
en: The Prophet of Allah declared, 'O old man, you [will have] these two trees; O old man, these two trees are in Paradise, by Allah.'
en_old: The Prophet of Allah declared: O elder, this tree of yours, O elder, this tree of yours is in Paradise, by Allah.

brh: دا غنی را درخست لیونی تیبا پیرنگا زد ٹی ئے اللہ نا نبی تے فر تا پیش تپا مجید نا نبی آ پیرنگا اللہ نا نبی
en: This ... tree ... the old man is being stubborn; the Prophet of Allah ... came out ... to the Prophet; the old man, the Prophet of Allah ...
en_old: This rich man's tree... the elder... the Prophet of Allah came out... to the Prophet... the elder, the Prophet of Allah.

brh: ارشاد فرمائے کہ او پیرنگا دا ہرا درخت ئے تے جنت اٹی نی ہرا درخت ئے دیوا؟ او پیرنگا، پیرنگا بش مس مسجد نبوی آن پیش تما بش مس او سے نوجوان
en: He declared, 'O old man, this tree to him, and in Paradise I will give you two trees?' The old man, the old man stood up, came out of the Prophet's Mosque, stood up; and a youth...
en_old: He declared: O elder, which tree of yours in Paradise will you give? The elder, the elder got up, came out of the Prophet's Mosque, got up; he, a youth...

brh: اسے انصار ئس صحابہ عرض بخشوس، پارے ئے اللہ نا نبی! ئے اللہ نا نبی! دا حکم صرف پیرنگا کنے یا ننا کلا دے کنے؟ دا حکم، ہا؟ نن کنے یا۔۔۔
en: One of the Ansar, a Companion, made a request and said, 'O Prophet of Allah! O Prophet of Allah! Is this ruling only for the old man, or for all of us? This ruling, yes? For us, or...'
en_old: One of the Ansar companions made a request and said: O Prophet of Allah! O Prophet of Allah! Is this ruling only for the elder, or for all of us? This ruling, yes? For us, or...

brh: دا کلا پیرنگا کنے یا دا کلاتے کنے ئے اللہ نا نبی او حکم فرمائیں یا کلا ہم ئے پیری نا برے نا حکم یا ہر کسء ئے دو درچ گفت پائے ہر جنتا دا دو درچ کدے اللہ نا نبی ئے فرمائیں ہر کسء ئے دو درچ گفت
en: Is this all for the old man, or for all of them, O Prophet of Allah? Did you give that order [for him], or for all as well? Is it an order about old age, or, he says, does everyone get two trees — everyone in Paradise these two trees? The Prophet of Allah declared: everyone gets two trees.
en_old: Is all this for the elder, or for everyone, O Prophet of Allah? Is the ruling for him, or for everyone? Does everyone get two trees, everyone in Paradise these two trees? The Prophet of Allah declared: everyone gets two trees.

brh: سودا مسنے سودائے دے کرینے امام الانبیاء کرینے پیرنگا توئے نا سوداگریئے کتو دا نوجوان نی برو جی
en: The deal is done; the Imam of the Prophets has made the deal. The old man did not make the trade with ... ; this youth, now, comes, sir.
en_old: The deal was made, the deal was struck by the Imam of the Prophets; elder, your trade... this youth, come, sir.

brh: دوئی مرے او تہ جلد مرے او داسہ اکا نو مطلب ہمے کا گڑا ننا او ڈاکٹر صاحب ڈاکٹر صاحب دا ہمو دوران سائیں بس اچھا بابو صاحب دا مٹھل خان تو سئی داسہ اسہ ئے ہیت ئس پاو سنگتاک داسہ ڈاکٹر عبدالستار براہوئی نا پنی بار بار بنرے
en: May it be obtained, and may it be soon. Now, ... I mean, that is, so our Doctor Sahib, Doctor Sahib — during that time Sain came. OK, Babu Sahib, this is Mithal Khan, right. Now let me say one thing: friends, now you keep hearing the name of Dr. Abdul Sattar Brahui again and again.
en_old: Let it be the second, let it be quick, now... I mean, so then our doctor sahib, doctor sahib, during that time Sain came. OK, Babu sahib, this is Mithal Khan, right, now say something. Friends, now the name of Dr. Abdul Sattar Brahui keeps coming up again and again.

brh: نا ٹائم اٹ فرمائے فے کہ مسیت نا پیرنگا نا دروازہ غا مدینہ غا اللہ نا نبی ہنو مدینہ غا دے اللہ نا نبی ارشاد فرمائے فے ما بین بیتی و منبری روضۃ من ریاض الجنہ او انسان آ کنا
en: ...at that time he declared that ... at the door of the mosque, to Medina — the Prophet of Allah went to Medina — that day the Prophet of Allah declared: 'Mā bayna baytī wa minbarī rawḍatun min riyāḍ al-jannah' [Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise], and that person ... my ...
en_old: ...at that time he declared that at the elder's door of the mosque, in Medina, the Prophet of Allah went to Medina... The Prophet of Allah declared: 'Ma bayna bayti wa minbari rawdatun min riyadh al-jannah' – that person, my...

brh: روضہ اور کنا منبر نا درمیان جنت نا باغات تیان اسہ باغ اسے اللہ نا نبی ارشاد فرمائفے من زار قبری وجبت لہ شفاعتی ہرا انسان ئس کنا روضہ نا زیارت ء کرے قیامت نا دے ئے اونا
en: Between my Rawdah and my pulpit is one of the gardens of Paradise. The Prophet of Allah declared: 'Man zāra qabrī wajabat lahu shafā'atī' [Whoever visits my grave, my intercession becomes due for him]: whoever visits my Rawdah, on the Day of Judgment, his ...
en_old: Between my Rawdah and my pulpit is one of the gardens of Paradise. The Prophet of Allah declared: 'Man zara qabri wajabat lahu shafa'ati' – whoever visits my grave, on the Day of Judgment, his...

brh: محمد اوڑکن سفارش کیوا اللہ نا نبی فرمائفے او کنا اللہ حضرت ابراہیم علیہ الصلوۃ والسلام نا مکہ کن دعا کرے ئے مکہ ء امن والا کرک ئے اللہ مکہ غان بیماری تے مر کرک اینا محمد اوٹ
en: ... I, Muhammad, will intercede for him. The Prophet of Allah declared: 'O my Allah, Hazrat Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him) prayed for Mecca: "O [Allah], make Mecca a place of peace; O Allah, remove the diseases from Mecca." I am your Muhammad...'
en_old: Muhammad will intercede for him. The Prophet of Allah declared: O my Allah, Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him) prayed for Mecca, make Mecca a place of peace; O Allah, remove illnesses from Mecca; this Muhammad...

brh: ئے تینا مدینہ غان دعا کیوا او کنا اللہ مدینہ غان بیماری تے مر کرک دا نوجوان سیدھا نیمروچ نا ٹائم ئے اینا دروازہ ء ٹک
en: '...I pray for my Medina: "O my Allah, remove the diseases from Medina."' This youth went straight, at noon time, and knocked on his door.
en_old: Pray for your Medina: O my Allah, remove illnesses from Medina. This youth went straight at noon and knocked on his door.

brh: ئے فیرنگانہ فیرنگا پیش تما آ بخیری بسس ابا نا خیر نا تھی دروازہ غا ٹکی ننگا ماما بیا کرتہ واپاری کنا
en: The old man, the old man came out: 'Welcome, you have come in peace; dear, is all well?' [The youth], having knocked at the door, [said]: 'Uncle, come, do business with me.'
en_old: ...the elder came out, he came in good spirits... knocked at the door... Uncle, come, let's do business with me.

brh: ماما واپار سیکن بس نوٹ ہنت واپار، داسہ دا نوجوان پائیکو پیرنگا نی ارادے رخصت لنجا گہ اریرا بونڈرے نی ہلارنا جی اریگنے، ہمہ کیسہ
en: 'Uncle, I have come for business.' 'What business?' Now this youth says, 'Old man, your intention ...' (the rest is unclear) ... that story.
en_old: Uncle, I came for business, ... business. Now this youth says: elder, do you intend to... are you... what are you doing?

brh: دا نوجوان پارے او ماما پیرنگا مسجد قبا نا پدٹی کنا چھ سو درختو الار نا۔ سبحان اللہ۔ جنت نا، جنت نا سودا ہی اندر نا سودا ہی
en: This youth said, 'O uncle, old man, behind the Quba Mosque I have six hundred trees.' Glory be to Allah! The trade of Paradise, the trade of Paradise is such a trade.
en_old: This youth said: O uncle, behind the Quba Mosque are my six hundred trees, elder. Glory be to Allah! The trade of Paradise, the trade of Paradise is this trade...

brh: ئے ہنی دے ملاح تنخواہ ایتیرے دا ملاح زیرے مدرسہ والا اکبر نا چندہ کین، پگہ چندہ کین بسونن، پگہ مولوی صاحب پگہ نماشی بیا گڑو دے آن، تو نماشی کش دے وتار
en: ... the day you give the mullah his salary, this mullah takes it; the madrasa people come for your donation — 'Tomorrow.' 'We have come for the donation.' 'Tomorrow, Maulvi Sahib; come tomorrow evening.' Then from day [to day], so in the evening ...
en_old: ...on the day you pay the mullah his salary, this mullah... the madrasa people collect donations for Akbar; tomorrow we came to collect donations; tomorrow Maulvi sahib, tomorrow evening come... from the day, so in the evening...

brh: او ماما کنا چیسو درختو، نی دا ایرا درختے گنی تے مسجد قبا ارا قبائے، اللہ نا نبی اسلام
en: 'O uncle, my six hundred trees — you, these two trees ...' The Quba Mosque — which Quba is it? The Prophet of Allah, Islam ...
en_old: O uncle, my six hundred trees... this tree of yours... the Quba Mosque, where Quba is, the Prophet of Allah, Islam...

brh: اسلام نا اولیکو مسجد مسجد قبا ہی اللہ نا نبی مکہ غان ہجرت کرے مدینہ غا بس اف دے انداڑے مس اولیکو بنیاد تخا مسجد قبا نا اور امام الانبیاء فرمائفینے ہرا بندغ مسجد قبا ٹی ایرا
en: The first mosque of Islam is the Quba Mosque. The Prophet of Allah migrated from Mecca and came to Medina, stayed here for some days, and laid the first foundation, of the Quba Mosque. And the Imam of the Prophets has declared that whoever, in the Quba Mosque, two ...
en_old: The first mosque of Islam is the Quba Mosque. The Prophet of Allah migrated from Mecca and came to Medina, stayed here for some days, and laid the first foundation of the Quba Mosque. And the Imam of the Prophets has declared: whoever, in the Quba Mosque...

brh: ننا پوسکن آ نسل شاید اوڑا واقف مفرو، او اسہ بھلو عظیم و انسان سے، انشاءاللہ زندگی مس تو اونا انٹرو کرون، براہوئی ادب ٹی جوہر صاحب تون اوار محنت خیرخواہی کروکا بندہ ڈاکٹر عبدالستار پنی
en: Our new generation will perhaps not be acquainted with him. He was a great, great person; God willing, if there is life, we will make an introduction of him. In Brahui literature, alongside Johar Sahib, the man who worked hard and with goodwill was Dr. Abdul Sattar by name.
en_old: Our new generation may not be familiar with him. He was a great man, and God willing, if life permits, we will introduce him. He worked hard and selflessly alongside Johar Sahib in Brahui literature: Dr. Abdul Sattar.

brh: چار رکعت نفل خوانک اللہ اودے قبول شدہ عمرہ سے نا ثواب ایتک۔ دا نوجوان پارے دا نوجوان پارے برک مسجد قبا نا پدٹی کنا چھے سو دے
en: ... or four rak'ats of nafl prayer, Allah gives him the reward of an accepted Umrah. This youth said, this youth said, 'Come, behind the Quba Mosque my six hundred ...'
en_old: Whoever prays four rak'ats of nafl, Allah gives him the reward of an accepted Umrah. This young man said, this young man said, "Come, behind Masjid Quba I have six hundred..."

brh: درختو، ہندا چھے سو درخت ئے نی دیوا ایرا درخت گنیٹ۔ دا پیرنگا پارے او، نوجوان مسخرہ تو کپیس زگندو ہند۔ پارے اللہ غان پناہ خواوئی مسخرہ کپہ برا پھل پیرنگا نا دوئی برم۔
en: '... trees, these same six hundred trees I give to you, for the two trees ...' This old man said, 'O young man, you are not joking, are you?' He said, 'I seek refuge with Allah, I am not joking. Come, old man, [give] your hand.'
en_old: "The trees, these same six hundred trees, you are giving for one tree." I counted. The old man said, "Young man, aren't you joking?" He said, "I seek refuge in Allah, I am not joking. Come, old man, give me your hand."

brh: سیدھا درے تما زدے کھوبانہ پدٹی بلا باغے بلا درختے پارے ماما حساب کرک حساب کن یک دو سے چار
en: He went straight ... behind Quba there was a big garden, big trees. He said, 'Uncle, count, count: one, two, three, four.'
en_old: He went straight there, and behind it was a big garden with big trees. He said, "Uncle, count, count: one, two, three, four."

brh: دتنو، افتا دے گدریفوس۔ داسہ گڑا اما کپ، انت ست تے نی نیلے دائے تاتے، نی دن کرک کہ ہمو بلوچی گہ دوائی تے مچ ہلارتے اوفتے مچ آرام ملیک، بش مے
en: ...[with their children] they would get through their days. Now then, what can be done? What... [unclear]... You do it this way: have them take all those Balochi medicines, and they all get relief and get back on their feet.
en_old: Like this, they get through their days. Now then, don't do that. What... you leave these. You do it like this: if they take all those Balochi medicines too, they all get relief, they get up.

brh: ہنک جوان داسہ تیوی نی ہرنگ ہنا سوسئی
en: All right, good. Now, where had you gone all this while?
en_old: Go then, good. Now all of you, wherever you go...

brh: دا اورچین اٹ توار کرے کنا سوٹ بلے ڈی کس سے خناٹ جوان دیرس کے خبر دیرسس
en: The cook called out... [unclear]... yes, I saw someone there. So who was it? I don't know who it was.
en_old: He called in the orchard... my suit... I saw someone, good, after a while, after a while I found out.

brh: ئے بورچی خانہ غا خیر ایناٹ؟ دانگ اینگ گوراٹ تا؟ خبر اف ارا غا غیب مس۔ ئے نی پاریٹ کہ دا کوبین او راسے۔ جن است او لف۔ اوہو۔ داڑے جن من ارا غا مس۔ تو گڑا دیر اسے گٹ۔ ہندا تو۔
en: I went to the back of the kitchen and looked for him this way and that. I don't know where he vanished to. I told you this house is haunted (lit. 'heavy'); there are jinns... Oho! Jinns and such, here? Where did he go? So then who was it...? That's the one, then.
en_old: Did you get to the kitchen safely? Was it near here? I don't know where it vanished to. You said it was a ... There is a jinn, oh. Oh ho! Where did the jinn go from here? Then it's someone else. That's just it.

brh: اوئے تکے او دیر ئس دا شعیب ارادے؟ شعیب تو ننا رندٹ ٹرائی کریٹک۔ شعیب کنا رندٹ ٹرائی کریس انتئے ہلاستا؟ نی کیورے؟
en: Hey, look, who was that? Where is this Shoaib? Shoaib was trying [to come] after us. Shoaib, were you trying [to follow] after me? Why...? What are you doing?
en_old: Hey, look, who is that? Is this Shoaib? Shoaib was trying behind us. Shoaib was trying behind me. Why did you take it? What are you doing?

brh: ئے کسرے کنا خاطر نعرہ ہندفے ہراٹ، دا سئے نورت کہ خلوئے چونا۔
en: ...for my sake... [unclear]... Now, today... the child must be struck.
en_old: On the way he raised such a cry for my sake, with which these three... struck the child.

brh: ابا ابا چوکیدار باورچی ہراڑے کیورے
en: Father, father! Watchman, cook, where are you?
en_old: Dad, Dad, the watchman, the cook, where are they?

brh: جی صاب ہنمس۔ شعیب ارا دے؟ کنے خبر اف۔ ئے بورچی خانے ٹی کسوٹ۔ صاب کنا خیال پئے ئے گتوار بس۔ کامپورٹ دا۔
en: Yes sir, what happened? — Where is Shoaib? — I don't know. I was in the kitchen. Sir, I think he came... [to the] compound(?)...
en_old: Yes sir, it happened. Where is Shoaib? I don't know. I was in the kitchen. Sir, I think he went outside. Take it easy.

brh: دا سفت چل درویش نا قصہ ء۔ افوہ! چڑہ باٹی ننا دا قصہ ء۔ اندا قصہ بینیفٹ بینیفٹ ئے تنگ بسوٹ۔ امر کہ مرے آئی یلو دا قصہ بنے۔ اوہو! نی تو چلتن نا مش نا دیوانہ مسنس۔ آخر دیر پارینے؟
en: This is the story of the forty dervishes. — Ugh! This story of ours is always on [your] lips. I've gotten fed up telling this same story over and over. — Whatever happens, today I'll hear this story. — Oho! You've really gone crazy about Chiltan mountain. Who told you, after all?
en_old: This is the tale of the forty dervishes. Oh! ... this is our story. I came to hear this very story again and again. Whatever happens, I will hear this story. Oho! You've become crazy about the Chiltan mountain. Who told you about it, after all?

brh: چلتنا مشنا۔ ٹھیک ئے اگر نی بنفتوس، اینو غصہ ماریٹ۔ آ جوان بابا، غصہ کپہ، بنفے بنے۔
en: Of Chiltan mountain. Fine, if you don't tell it, I'll get angry today. — All right, good, dear, don't be angry. I'll tell it, listen.
en_old: Of the Chiltan mountain. Fine, if you don't tell me, I'll be angry today. All right, dear, don't be angry, tell it, I'm listening.

brh: شعیب شعیب شعیب شعیب انت مس شعیب خنت مئے
en: Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib, what happened? Shoaib, open your eyes!
en_old: Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib, Shoaib, what happened, Shoaib, look...

brh: دیر اسٹ بزوکا، زو دیر اسٹ بزو، شعیب، شعیب، مل خنتے، شعیب، خنتے مل، خنتے مل، ہن مس، شعیب، صاب دادے دشا
en: Bring some water, quick! Quick, bring some water! Shoaib, Shoaib, open your eyes! Shoaib, open your eyes, open your eyes! What happened? Shoaib! Sir, this...
en_old: Someone come, quickly, someone come! Shoaib, Shoaib, look son, Shoaib, look son, look son... it happened. Shoaib, sir, look at him.

brh: شوئے شوئے ابا ابا ہن مس ہن مس کنا مار ابا خبر اف ایڑ کسس کنا لنک بس ولئی تماشٹ دانا ویمے نہ نہ ئے تینا خناٹ دے عجب
en: Shoaib, Shoaib! Father, father! What happened, what happened, my son? — Father, I don't know... someone came up to me there, but... [unclear]... no, no, I saw it myself. Strange!
en_old: Shoaib? Father, father, it happened, it happened, my son. Father, I don't know... I was here... I watched him... no, no, I saw it myself, it's strange.

brh: او بندغس ئس ہاں جوان۔ ئے بوڑہ صاحب ریسٹ ہاؤس نا خیرن اٹ ہرفتے ہموڑے ڈکو ایتینی۔ کمبو بش مبو۔
en: It was a man. — Yes, all right. Then, sir, hide there at the back of the rest house. Come on, let's go, get up!
en_old: He was a man, yes, good. Sir, the old man at the rest house, those he left there... Let's go, get up.

brh: شاباش اوک
en: Well done, okay.
en_old: Well done.

brh: علم روشنائی بابا جی چل درویشا
en: Knowledge is light. Baba ji, the forty dervishes'...
en_old: Knowledge is light, Baba ji, the forty dervishes'...

brh: دا قصہ ء بنف، دا دیرے سورے؟ کنا مار، نی ہم چل درویش تا قصہ نا دیوانہ مسوسا؟
en: Tell this story — who were they? — My son, have you too become crazy about the story of the forty dervishes?
en_old: Tell this story, who was this? My son, have you also become crazy about the story of the forty dervishes?

brh: آخر امر کسہ دا کسہ؟ بابا جی کنا ئے ہر شام کنے دا کسہ بنفک ولے اینو تسکان پورا متنے۔ کسہ بنفو انے؟
en: After all, how does this story go? My Baba ji tells me this story every evening, but to this day it has never been finished. He tells the story, but...
en_old: So how does this story go? My Baba ji tells me this story every evening, but today it hasn't been finished yet. Will you tell the story?

brh: ولے سواری چا داندا لڑکننگٹی شولنگٹی انچا بور کتے جی او
en: But... in the middle of... [unclear]... he never finishes it like that. Yes.
en_old: But the riding... in rolling along, in... so tired, yes.

brh: باباجی، نم چاکمبو قصہ ئس بنف؟ تو بن کنا مار، دا مودی نا ہیتے
en: Baba ji, would you tell a story? — Then listen, my son: this is a tale of a time...
en_old: Baba ji, will you tell us a story? Then listen, my son, this is a matter of...

brh: کچار ما کنڈان تارماسکا چلتن نماشن خاخرس پشتمکا
en: ...when on all four sides it was dark, and from Chiltan mountain a fire was coming forth.
en_old: From the side of Kachar, darkness fell on Chiltan; in the evening, something... behind.

brh: بلا قضا تہ سورے اور چلتن نا مشہ تینا قبضہ ئے کرے سورے کنا وارثی وختس چل درویش سفر آ پیش تمار سفر کرے سا کرے سا کرے سا
en: Demons had brought calamity and had taken Chiltan mountain into their possession. Once upon a time, the forty dervishes set out on a journey; they travelled and travelled and travelled.
en_old: Calamity and misfortune had struck, and they had taken over the Chiltan mountain... Once upon a time, the forty dervishes set out on a journey; they travelled and travelled and travelled.

brh: اندا چلتن نا مش آ گدرینگیسا، اندا چلتن نا خورکا بسٹ، دا درویشاک پیوننگا
en: Passing by this very Chiltan mountain, they came near this very Chiltan; these dervishes [were] in white...
en_old: They were passing by this very Chiltan mountain, they came to this very Chiltan..., these dervishes were...

brh: ئے بے عزتی کاٹم آن ہلیس نت اسکان ہسوارے پر نور انگا چہرہ اوفتہ چہرہ غاک نورم بار ہسوارے ہرا وخت کہ او
en: ...[garments] from head to foot, with radiant faces; their faces were like light. When they...
en_old: ...dishonor, from head to toe... a radiant face; their faces were... when they...

brh: چلتن نا مش آ سرمسور تو اوفتہ دا فیصلہ مس کہ نن دا ننے ہندا مش نا نیام اٹ کدرے فین
en: ...reached Chiltan mountain, they decided: 'We will spend our days right here, in the middle of this very mountain.'
en_old: When they reached the Chiltan mountain, they decided that we will... in the middle of this very mountain.

brh: او مبلاتی دا ایت اسل خوش بتو، اوف دایتے برداشت کتو، مچ نن اوفتا نیامٹی مقابلہ مس، اسے کنڈان تارماس
en: And the demons were not at all happy with this matter; they could not bear it. All night long a contest went on between them: on one side was darkness,
en_old: And they were not at all happy with this; they could not tolerate it. Then a contest took place between them, and from one side darkness...

brh: ایلو کنڈا روشنائی۔ وار کے ہمو نن چلتن نا مش آن اسے ہندن و خاخر ئس پیش تما کہ ہڑ کنا ڈغار و شنگار سیاہ جوڑ مسر۔ مون نا سنگار۔
en: on the other side light. Then that night such a fire came out of Chiltan mountain that all the land and its beauty turned black — the beauty of its face.
en_old: Light on the other side. Then such a fire came out of the Chiltan mountain that my land and its beauty all turned black. The beauty ahead.

brh: مچ آ نن دا ڈغار جولان کننگے گڈ گڈ تسکے سوبت کے مخلوق بش مس خنات کے
en: All night long this land kept shaking, rumbling 'gad gad'. In the morning, when the people got up, they saw that...
en_old: In the evening we were wandering this land, little by little, because of that the people became happy, I saw.

brh: چلتن نا مش نا خاخر ختم مسنے۔ او چلتن نا مش پیون پیون برف ئے ولے دا چل درویش آ تا؟
en: ...the fire of Chiltan mountain had ended, and Chiltan mountain was white, white with snow. But these forty dervishes — what of them?
en_old: The fire of Chiltan mountain has ended. That Chiltan mountain is white, white with snow, but these forty dervishes, who are they?

brh: ہنمس کنا مار خلق والا کو دا کماشاک پار کے ہمو دے آن اینو اسکان ولدا دا چل درویشی کس خنتو بابا جی
en: ...what happened [to them]? — My son, the village folk and these elders say that from that day until today no one has seen these forty dervishes again. — Baba ji...
en_old: Then, my son, the people, these elders say that from that day until today no one has seen these forty dervishes again, father.

brh: چار پنچ شش ہفت شش ہشت درخت نا حساب کٹ چھ سو درخت حساب کرین ماما نین ویشت مسخرت نہ کننگائے
en: Four, five, six, seven, six, eight — counting the trees one by one, he counted six hundred trees. "Uncle, I am not joking with you."
en_old: Four, five, six, seven, six, eight. Counting the trees, they counted six hundred trees. "Uncle, you aren't joking with me, are you?"

brh: پیرنگا پائے کہ او نوجوان مسخرہ تو کپے سے پارے ماما مسخرہ کپارے بس بدلی مس
en: The old man says, "O young man, are you not joking?" He said, "Uncle, I am not joking." So the exchange was made.
en_old: The old man says, "Young man, aren't you joking?" He said, "Uncle, I am not joking." And so the exchange was made.

brh: پارے مس ما مفیرنگا خوش مس چھے سو درخت ملانے دا نوجوان پیشی مان زرس مستی دوڑ کرے سا اینا وراغا تینا وضو کین کہ کاو امام الانبیاء نا رندا نماز خوانو
en: He said... the old man was happy, because he had received six hundred trees. The young man came out and ran on a little way ahead, to go to his house, do his ablution, and then go and pray behind the Imam of the Prophets.
en_old: He said... the old man was happy because he had gotten six hundred trees. The young man came out and ran a bit fast, saying, "I'll go home and do my ablution so that I can pray behind the Imam of the Prophets."

brh: بس ورا غاب علی نا نیاما سنوکے بے بے کمر نا تیتھٹی ئے بے بے کمر نا تیتھٹی ئے توار کرے او فلانی
en: Then he came to the house... [unclear words]... his wife was inside the room, his wife was inside the room. He called out, "O so-and-so."
en_old: Then at home... his wife was inside the room, his wife was inside the room. He called out, "O so-and-so."

brh: ئے فون او پارے کمرہ نا تیٹی ئس پارے جی، ہاں اللہ کے ننا بے بے کے جی کیرے، ہاں ننا بے بے تو دا حالت ئے اج مولوی صاحب ئس پیت کرئے کہ، بکسو بنا بوس
en: ...and from inside the room she said, "Yes (ji)." Yes, by God — do our wives say "ji"? Yes, as for our wives, this is their state... today a maulvi sahib asked whether... [rest unclear]
en_old: ...he called, and from inside the room she said, "Yes." Yes, Allah... our wife said yes. Our wife was in this state; today a maulvi sahib had asked whether..., begin...

brh: ارے اونا کاہ کاریم کن کے کے کے دیغر نا ٹیما گڑا سگر کمائفک دیغر نا ٹیما کے کمائفک گڑا چہ پلاسٹی کا سے آ زرس زیتون نا او زرس مالٹا نا او دا گنڈیری ہلی بریک دا دندانی او دا نی اورا کے ٹی ایم دو نو ری
en: Yes, his work... at the time of the afternoon prayer he then earns a little — at afternoon-prayer time he earns — then in a plastic bag a few olives and a few oranges, and he buys this sugarcane and brings it... [rest unclear: 'these teeth...']
en_old: Hey, for his fodder work... in the afternoon he earns something... in the afternoon he earns, then from a plastic one a little olive and a little malta, and he brings this sugarcane... (partly unintelligible)

brh: ارے او ڈیڈی دا دن کے خنک تا ارے بس گڑا چنا تے بش مرے ایک خٹ برے چنا تے بمبر کبو باونما بندنگٹے بش مرے گڑا سڑو کوریلی استالان کے
en: Yes, and when they see Daddy this day... yes, then the children get up, come over to the bed... "Children, get up, your father is coming!" They get up, then... [rest unclear]
en_old: Hey, daddy, he sees this day... then the children get up... wake the children... get up, then... (partly unintelligible)

brh: براہوئی او ڈاکٹر عبدالستار براہوئی نا پین اسہ بھلو خصوصیت ئس او ہزار آ نوجوان آتیٹی جذبہ ئس تیار کرے اینو ہم اسہ قصہ ئس بنفیو ئے ہنا کبو سید خان اسکول اٹی خواناٹا اوڑے ہنا خبر تما کہ یار دا مار ئس ارے مچٹ دا ڈیگڈاس تو کنا
en: ...Brahui. And another great quality of Dr. Abdul Sattar Brahui is that he created a passion in thousands of young people. Today too I will tell you a story: I was studying at the Syed Khan school, and news came there that, "Man, there is this boy, a bit..." [rest unclear]
en_old: Another great quality of Dr. Abdul Sattar Brahui is that he inspired passion in thousands of young people. Today we will also hear a story. Go on, Syed Khan... I was studying at school, and news came that there's a snake, and all of this... of mine... (partly unintelligible)

brh: بارش نا پدا تتخی تتیلفت تے پلاسٹک نا ڈول جوڑ کننگ اٹی ئس، ارا دے دا بیوس نا دیہاڑی کے لگے بک، دیغر نا ٹیم ئے دو خالی ونی ہٹے، ارودس دن کے اورے کینو خودا
en: After the rain [unclear words], he was busy making plastic [buckets]. On the day this helpless man gets no daily-wage work, at the time of the afternoon prayer he [comes home] empty-handed... [rest unclear]
en_old: After the rain, ...making it like plastic. On the day this helpless person's daily wage..., in the afternoon two empty... (partly unintelligible)

brh: خالی بننگٹی ارا وت بس کمرہ نا خوڑکا نانو رلی نا بالشت ئس اسگڑا وقت ئے کہ کمرہ نا تیا پیا مونا تو بش مفک کوپیاستے نا کسرٹ ایننگٹی
en: When he comes back empty-handed, he just [lies] in a corner of the room with a pillow made of a quilt, and at that time, when he is in front of the room, nobody gets up [to greet him] as he comes in... [rest unclear]
en_old: ...while coming empty... just a pillow near the room... at the time when in front of the room... does not get up... on the way... (partly unintelligible)

brh: دا او بے بے اللہ تعالی نا تحفہ نا بے بے ئے توار کرے تینے اونا حال کو او فلانی
en: This — O [friends], a wife is a gift from Allah the Exalted. He called out to his wife [to tell her] his news: "O so-and-so."
en_old: "This, O wife, is a gift from Allah." He called his wife and told her what had happened: "O so-and-so."

brh: ئے بے بے پاک جی خیرے پارے برک سوداگری اسل گھنوٹ آن سوداگری خلگنس سوداگری دا خلگنوٹ چھے سو درختس ورا نی معلومے بے بے پارے
en: ...the wife said, "Yes? Is everything all right?" He said, "Look, I have struck a real deal — I have made this deal: six hundred trees... Do you know [about it]?" The wife said,
en_old: ...the wife says, "Yes, is everything alright?" He said, "Come, I've made a trade, a real trade. I made this trade: six hundred trees. Do you know about the garden?" The wife said,

brh: ئے ہمت و محنت کرینوٹ کنے معلوم ئے مسجد قباء نا پدٹی ننا باغ ئے دہ سال نا درخت و جوان مسنو داسہ پچکن الارتن لنگا برمتن لنگا تیارو پارہ برک سوداگری خلکنٹ ہم سوداگری
en: "I have put in effort and hard work [on it]; I know — behind Masjid Quba is our garden, ten years of trees that have grown well, and now they are laden with fruit and ready." He says, "Look, I have struck a deal, and what a deal."
en_old: "...I put in courage and hard work. I know that behind Masjid Quba our garden has trees that have grown well for ten years, and now they are ripe and ready... Come, I've made a trade, a real trade."

brh: نی پارے ایرات درخت الکنوٹ دسے سد درخت دسے الکنوٹ پارے نما مغز خراب ئے دہ سال ئے اونی خوار نی ایرات درخت کن پارے بر سد
en: He said, "I have bought two trees — for six hundred trees I have bought two." She said, "Have you lost your mind? For ten years I toiled over it, and you [traded it] for two trees?" He said, "Look..."
en_old: "You said you've given them for one tree? Six hundred trees for one tree?" She said, "Have you lost your mind? For ten years you labored, and for one tree..." He said, "Come..."

brh: او دا پین گڑاسینا پارے ہم پارے اللہ نا نبی فرمائفینے ارا بندہ دا ایرا درختے الیک ارا بندہ دا ایرا درختے الیک جنت اٹی اودے ایرا درخت ایتیوہ دا درختات نا نام ہرے کنا نام
en: And he said this other thing too: "The Prophet of Allah has declared: whoever takes these two trees — whoever takes these two trees — I will give him two trees in Paradise. And the name on those trees is now my name."
en_old: And he said something else too: "The Prophet of Allah has said that whoever gives these trees for one tree, whoever gives these trees for one tree, will be given one tree in paradise. The name of this tree is... my name..."

brh: ارے، نی ہم محنت کرینوس، ئے ہم محنت کرینوٹ، داسہ ئے جنت اٹی ناٹ، نی ہم تو کنا بے بے اوس، ایمان والا اوس، ئے نی ہم جنت آ داخل مریسہ، داسہ پا، داسہ بے بے شیر زالنگان پائے، او کنا ارے باز سستا او سودا کرینوس
en: "Look, you worked hard too, and I worked hard too. Now I am [bound] for Paradise; and you are my wife, you are a believer, so you too will enter Paradise. Now tell me." Then the wife, a lion-hearted woman, says, "Oh my dear, you have made a very cheap bargain!"
en_old: "Hey, you worked hard too, and I worked hard too. Now I'm in paradise. You are my wife too, and a believer, so you will enter paradise too. Now tell me." Now the wife says like a lioness, "You have made a very cheap bargain."

brh: دا خلق کہ ارے باز داکا مڑ بلوچستان نا سرحد آ او بالکل ہمیرے ہچو نہ سواری ئس نہ انتس ہمیرے تینا موٹرسائیکلا سستہ ہمے موٹرسائیکلا ہمے دورٹی ہمیرے بس سربس صرف ئنا خاطرا
en: This village, which is very far from here, on the border of Balochistan — and absolutely, right there, there was no transport, nothing at all — he came there on his own motorcycle; on that same motorcycle, in that era, he would come right there, he would arrive, only for my sake,
en_old: These people who are here, so many from this land on the Balochistan border, and absolutely, there was no transport, nothing at all; they came on their motorcycles, on those motorcycles, in that era, they just came, solely for the sake of this.

brh: کہ کنے انکریج کے بس کنا چنکو خلکس غریبی ہالٹ ہمیرے توس کنتو کچاری کرے کنکن کتاب ہیس او اوڑان پد ہنو کنتو دوستی ئس محبت ئس جاری تخا ہزا ہزا کتابا کنے دیس کنے
en: so that he could encourage me. Just my small village, in a state of poverty — right there he sat and held sessions with me, brought books for me, and after that he kept up a friendship and love with me; he gave me thousands and thousands of books.
en_old: that he encouraged me. I had just a small, poor background, and he worked hard with me, he took me books, and after that he kept up his friendship and love with me; he gave me thousands and thousands of books.

brh: ئے شعور تے اسکان پانہ فے اوڑا پد وقت ئس ہنو بس کہ ہرا وقت آ کنا ہمے کا خلق آ بننگ ایننگ داڑے ہائی سکول آ مشکل ئس تو ڈاکٹر صاحب کرے آفر کرے ئے ہنا ڈاکٹر صاحب استا وتا خٹی تکر
en: ...[he raised] my awareness up to [that level]. After that a time came when coming and going from that village of mine to the high school here was difficult, so Doctor Sahib made an offer; I went, and Doctor Sahib kept me in his own home.
en_old: ...he brought awareness to me. Then after that a time came when it was difficult for me to come from that area of mine to the high school here, so Doctor Sahib offered, he said, come stay at my own house.

brh: تقریبا شش تو اسکا ئے داڑے رہاٹ اور کنے دا تینا اولاد آ پالار کنے خوانفیر کنے کتاب تسور کنے ایرغ تسور ہنو سمجھ کہ کنا اگر مچٹ او دا سماج اٹ ایڑا کنٹریبیوشن ارے تو اونا بن
en: I stayed here for about six [years], and they raised me as their own child, educated me, gave me books, gave me food. So understand that if I have even a little contribution in this society, its root is him.
en_old: For about six years I stayed here, and he raised me like his own child; he educated me, gave me books, gave me food. So understand that if I have any contribution at all in this society, its root is him.

brh: بنیادی سبباک ہمے بندغاکو ہرافتے اسٹ ڈاکٹر صاحب ہم ارے ایلو بازاک اریرو ایلوفتا بھی ذکرے کرو تو اینو کن ہمو خاطران خوشی ئے کہ ڈاکٹر صاحب تو موجود اف لیکن ڈاکٹر صاحب نا ایلم کہ ارے عبدالحق مجروح صاحب موجود ئے ادانگا میر محمد سائیں موجود ئے تو بازی خوش
en: The basic reasons are those very people, one of whom is Doctor Sahib; there are many others too, and I will mention the others as well. So today I am happy for this reason: although Doctor Sahib is not present, Doctor Sahib's brother, Abdul Haq Majrooh Sahib, is present, and Mir Muhammad Sain is present here too, so I am very happy.
en_old: The main reasons are those people, one of whom is Doctor Sahib, and there are many others; I'd mention the others too.
