And in saag you don't add spices; spices spoil the saag and make it bitter. So how do they make the saag? I'll show you how the saag is done. You add the onions and good ghee; you've added four ladle-spoons, or if it's a big [pot of] saag, then ghee...
en_old: ...it's green and saltless, the ghee makes it tasty. Then in saag, don't add a lot of chilli either — add less to this one, add lots of chilli to that one. Then don't add spices to saag; spices spoil the saag, make it bitter. Then they do the saag like that. I'll tell you about the saag: you add onions, good ghee, you've added four spoons of the big one, or if it's a big amount of saag...

brh: ارے تو نے بھاز ہی سی ئناشش چمچہ کہ شاغاس تہ گڑا امہ کریس سی کہ لہر کریرگڑا تھوم بھی شاغ ٹی تہ کٹے
en: ...if you have a lot, add six spoons of ghee. Then, once you've done that and they've simmered in the ghee, add garlic too, crushed.
en_old: ...then you have a lot, add six spoons of ghee, then once you've done that, they fry it in the ghee, then add garlic too, crushed.

brh: تھوم شاغاس ولداہندن سو ئے شاغ تہ مچہ ہڑسے تہ سو ئنا تہ ہندن دیک خشک مریر تاکہ تھومہ ئے انت ککڑ نا گند کائہہ دیرک تہ خشک مسر ساگ ئنا گڑا اوکا پد ئے انت کر تہ انت پارہ تہ پین بھی ہموڑے بٹیس تہ کہ سوتہ بے ئکہ پدا ارفپک گڑا ولدا امہ کریس اوکا پد ٹماٹہ ئے انت شاغ تہ پلپل خیسنو جوان انگا زیباانگا
en: Once you've added the garlic, add the meat the same way and stir-fry it a little, so the meat's water dries off and the garlic's... the chicken smell goes away; its water has dried. For the saag, after that, do the, what's it called, put the rest in right there too, because the meat won't take up the salt later. Once you've done that, add the tomato, er, red chili, good nice ones...
en_old: You've added the garlic, then add the meat like that and fry it a bit, so that the meat's water dries off, so that the garlic... the chicken smell comes out. The water of the saag dries off. Then after that you do the, as they say, otherwise it sticks there, so that the meat... then it won't lift up. Then once you've done that, after that add the tomato, red chillies, the nice good ones...

brh: لاہوریئادا پلپلاک اریرہمو جوان زیبا کٹے کٹےجوغن اٹ پیالہ سے نا خاسے اٹ چمچہ ئس پر کہ شاغ تہ گڑاولدا مچہ ہڑسے تہ ہڑساس ہڑساس تہ ولدا مچہ دیر شاغ تہ چڑچڑارہ کے گند پلپلات آ کائک پلپلاک جوان صحیح بسر داسا چائسس پلپلاک فل جوان گچین بسیر گڑا داسا ٹماٹرات ئے شاغ تہ ٹماٹراتے شاغاس تہ گڑا ہڑسے تہ
en: ...these Lahori chillies, the good ones, ground and pounded in the mortar. Fill a spoon, the kind used for a teacup, and add it. Then stir it a little; once you've stirred and stirred, add a little water so it sizzles and the raw smell of the chillies goes off and the chillies cook properly. Now, you see, the chillies are fully and nicely cooked; so now add the tomatoes, and once you've added the tomatoes, stir them.
en_old: ...these Lahori chillies, the good ones, ground, ground. Fill a spoon up to about a cup's... and add it, then fry it a bit, keep frying and frying, then add a little water so it sizzles and the chilli smell comes out. The chillies cook properly. Now you see the chillies are cooked really well, then now add the tomatoes; once you've added the tomatoes, fry them.

brh: ولدا اشکن خرنو پلپل کتر کہ شاغ تہ راست اوڑے بھی مزہی مریک یا رست بڑیس ٹی تہ نا مرضی کتر کریس تا نا مرضی اوڑے شاغاس تا گڑا جوان صحیح سوئے نا زیا ڈھکن ئے تخسہ ہندن لہر کے سو تہ کڑھے خوڑت مرے صفا دہن بر بر مرے بسٹ مف ولدا مچہ جوان زیبا خوڑت مرے گڑا اوکا پد ڈھکہ ولدا داسا چائسس کہ سو تہ
en: Then chop some thin green chilies and add them; honestly, that makes it tasty there too. Or put them in whole, as you like: chop them as you like and add them there as you like. Then put the lid properly over the meat, and let the meat simmer like that and boil down so it becomes tender, completely and evenly done; then let it get a bit more nice and tender. After that cover it again. Now you see that the meat...
en_old: Then chop a little green chili and add it; that really makes it tasty too. Or chop it however you like and add as much as you want. Then put the lid on the meat properly and let it steam like that so the meat cooks soft, evenly done and not undercooked. Once it's all nice and soft, then cover it again. Now you see the meat...

brh: داسا جوان کرینے مسنے گڑا ساگات ئے داسا شاغ ٹی تہ داسا ساگ اگہ بہ راست بھازاک ہندن کیرہ ساگ ئے لہر تیرہ خوڑت کیرہ گڑا پدا ہنداڑے سو ئٹی شاغرہ تہ گڑا بائے تہ بند کیرہ جٹس جوان مچٹ لہر خلیک گڑا اوڑے زو زو تیار مریک بھازاک ہندن کیرہ ساگ ئے مہالو لہر تفسہ وری ہنداڑے شاغرہ تہ اوڑے ہراٹیم آ ساگ ئے لہر تسس شاغاس
en: ...is now nicely done, so add the saag now. Honestly, many people do it this way: they steam the saag and soften it first, then add it right here into the meat and close the lid; it simmers nicely for a short while, and then it's ready very quickly. Many people also do it this way: you don't steam the saag first, they put it straight in here. Now, when you've steamed the saag and added it,
en_old: Now it's done nicely, so add the greens now. A lot of people actually do it this way: they steam the greens first, soften them, and then add them right here to the meat. Then they close the lid and it steams nicely for a short while, so it's ready quickly. A lot of people steam the greens separately first and then add them here, once they've steamed them.

brh: تہ ہندا سوئے تہ اوڑے کاڑھسہ گڑا ساگ ئے شاغسہ تہ گڑا اوڑے بائے تہ بند کیسہ گڑا جوانو جٹس جوانو مس مس لہر کرے وری بس اسٹ ایلو ٹی رس تا اسٹ ایلو ٹی اوار مس
en: ...you boil down that same meat there, then add the saag, close the lid there, and let it simmer nicely for a good while. Then it's cooked: they've got into each other and blended together.
en_old: So while the meat is cooking in it, add the greens, close the lid, and it steams nice and well for a good while, and then they come together and mix into each other.

brh: توگڑا پائہہ دا گھنٹہ کنے خوانف پائہہ دا پارے پائہہ ای دچہ اٹ کلو میٹربریوہ اوخہ کلو میٹر گڑا نت آ پاسہ خوانفوٹ نے تولنگ خوانفوکو کن تو ٹیم اف ہننگ ہننگ ئٹی دا چنا ئے ہنداخہ خواننگ نا شوق اس پائہہ او نی خرہ خہ غائے انت کرک ہلی آ نے ہنسٹ کر ای نے تو ہندن برسٹ کیوہ نی ہنسٹ کر ای برسٹ کیوہ صرف ہموڑے کنے ہنداخہ خوانف ای سہ
en: So then he says, 'Teach me for this one hour.' The other one says, 'I come so many kilometres, that many kilometres; so you want me to teach you on foot? There's no time to sit and teach you.' Along the way (this child had such a passion for learning) he says, 'You, on a donkey or whatever, on a horse: you keep riding, and I'll keep coming along with you like this. You keep going and I'll keep coming; just teach me that much there.'
en_old: Then he said, 'Teach me for this one hour.' He said, 'I come from so many kilometres away.' 'How will I teach you on foot? There's no time to sit and teach you.' On the way, this child had such a passion for learning. He said, 'What does it matter if you're on a donkey or a horse? You ride, and I'll keep walking alongside you like this. You ride and I'll keep walking, just teach me that much along the way.'

brh: سوال ہرفسٹ کروٹ ای آن نے نی کنے صرف جواب ترسٹ کر بس سوال کروٹ جواب ایت پین آہہ تعلیم ہناد اے ظاہر اے ہلی آ خرنگنگ آخرنگوکا خواننگ تو ہندن مرو پین تومروف داسادوٹی پین ئس تختیس پینسل ئس ربڑئس تو ہرفوف ہننگ ہننگ ئٹی تو دا چنا نا ہر نی شوق اے پائہہ ای نے آن سوال کروٹ است آن نی کنے جواب
en: 'I'll keep asking you questions and you just keep giving me answers. That's it: I ask a question, you give the answer.' What other kind of education would it be? Obviously studying while riding on a horse would be like that. It wouldn't be like now, carrying a pen, a slate, a pencil and an eraser in hand. So on the way this child, with all his passion, says, 'I'll ask you questions, and you [answer] me from memory.'
en_old: 'I'll keep asking you questions and you just keep giving me answers. I'll ask a question, you give the answer.' What other kind of education would it be? Obviously, studying on a donkey, studying while riding, would be like that. It wouldn't be like now, with a slate, a pencil and an eraser to carry along. So on the way this child, with his passion, said, 'I'll ask you questions and you give me the answers.'

brh: ترسٹ کیس پائہہ گڑا دا ڈیلی استاد پچیس کلو میٹر بسکہ دا چنا ہلمہ ہلمہ سیٹ بسکہ اوڑتو اوار ایندے بادشاہ نا ارا اسکا کسری ہرفسٹ کریکہ تو ای آن تہ وری ہناکہ وری ہمیڑسکا چنا ہلمہ ہلمہ سے اٹ بے خو ڈیلی بس چنا نا ہندا روٹین اس ڈیلی ڈیلی ہندن بس کریکہ ہندا اے انت تہ اسکہ گڑا ہندن کرے کرے
en: '...keep giving [answers],' he says. So every day this teacher would come twenty-five kilometres, and this child would come running and running with him, up to where the king's house was; he would keep to the road. Then from there he would go back again, and come back again, the child running and running. Every day, that was the child's routine; every single day he kept doing it like that. That's how it was, and he kept on doing it like that.
en_old: He would keep giving him answers. So every day the teacher came twenty-five kilometres, and this child would come running alongside him on foot. He would come with him to the king's house, where he went to teach. Then he'd go back again and the child would come running alongside him again on foot. Every day the child had this same routine; every single day he came like that. That's how it was, and he kept doing it like that.

brh: پائہہ ہمو چنا پدائے خوانا بھلوس مس امام غزالی جوڑ مسک ہاں او اسرہ بندغاک او خوانوکا بندغاک تعلیم یافتہ بندغاک خواننگ نا شوق کہ ہر کس ئے مرے ی پائہہ اسہ وارس ئس اس اے دیر پارے اے انت پارہ تہ ارسطو پارے پائہہ ای انت کریٹ تعلیم تسٹہ بھلا بھلا بندغات ئے پیشن نا پیشن نا
en: They say that child later studied and became a great man: he became Imam Ghazali. Yes, they were such people, studious people, educated people, with the passion for learning that everyone should have. They say once there was a... who said it, what do they call him... Aristotle said, 'What did I do? I gave education to great, great people from abroad, from abroad...'
en_old: That child later studied and became a great man: he became Imam Ghazali. Yes, there were such people, people who studied, educated people, with a passion for learning that everyone should have. Once there was... what was it... Aristotle said, 'What did I do? I educated great men from all over.'

brh: بندغاک بسر گڑا پائہہ داسا دا شاگردات ئے تینا بش کہ سلیف ہرن تا کہ نا دا شاگردات ئے ٹی اخہ خوانوکو بندغ ارے
en: The people came, and then he says, 'Now stand these students of yours up, line them up, so we can see how many educated people there are among these students of yours.'
en_old: The people came, and then he said, 'Now line up these students of yours so we can see how many educated people there are among your students.'

brh: گڑا بارفس ہراٹیم اے انتات ئے انت پارہ تہ آبوسات ئے نہ دافتے بسیس تا ولدا ٹپیسہ تا بوچات ئے تا کشسہ اس کیسہ تا چکیسہ تا کل ئے تا خا خرابنگا خرابنگا گڑات ئےتا ٹونڈات ئے تااوفت ئے تا کل یے یکہ کیسہ گڑا اے انتات ئے غلہ غات ئے تا یکہ کیسہ گڑا غلہ غات ئے تخسہ السہ تا باررہ باررہ ڈڈ مریرہ پالن
en: Then you dry them. When those, what are they called, the half-cooked grains, right: once you've cooked these, you beat them, remove their stalks, pick them over, and separate out all the bad stuff, the bits and stubs, all of it. Then you separate out the, well, the grains; then you put the grains down and leave them, and they dry and dry until they're hard, and so on.
en_old: Then you dry them. When... what's it called... the rain, no, you bring them, then you thresh them, pull off their husks, sift them, clean out all the dirt, the bad stuff, the stalks, and gather them all together. Then you gather the... the grain, put the grain aside and leave it to dry. They dry until they become hard, and so on.

brh: پالن کنگس تا توہموڑے گڑا کنیسہ تا بس اگہ خرن کریس تا گڑا بارفسہ تا بارسر داسا چٹار نہ گڑا اگہ ارا ٹی سہ مشین اگہ مشین نا سہولت ارے نے بازارت ئے ٹی ایت نسف تا اگہ اف نے سہولت گڑا ارات ئے ٹی بندغاک تینات ئے تینٹ کٹیرہ نسخل مست ئنا اسکہ بھلو ارا خل اسرہ تین پتین زی پہ زیا تخرہ تا گرا دانا
en: You do this and that to them, then you deal with them there. That's it: once you've made them into green [grain], you dry them, and once they're dry, now comes the grinding. If there's a machine, if you have access to a machine, take them to the market and have them ground. If you don't have that facility, then at home people grind them themselves: there used to be a hand mill, two big stones; they would put them one on top of the other, and then this...
en_old: ...and so on. Then you take them there, and when you've finished, you dry them, and once they're dry, now the grinding. If there's a machine in the house, if you have that facility, you take them to the market. If you don't have the facility, people at home grind them themselves with a hand mill; there used to be a big stone in the house, they'd put one stone on top of the other, and then this...

brh: چھنکو لٹ ئس مریک ای ٹی تہ گڑا مچٹ مچٹ آ غلہ شاغسٹ ہڑسسٹ کیسہ ولدا شاغسٹ ہڑسسٹ کیسہ بھاز غلہ شا غپسہ اوڑے ڈلک تا ہندن خراب خراب کہ کشک تا اے انت ڈارو کیک تا مچہ غلہ شاغ ایلو سلو سلو ہڑسہ تا گڑا جوان زیبا زیبا خل ئٹی دہن برسٹ کیرہ خوڑت مرسٹ کیرہ گڑا خرمینت ئے تا کشہ خرمینت ئے کشاس گڑا خرن خیت ہندن جوان زیبا صاف
en: There's a small stick [for a handle]; put it in, then keep pouring in a little grain at a time and keep turning, again pour and keep turning. Don't pour in a lot of grain, or it just gets cut up there and comes out bad like that; it, well, only cracks it. Pour in a little grain and turn it slowly, slowly; then it comes through the stones nicely like that and keeps getting fine. Then take out the khurmin; once you've taken out the khurmin, the green [grain] comes out nice and clean like that.
en_old: There's a small stick. Put it in, then add the grain a little at a time and keep roasting it, then add more and keep roasting. Don't add a lot of grain at once, or it'll go lumpy and turn out bad, it gets... what's it called... burnt. Add a little grain, and roast it slowly, slowly, so it's nicely evenly done in the pan and turns soft. Then take out the khurmin. Once you've taken out the khurmin, the finished khurmin comes out nice and clean like that.

brh: مریرہ گڑا کشاس تا گڑا شاغ تا تھال ئسے ٹی مچہ چکے تا دا ئے سا مچٹ ہو سکتا ہے گڑامڑا مس تا گڑا اوفت ئے گڑا تخ گڑا اودے بھی خرمین ئٹی کیرہ گڑا او خرمین ہندن مزہی مریک گڑا خرمین ئے خنسہ اودے جھکہ ٹی گلو کر چنا ت ئے تینا ہیت چناک نا گلو کیر سینہ ئے گور ئے اڈا فل چٹ چٹا دوائی نا بھی ضرورت اف اوڑکہ
en: ...they become [fine]. Once you've taken them out, pour them into a tray and sift them a little; this may be a bit... it may have got mixed up, so set those aside. They put that into the khurmin as well, and that makes the khurmin tasty. And khurmin, you see, for a cough, for the throat: for children, I'd say it [helps] children's throats and settles the chest, completely; there's no need even for medicine for them.
en_old: Then take them out, put them in a tray and sift them a little. It might be a bit mixed, so put them aside and they also add it to the khurmin, and that makes the khurmin really tasty. When you see the khurmin, pound it in the mortar. The children... it's good for children, for the chest; it soothes it, there's no need for medicine at all.

brh: گڑا خرمین ئے امہ جوڑ کیرہ خرمین نا طریقہ ئے پاوہ نمے داسا نتات ئے تا جوڑاس ہندن نا گڑا اوٹی بھی اونا اودےگڑا نن امہ کینہ اونا سوت ئے تینالہر
en: So how do they make the khurmin? I'll tell you the method of khurmin. Now, you've made the flour like this, and then in it too, its... then what we do is, its meat, we steam it ourselves...
en_old: Then how do they make the khurmin? I'll tell you the method for the khurmin. Now, you make its ingredients like this, and in it too... then what we do is, its meat, you steam it...

brh: دیر شاغنہ پلپل شائہ دیر شاغنہ بے شا بے ئے ککڑا بے شاغنہ دیر شاغنہ بھلو پوٹا شاغنہ ککڑئے کینہ بند گڑا او لہر کیک کیک بیست منٹ مرے تہ یا تیس منٹ مرے تہ ککر جوان صحیح پریشر تہ چرینگا تو گڑا ککڑ صفا خوڑت مریک گڑا اگہ کینہ متوس تا تو ایہن انگا
en: We add water, add chili, add water, add salt (we salt the chicken), add water, add a big cardamom, put the chicken in and close it. Then it steams and steams for twenty or thirty minutes; once the cooker has properly built up pressure, the chicken becomes completely tender. And if we didn't have one, then this way...
en_old: We add water, add chili, add water, add salt, add salt for the chicken, add water, add a big onion, put the chicken in and close it. Then it steams for twenty or thirty minutes; once the cooker builds up proper pressure, the chicken gets nice and tender. And if we didn't have one, then like this...

brh: دیگ ئٹی گڑا مچہ زیادہ ارے کیک ککرئٹی مچہ ہمو بیست تیس منٹ ئٹی بریک پڑک گڑا ککڑا ئے تہ ملسہ ہرسہ کڑھا اگہ دیک تہ خشک اوتوجوان او خشک افس گڑا مچہ کہ تا جوان اےگند کائہہ ککڑ ناہنداڑئے پدا خرمین ئٹی وری گند تا بریک گڑا لہر کرے نا گڑا اوکا پد ککڑ ئے مچہ مچہ ریشہ ریشہ کرک اوکا کشے تہ اوکا پد پیٹ ئسے جوانو صحیئوبھلو یا ڈونگا س مرے یا تھال ئس مرے
en: In a pot it takes a bit longer; in the cooker it's done in those twenty or thirty minutes. Then open the chicken and look: if it has boiled down and its water is dry, that's good. If it isn't dry, dry it off a bit so that the chicken smell goes away, otherwise the smell will get into the khurmin too. Then let it steam. After that, shred the chicken into small strips and take it out. Then take a nice, proper big plate, either a deep bowl or a tray.
en_old: In a pot it takes much longer; in the cooker it's done in those twenty or thirty minutes. en_old: The one who had come from far away would strike his blow. And it went like this: after the challenge, if one side couldn't hold its ground and gave way, the men would flee and give up the fight. A Brahui would not chase someone who had fled. That man was counted as defeated.

brh: یا ہڈاتے یا سوتے ای خسالپرہ کنپرہ ہندا ڈولٹ لٹ ئے او پاریکہ ای تینا جان ئنا انت ئنا دادے ہلپرہ دا اونا رسم ٹی ہرا وختا غاواک مسرہ جنگاک مسرہ یام تموکا بندغاک مسرہ اسہ قبیلہ ہڑینگاکہ ایلو قبیلہ والا یام تمارہ
en: '...or their bones or their flesh, I will not sell them and eat off them.' In the same way, about the beating penalty he would say, 'I will not take this for my own body, for whatever was done.' en_old: "...or their bones, I will not sell them or live off them." In the same way, about the penalty he would say, "I will not take this in exchange for the life of my own." This was in his custom when there were feuds and wars and people were killed: one tribe would clash and people of the other tribe would be killed.

brh: دا اوفتا دا مسرہ ہندا ڈولٹ براہوئی ہرا تینا زندگیس گدریفیکہ براہوئی نا زندگی کل آن زیادہ دا اسکہ کہ او مالداری اسکہ او کہ ارے کھر خوافیرہ
en: These were their ways. In the same way, the life the Brahui lived: the Brahui's life above all was this, that he was a herder; they had flocks and they grazed them.
en_old: These were their ways. In the same way, the life the Brahui lived was mostly that of a herder. He had flocks and they grazed their flocks.

en: Or they ploughed, looked after their lands and farmed; or else what they did was migrate and camp: they migrated, to Sindh and Khorasan they migrated, going and coming. And this was the life of the Brahuis, and...
en_old: Or they ploughed and looked after their lands and did farming. Or else they migrated: they went back and forth between Sindh and Khorasan. And that was the Brahui way of life.

en: ...their life was spent in these two or three occupations. And theirs was always a tent-dwelling life; they had flocks, and they grazed their flocks.
en_old: Their life was based on these two or three occupations. They always lived a nomadic tent life. They had flocks and they grazed their flocks.

brh: مالتے تینا خوافیرہ ہا یا ملکاتے تینا لنگارؤ ناڑی کریرہ دا ڈول تینا زندگی تے گدریفیرہ دا اوفتا زندگی نا دا طریقہ آک اسرہ۔

brh: مریک ہرادے سی ئکہ یا کوکنگ آئل کہ بکار ئٹی ہتیک براہوئی مخلوق
en: it is, which is the ghee, or the cooking oil, that the Brahui people put to use.

en_old: So this was our Brahui talk about ghee and cooking oil. The Brahui makes his ghee like this. Well, we talk about livestock, we talk about animal herding, and from livestock a lot...

brh: مخلوق نا ہراکہ کنوکا گڑاک او اوفتا ہنا مال مالداریت ان پیش تمرہ اگہ نن دانا ہمر کہ ای پاریٹ کہ دا ہراوخت آ ہیزک پورنگک کھلی پورنگک اوکا پدا داڑان خسی پیش تمک تو خسی ان پد ہرا بچوکا ہیزک ئٹی پاڷک مریرہ او خاسن پاننگرہ
en: the foods that people eat come from their, uh, livestock and herding. If we take this, as I said: when the skin bag is churned, the skin is churned, after that butter comes out of it; then after the butter, the milk that remains in the skin bag is called xāsin (buttermilk).
en_old: The food people eat comes from their livestock. If we take this, as I said: when the churning skin is churned, the buttermilk is churned, butter comes out of it. After the butter, the little milk left in the churning skin is called khasin.

brh: خاسن خاسن ئے او ا ا ہندا خریش اوار کرک سی و پاڷ کرک دوفتے تریت کرک کنک تو دا بھاز مزہ دارو بھاز گچینو تامس مریک ہرادے براہوئی مخلوق بھاز خو ہبس اٹ بھاز شمق اٹ کنیرہ
en: Xāsin: they mix that xāsin with, uh, uh, the same fine ghee, add ghee and milk, crumble bread into it and eat it; this is a very tasty, very excellent dish, which the Brahui people eat with great desire and great relish.
en_old: Khasin: they mix that khasin with the buttermilk, ghee and milk, crumble bread into it and eat it. It has a very delicious, excellent taste, and the Brahui people eat it with great pleasure and relish.

brh: بسم اللہ الرحمن الرحیم اینو نا ہرا کہ دا سرحال نا زیہا ہیت کننگ خواہوہ کنا سرحال ارے دادے کہ ای امر کہ نن تینا دے ئے شام اٹ وخت گدرینہ تو ننا براہوئی نا ثقافتاک رسماک ہندا دوداک ہندن چلینگ ٹی او داکا مست داسہ تو شاید
en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The topic I want to talk about today, my topic, is this: how we used to spend our days and pass the time in the evenings, and how our Brahui culture, customs and these traditions carried on like that, which before... now, perhaps,
en_old: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The topic I want to talk about today is how we spent our days and evenings, and how our Brahui culture, customs and traditions carried on, and that before... now perhaps...

brh: مچہ بھاز کم مسنو مہالو تو بھاز گچینی اٹ مست ئنا بندغاک پیرنگاک ورناک توسرہ اسہ جاگہ سے ٹی کس ئنا خلقا بسرہ اسہ شام ئس ہندنو گدرینگاککہ اینو کنا اراٹی بسر تو شام ئنا او شروع کریر ہندا توسر پنچ شش بندغو توسر کچاری مسکہ گڑا کسس تینا خراس ئسے
en: all of it has become very rare. Earlier, very pleasantly, the people of the past, elders and young men, would sit together in one place; they would come to someone's house, and an evening would pass like this: today they came to my house, so they started in the evening; they sat, five or six people would sit, a gathering would take place, then someone would talk about one of his oxen,
en_old: ...gatherings have become very rare. In the old days, very nicely, the people of the past, elders and young men, would sit in one place. They would come to someone's home, and an evening would pass like this: today they came to my house, and from the evening they began. Five or six people would sit together and a gathering would take place. Then someone would talk about his ox...

brh: نا حوالہ اٹ ہیت کریکہ کسس تینا اچ سے نا حوالہ اٹ کسس پائے ای دا کس تینا زغم سے نا ہیتے کریکہ تو ہندا ردٹ دا ہیتاک مرسامرسا ہندنو وخت مسکہ نن ئنا یک بجہ مسکہ یا دو بجہ مسکہ تو اوفک گڑا دا کچاری ایسر مسکہ گڑا ہر کس تینا خلقاتا ہناکہ صوب تماکہ
en: someone about his camel; someone would say, 'I...'; someone would talk about his sword. So in this way these talks would go on and on, and the time would pass like that until it was one o'clock at night or two o'clock; then that gathering would end, and then everyone would go to their homes and lie down until morning.
en_old: ...someone about his camel, someone would say... someone would talk about his sword. So in this way the talk would go on and on until it was one or two o'clock. Then the gathering would end, and everyone would go to their homes and sleep until morning.

brh: کس ئنا انت مال ئس اسکہ کس ئنا کھر ئس اسکہ خراس نا وڑٹ اچ ئنا وڑٹ میل دغر ککڑ مرو دا ہر وڑ ئنا سادار اوفتا اراٹی اسکہ تو کس بش مسکہ گڑا کھریئاہراکہ کھرے خوافیکہ بش مسکہ تینا کھرے
en: Whatever livestock someone had: someone had a flock, someone had animals like oxen or camels, and there would be sheep, kids and chickens. Every kind of animal was kept in their homes. So someone would get up, and then the shepherd, the one who grazed the flock, would get up and his flock...
en_old: Whatever livestock a person had, someone had a donkey, like oxen, camels, sheep, goats, chickens. Every kind of animal was in their homes. So someone would get up in the morning, the one who had a donkey would get up and wake his donkey...

brh: تینا زئے ہرفیکہ یکہ کریکہ خوڑدہ غاتے تینا ہڑفیکہ او تینا میل تے کشاکہ گڑا خوڑدہ غاتے ہڑساکہ ہنداڑے اراٹی
en: ...he would take his young kids and set them apart, hold back his lambs and drive out his sheep, and then he would keep the lambs back right there at home.
en_old: ...he would take his saddle and get it ready, take his young animals, drive out his sheep, and then load the young ones right there at home.

brh: گڑا ہندادے پارہ کہ زہ مطلب خوڑدہ ئ چنکا زہ پارکہ ہراکہ میلک اسرہ او کھرے تو کھریئا گڑا بش مسکہ تینا لٹ ئے ہرفیکہ تینا کلی ئے ہرفیکہ گڑاس چھنکو دستر خوان سے ٹی ہرادے نن دسترخوان ئے دسترخوان یا پڑنگ پارہ تہ ہرفیکہ اوڑا گڑا سی ؤ
en: Then this is what they call 'zah', meaning the lambs, the little ones. They called the ones that were young sheep 'zah'. And as for the flock, the shepherd would get up, take his stick, take his water skin, and take some small things in a cloth, which we call a dastarkhwan; they call it dastarkhwan or 'paṛang'. In it there would be ghee and...
en_old: Then they call this 'zeh', meaning the small young ones. 'Zeh' is what they call the young of the sheep. And the donkey owner would get up, take his stick, take his axe, and take something small in a cloth, which we call dastarkhwan or 'parang', and on it ghee and...

brh: ارغس ہرفیکہ ہراکہ خریش اٹ چرپ مسکہ انتس تیار مسکہ بوڑ ئس اودے ہرفیکہ شاغاکہ تینا چنکو وٹی سے ٹی گڑا او راہی مسکہ تینا ہرفیکہ کھرے ہکلاکہ لٹ ہندنو مسکہ گڑاس خط ئنا لٹ مریک ہرا درخت سے خط پارہ مش ٹی مریک او تو بھاز پختہ او ڈڈو لٹ ئس
en: ...some bread that had been greased with fine ghee. Whatever was ready, some curry, he would take and put in his small pouch. Then he would set off, take his things and drive the flock. The stick was like this: sometimes it was a stick of wild olive. The wild olive, which they call 'khat', is a tree that grows in the mountains, and it makes a very strong, hard stick.
en_old: ...he would take bread greased with buttermilk, whatever was ready, a bowl of something, and put it in his little bag. Then he would set off, taking his donkey and driving it on. The stick would be a 'khat' stick. Khat is a tree found in the mountains, and it makes a very strong, thick stick.

brh: مریک تو اود ہرفتے کھریئا تینا لٹے گڑا ہکلاکہ کھرے تینا مشٹ راہی مسکہ گڑا صوب ئنا داکا پیشتنگاکہ گڑا ایلو بقایا مخلوق گودی بش مسکہ تینا ہرفیکہ نسخل ئس نساکہ یا تینا بوڑ ئسے نا بندوستے کریکہ یا تینا ارغ نا بندوبست ئے کریکہ شروع مسکہ گڑا چھناک اوکا مچ مسر بسرکہ
en: ...So the shepherd took his stick, drove the flock and set off into his mountains, leaving from here in the morning. Then the rest of the people, the women, would get up. They would take the hand mill and grind, or prepare some curry, or prepare the bread. They would get started, and then the children would gather there and come.
en_old: So the donkey owner took his stick, drove his donkey and set off to his mountain. He would leave in the morning. Then the rest of the people, the women, would get up, take the hand mill and grind, or prepare a bowl of something, or arrange the bread. Then the children would gather and come.

brh: گڑا انتس اراٹی اسکہ او ٹائم ئنا غریبی نا وخت اسکہ او ٹائما تا سی ؤ پال ئس اسکہ چائے خاسن ئس اسکہ چائے خسیس اسکہ انتس اسکہ ہموفتے تینا ہیسکہ گڑا چھناک تہ مچ مسرکہ گڑا ہوس آن کہ اینو دا گڑا مسنے کریرکہ انتس مسکہ کنگرکہ اوکا پدا voice خواجہ ہرفیکہ ارا خواجہ بھلا
en: Then there was whatever there was at home. That was a time of poverty. In those days there was ghee and milk, maybe some lassi, maybe some butter. Whatever there was, she would bring it out to them. Then the children would gather, eager to see what had been made that day, and they would eat whatever there was. After that the master, the master of the house who was the elder, would take...
en_old: Then whatever there was at home... that was a time of poverty. In those days there was ghee and milk, tea, khasin, tea, butter, whatever there was, they would bring it. The children would gather and ask what had happened today, and they would eat whatever there was. After that the head of the house, the elder...

brh: مسکہ او ارا خراس جفت کریکہ ہرفیکہ دریکہ تا ہناکہ کاریم نا اگہ موسم مسکہ ناڑی نا یا لنگارنا تو ہرفیکہ تینا جفت ئے ہڑتوما ارا خراس مسرکہ
en: ...would yoke the two oxen together as a pair, take them and go to work. If it was the sowing season or the plowing season, he would take his pair. Both of them were oxen.
en_old: ...the elder would yoke the oxen, take them and go to work. If it was the sowing or plowing season, he would take his pair; both were oxen.

brh: گڑاس کاریگر پارہ تا گڑاس جفت خراس تے گڑا ہناکہ تینا ملکا ہمیڑے تینا ڈغار ٹی گڑا ہرفیکہ لنگارے اسیکہ voice شاغاکہ خراس تا نیام ٹی ہراکہ خراس تے ارٹ کیک ہڑتوماتے اوار تفیسہ تا اور اگہ پاٹ ئس اوتا لخ تے ٹی شاغنگک اودے پارکہ جغ
en: Some call them 'kārīgar', and some say a pair of oxen. Then he would go to his field, right there on his own land, and take the plow. First he would put [unclear] between the oxen, the piece that joins the oxen and ties both of them together. The piece of wood that is put on their necks was called the 'jugh' (yoke).
en_old: Some call them workers. Some would yoke the oxen, then go to their land, there in their own field. They would take the plow, first put [unclear] between the oxen, which joins the two oxen together, and a piece of wood placed on their necks is called 'jugh' (yoke).

brh: پارہ جغ جغ اسکہ جغ کریرہ ہڑتوما خراس تے اوفتے یام اٹ تا شاغاکہ لنگارے اگہ لنگار ہرا پاٹ ئے مرغنا یام ٹی بریک اودے شتینک پارہ شتینک بریک ؤ شتینک ولا کائک ایٹی لگیک اینا شیف ہرا آہن بریک آہن ئس بھاز تیزو اور زمینے ہرا ارک اودے پارہ کمیرگڑا دا خراس تے صوب نا شروع کریکہ کاریمے
en: They call it 'jugh'. There was a jugh, and they would yoke both oxen with it and put the plow between them. As for the plow, the long piece of wood that comes in the middle is called the 'shatīnk'. The shatīnk part goes on and is attached to it, and under it comes the iron, a very sharp piece of iron that cuts into the ground. They call that the 'kamīr' (plowshare). Then in the morning he would start the oxen on their work.
en_old: They call it jugh. There was a yoke, and they would yoke both oxen, line them up and attach the plow. The wood in the middle of the plow is called 'shatink'. The shatink goes back and forth, and attached below it is a very sharp iron blade that goes into the ground, which they call 'kamir'. Then they would start working the oxen in the morning.

brh: تینا گڑا ہندا لنگار ہناکہ دریکہ ہنداتیکہ لنگار مسکہ لنگار چٹاکہ گودی ہیسکہ ارغاتے او تینا توسرہ اوار کنگرکہ ہنتس اسکہ بارن پالن کنگرتا اوکا پدا شروع مسکہ مالہ مالہ ہمودے کہ اسہ پاٹ ئس مرغنو پلک آن بارو جوڑارکہ اوٹی داخسو آہن لگاکہ
en: ...his. In this way the plow would go on, he would drive it, and the plowing would get done. When the plowing was finished, the woman would bring the bread, and they would sit together and eat whatever there was, dry or moist. After that the 'māla' (leveling) would begin. The māla is a long piece of wood made like a plank, and they fixed this much iron onto it,
en_old: ...then the plow would go and the plowing would be done. Once the plowing was finished, the women would bring the bread, and they would sit together and eat whatever there was until they were full. After that the leveling ('mala') would begin. A wide plank of wood was made into a board, with this much iron attached to it,

brh: ہراکہ نیش پارہ تہ او مطلب نیش پاریرہ تہ یا ہندن تیزو آہن سے اوفتے کمیر پاننگ کیسہ تہ یا اوفتے شاغارہ گڑا ہندا تفیرہ تا خراس تے ٹی تفیرہ تا خراس تے ٹی گڑا سوار مسکہ زیہاتا ہرا بندغ اسکہ ہراکہ مالہ ئے گراکہ تہ خراس گرارہ تہ دا سوار مسکہ زیہا تہ گڑا ہندادے پیری
en: ...which they call 'nēsh', I mean they called them nēsh, or sharp pieces of iron like that; you could also call them 'kamīr'. They would put those on, then tie it to the oxen, tie it to the oxen. Then the person dragging the māla would ride on top of it. The oxen pulled it, and he rode on top. Then, going in circles...
en_old: ...which they call 'nesh', meaning they call it nesh, or such sharp iron, you could also call it kamir. They would attach these and hitch them to the oxen. Then a person would ride on top, the one pulling the mala, while the oxen pulled it. He would ride on top, and this they call 'piri'.

brh: ترسا ترسا ہندا لنگار تے اٹ گڑاس شوم بسکہ
en: Turning round and round with these plows, eventually some of the land would become soft, tilled soil.
en_old: Little by little, with this plowing, the soil would become fine and soft.

brh: شوم مسکہ گڑا دا مسکہ بالکل زمین یلہ یلہ مسکہ گڑا ہراکہ مستی بروکا وخت ٹی ہراکہ فصل مسکہ اونا خولم شاغارہ تہ یا سا شاغارہ تہ یا جواری یا ماش مٹر ہنت فصل ئس کریکہ اوٹی شاغارہ تو دا طریقہ اٹ ہراکہ خراس تا نیام ٹی ہرا چٹ بسکہ ہڑتوما خراس تے اسٹ کریکہ اودے
en: It would become soft, tilled soil, and then the land would become completely loose. Then in the coming season they would sow whatever crop there was: wheat, barley, sorghum, mung beans or peas. Whatever crop he grew, they would sow it in that soil. So in this way, the cord that came between the oxen and joined both oxen into one, that...
en_old: It would become soft, and then the land would become completely loose. Then, in the coming season, whatever crop there was, they would sow its seed, whether wheat, sorghum, mung beans or peas. Whatever crop he grew, they would sow it in that soil. So in this way, the wood that came between the oxen and joined both of them together, that...

brh: پسید پارہ ہراکہ خراس ئے دا خراس اے خراس ایوار مون اٹ اسہ خراس مسکہ ایلو پدٹ ہرا خراس ئے دریکہ اسٹ مسکہ چٹہ اودے پسید پارہ بقایا ننا ایلو اچ اسکہ اچا تینا پاٹ ئکہ مش تا ٹرنگڑ ئے ہرفیکہ اونا زیہا تخاکہ رخت ئے رخت ٹی قتباک بریرہ ہراکہ مون نا اونا پاٹ کو خواجہ ئے پاس ہراکہ ہرا اچ ئنا کیرہ غان
en: ...they call the 'pasīd'. With the oxen, this ox and that ox together, one ox in front and the other behind, the cord that leads the ox becomes one, and that is called the 'pasīd'. Besides that, we had the other animal, the camel. For the camel, for his firewood trips to the mountains, he would take the ṭarangaṛ (load frame) and put the pack-saddle on top of it. The pack-saddle has the saddle-trees, its front wooden pieces, sir, as I said, which sit on the camel's flanks.
en_old: They call it the 'paseed', the one that is the string of camels. One string would be in front, another behind, and whichever string you kept, there was one leader, they called it the paseed. As for the rest of our camels, on each camel's back they would lift the saddle frame made of dwarf palm and put it on top, and the load would go on top of that. The bags would come into the load, sir, as I said, the ones that are put on the camel's sides.

brh: چٹ ئس بریک اودے پادہ پھڈ کش ہراکہ اچ ئنا بامس ٹی شاغنگک ہرا اسہ آہن ئس مریک اودے لانٹی پارہ لانٹی ٹی ہرا مہر شاغرہ تہ اودے نی مہر کیسہ او مہٹ اچ نی رندٹ اوکا خواجہ ئے پاریسٹ ہراٹائماتا ہراکہ دا ننا رخت زیہا تخوکا بریک رخت ٹی خشتہ ہرا پاٹکو اوفتے باسکی پارہ
en: A cord comes, which they call the 'piḍkash' (belly-band). The thing put into the camel's nose is a piece of iron, and they call it the 'lānṭī'. They put the nose-rein into the lānṭī, you hold the rein, and by the rein the camel follows behind you. After that, sir, as I told you, at that time this pack-saddle of ours that is placed on top: in the pack-saddle there are blocks, wooden ones, and they call them 'bāskī'.
en_old: A piece comes that they call the nose peg, which is put into the camel's nose. It is a piece of iron, they call it 'lanti'. Into the lanti they put the lead rope, then you hold the rope and the camel follows behind you. Then, as I told you sir, at that time the load that is put on top, the bricks of salt go into the load, and the bags for them are called 'baski'.

brh: ہراکہ اونا بندغ پد ٹی جکو اسہ جوڑ مریک اودے کونٹی مریک ہرا کہ بندغ جھوکہ خلیک ایہاتہ اودے پارہ کونٹی ہراکہ اچ ئنا کوہان نا زیہا شاغرہ اودے جل پارہ جل ئس بریک اودے پارہ جل ہراکہ اچے رخت ئے تہ ہلنگان بچفک اچ ئنا ہراکہ جاگہ غاک رخت ئنا ڈڈ مریرہ تو او اچے بچفک ٹھپ مننگان
en: For its rider at the back a seat is made. That is the 'konṭī', where a person sits swaying on it; they call it the konṭī. What they put over the camel's hump is called the 'jul'. A jul goes on, they call it jul, and it keeps the pack-saddle from chafing the camel. Wherever the pack-saddle is hard on the camel, it protects the camel from getting sores.
en_old: The person who rides at the back has a seat made for him, called the 'konti', where a person sits and swings, that is called the konti. What they put over the camel's hump is called the 'jul'. A jul comes, they call it jul, which protects the camel from being hurt by the load. Wherever the load has hard spots, it protects the camel from getting sores.

brh: ہرا کہ تنگ ئس بریک تنگ اٹ کونٹ کونٹی پارہ تنگ اے ہرا تنگہ اے ہرا تنگہ اٹ جوڑہ رخت ئے او رخت نا تہٹی کانز شاغارکہ
en: Then a girth comes. With the girth the konṭ... they call it konṭī. That is the girth, the girth they fasten the pack-saddle with, and inside the pack-saddle they would put kans grass.
en_old: Then a girth comes, the strap of the konti is called the girth; with the girth they made the load fast, and inside the load they would put stuffing.

brh: کانزاکثر دہن ایہن جاگہ تے ملپک کانز شاغارہ تہ گڑا زو زو برتوکہ او زو ہرے اسکان پائیدار مسکہ اور ہراکہ کونٹی نا بج ٹی ارا مون ہروک خلکرکہ مون ہروک خلکرکہ ؤ خوبصورتی کہ اونا زیبائی کہ اگہ مر آن اچ خننگاکہ بجی مسکہ تو اونا ہمو شمبلاخ تہ سرک بج ئنا تہ
en: Kans grass is mostly not found in places like this. They would put kans grass in, so it wouldn't wear out quickly and would last a long time. And on the back of the konṭī they would fix two mirrors, they would fix mirrors for beauty, for its decoration, so that if the camel was seen from far away, the glint from its back would reach you.
en_old: They usually didn't find stuffing in places like this. When they put stuffing in, it wouldn't wear out quickly and it would last for a long time. And in the middle of the konti they would fix mirrors, they would fix mirrors for beauty, for its decoration, so that if the camel was seen from far away, its glitter would reach far.

brh: شیشہ مورونکاک تو گڑا او شوق کریرکہ اچ ٹی چمر ئس شاغارکہ خواجہ ئے پاریسٹ اونا لخ ٹی چڑینگ شاغارکہ او وختس اچ ئس یلہ مسکہ یا راہی کریرہ تہ الارہ تہ خواہنگ کہ یلہ کریرہ تہ اچ ہرانگ ہناکہ تو ہراتم مالک بش مسکہ بھئی کاو اچے تینا اتیو بریو اراغا تا پٹینگ ؤ
en: Glass, mirrors and things like that: they were fond of them. They would put a tassel on the camel, sir, as I told you, and put bells on its neck. Sometimes a camel would get loose, or they would send it off and let it go to graze, let it loose, and the camel would wander off somewhere. Then when the owner got up he would say, 'Well, let me go and bring my camel back,' and while he searched for where it was,
en_old: Mirrors and things like that; they were fond of it. They would put a tassel on the camel, sir, as I said, and put bells on its neck. So when a camel got loose or they had let it go to graze, wherever the camel went, when the owner woke up he'd say, let's go fetch the camel, and they'd search for it by its sound.

brh: چڑینگو توار کریکہ اوٹی چھیر شاغارکہ چنکا ہیژرو تان شاغارہ اوتا نت تے ٹی تاکہ اچ ٹی خوبصورتی پین برے زیبائی اودے رنگ کریرکہ اودے انام کریرکہ اچ ئے ہراکہ او اخس پین خوبصورتی بسکہ ایٹی تہ تو ہندا اچا ہنا رخت تہ مسکہ رخت ئنا زیہا شاغارہ تخارہ ٹرنگڑ ئے ٹرنگڑ ٹی
en: the bells would ring out. They would put ornaments on it, small ornaments on their feet, so that the camel would get even more beauty and decoration. They would paint it and decorate the camel so that it got that much more beauty. Then the pack-saddle would go on this same camel, and on top of the pack-saddle they would put the ṭarangaṛ (load frame). In the ṭarangaṛ...
en_old: The bells would ring. They would put in tassels and small shells on its legs so that the camel would look even more beautiful; they would color it for decoration and adorn the camel, so that much more beauty came to it. Then on this same camel the load would go; they'd put the load on top of the saddle frame, on the frame.

brh: اسہ واڈر ئس مسکہ ہرا چٹ ئس بریک اودے ارہ واڈر گڑا اودے دریرکہ انارکہ مشا مش ٹی ہراکہ او پاٹ کریرکہ پیش ئنا ہم بریک اوڑے خط بریک خواجہ ئے پاریسٹ پین مختلف قسم ئنا اوڑے وڑئنا پاٹ بریک اچھاکسے پیش بریک ہرابھئی او پالنا پیش ہرا بارک اودے پارہ
en: ...there would be a 'vāḍar', a cord that goes on. That is the vāḍar. Then they would take it and go to the mountains, into the mountains, where they collected firewood. Dwarf palm also grows there, and wild olive grows there, sir, as I told you, and other different kinds of wood. A good amount of dwarf palm grows there. The fresh dwarf palm, the fine kind, is called
en_old: There would be a rope, a piece that they call a rope, and they would hold it and bring it from dwarf palm to dwarf palm. With it they'd make the bags, out of the palm leaves; mats are also made from it, sir, as I said, and other different kinds of things. A good amount of palm leaf would come out, that is, the leaf they call 'palan'.

brh: پیشنگ تو اکثر ننا جنداک کرینن اچاتا ہنانن بیش تاہنانن ٹرنگڑ ٹی پیش کرینن ہراکہ پڑچ کہ بریک ہرا پیش
en: 'pīšing'. Mostly we ourselves have done this. We have gone with camels and with donkeys, and we have loaded dwarf palm into the ṭarangaṛ, the dwarf palm that is used for mats.
en_old: Mostly our own people have done the palm leaf work. We went to the camels, we went for palm leaves, we made palm leaves into saddle frames, and the palm leaf comes for mats too.

brh: او گڑاس اونا مختلف مختلف وڑ ئنا مریرہ ہراکہ ہرکسے ہر وڑ ئنا اوفتے ٹی پیش بریک ء اوفتان پڑچ جوڑ مریک ارافتان وارڈر چٹ جوڑ مریک اوفتان پیش آن او نن ہنانہ اکثر ہرا پیشک مسرہ پیش تے ہراکہ کچوو مسرکہ چاہسنہ دا کاریم چور اوفتے نن تڑتونہ کہ
en: Its products come in many different kinds and serve everyone in every way. Dwarf palm goes into them: mats are made from it, ropes and cords are made from it, from the dwarf palm. We would mostly go where there was dwarf palm. The dwarf palms that were still young (we knew this work), those we would not cut.
en_old: These things come in many different kinds; everyone uses palm leaf in his own way. Mats are made from them, ropes and pieces are made from them. From the palm leaves we would go, mostly where there were palm leaves, the ones that were half-grown, you know, this work, we used to pick them.

brh: لشی ننتو مسکہ تڑتونہ تا پانہ کہ بھئی مستی برور بھلن مروربارور گڑا بارنا ت دین سہی اے ہشنگ کہ ننے کاریم بھی تیرہ پالناک پرچ کہ کاریم تیرہ چٹ ئس گوفنگ کہ کاریم تیرہ اوکا مستی پین ہم اوفتے ٹی ہا پیش ٹی بھکی بریک بھکی ٹی اسہ پین مزہ ئس مریک voice اودے کشارک ہرا زی
en: Even if there were a lot of them near us, we wouldn't cut them. We would say, 'Well, let them grow on, get big and dry out.' Then the dry ones are good for burning, so our needs get met too. The fresh ones are useful for mats and for weaving cord. Beyond that, inside the dwarf palm there is also the 'bhakī' (palm heart), and the bhakī has a different taste. They would take it out, the part that
en_old: We would gather a lot of them. We'd pick them, we used to say, let them get ripe, let them grow big, then the leaf will be right to cut so our work gets done too. The palan gets the work done, cutting a piece gets the work done. After that, a palm heart also comes inside the palm leaf, and the palm heart has a different taste. We would take it out, the one that...

brh: ئٹی تے بریک ہراکہ مطلب اونا پھل تیا ہندا بھکی بریک بھکی ئے کشانکہ خل ئسے آ کٹانہ گڑا کنگنہ آن تہ بھی اور خوبصورت اونا ذائقس بھی اسکہ بھاز بھکی کنگنکہ اوکا بسنہ گڑا او اچ ئنا ہرا ٹائم بارنا پیش تان چائے خط ئنا مسرکہ چائے ہم ئنا مسرکہ تیار مسکہ باریم باریم گڑا ارا
en: grows inside at the top, meaning its fruit. That is the bhakī. We would take out the bhakī, pound it on a stone and eat it. It was lovely, and it had a taste too; we ate a lot of bhakī. After that we came back. Then, when it was time for the camel's load, of dry dwarf palm, maybe wild olive or maybe other wood too, the load would be ready, load after load. Then two
en_old: ...comes in the middle, meaning its bud, that is the palm heart. We'd take out the palm heart, crush it on a stone, then we'd eat it, and its taste was really lovely. We ate a lot of palm heart. After that, when the time for the camel's loads came, the palm leaves, maybe tea, maybe salt, tea would be ready, the loading would be ready, and then two...

brh: مسہ بندغ بسنکہ دانگان تورینہ ٹرنگڑئے اینگان اے سنگت ٹرنگڑ ئے توریکہ شاغانہ پاٹ تے تہٹی تہ گڑا وارڈر ئے دانگان شاغانہ اینگان چکانہ تہ بڑز کرینہ تہ بڑز کرینہ تاکہ اچے ہلپ خشت آن دانگان اینگان و جل بھی شاغانہ تہ وختس بھلو جل ئس شاغانہ چنکوس مسکہ گڑا دا ٹرنگڑ ئے جوان سوگو کرینہ ایکا ٹرند تفینہ مٹاتے تہ تاکہ او
en: or three people would come. We would hold the ṭarangaṛ from this side, and that friend would hold the ṭarangaṛ from the other side. We would put the wood inside, then put the rope over from this side and pull it from the other side, and lift it up, lift it up, so that the blocks wouldn't hurt the camel on either side. We would also put the jul on, sometimes a big jul, sometimes a small one. Then we would make this ṭarangaṛ nice and firm and tie the knots tight, so that it
en_old: ...three people would come, here and there we'd hold the saddle frame, this friend would hold the frame from that side, we'd put the bags in, then we'd put the rope over from here and there, pull it and lift it up, lift it up so the bricks wouldn't hurt the camel, and we'd also put the jul on. Sometimes we'd put on a big jul, sometimes a small one, then we'd tie this saddle frame tight, tie it hard all over so that it...

brh: بڑز مرے باریم اچے خوار کپ تو گڑا راہی مسنہ گڑا اچ ہندن اسکہ ہیل اسکہ نن او نن پدٹ تہ مسنہ او مونٹ
en: would be raised up, so the load wouldn't distress the camel. Then we would set off. The camel was like that: it was trained. We would be behind it, and it would be in front.
en_old: ...would be raised up, so the load wouldn't hurt the camel. Then we'd set off, and the camel was like that, it was trained; we'd be behind and it in front.

brh: خلقے خناکہ کسر چائے اشکنومسکہ چائے زنڈوجاگہس مسکہ چائے کھڈو جاگہس مسکہ اچ خنوک اسکہ گڑا وختس ہندن مسکہ ہنانکہ دیر کٹفینکہ دیر تینتو ہرفتونہ دیر کٹفینکہ گڑا امر کرینکہ ہرا کہ ننا جھلک اسرکہ جھراک مش تے ٹی ہراکا ہنانہ پٹانہ نمبہ او جاگہ پٹانہ خنانکہ بھئی دا
en: It knew the village. The road, whether it was narrow, a resting place or a place full of pits: the camel had seen it all. Then sometimes we would go and run out of water, because we didn't carry water with us. So what would we do? There were our riverbeds, the streams in the mountains, where we would go and search for damp ground. We would search for a spot and see that this
en_old: It saw people, it knew the way, it was the road, maybe a flat place, maybe a hollow place, the camel had seen it. Then sometimes it happened that we went and stopped for water, we carried water with us and stopped for water. Then what we did, there were our streams, the streams in the dwarf palm hills, we'd go and search for damp spots, search for a place and see whether here...

brh: جاگہ آ امیدارے دیر ئنا تو گڑا ہنداکہ ختانکہ ہمو جاگہ ئے ختانکہ چنکو او ٹائم دیر لڑد مسکہ لڑد مسکہ دیر مچٹ انتظار کرینکہ توسنہ رہا تہ گڑا دیر ہراتم روشن مسکہ گڑا او دیر آن کانی مسکہ کانی پارینہ تہ کنگنہ آن تہ اونا دیر ٹی ہمو گچینی اسکہ ذائقہ اسکہ کنگنہ سمجھہ ننا
en: place had hope of water. Then we would dig right there, dig that spot a little. At first the water would be muddy, it would be muddy, so we would wait a little for the water and sit at ease. Then when the water became clear, it became 'kānī', as we call it, and we would drink it. Its water had that goodness, it had a taste when we drank it. You understand, our
en_old: ...there is hope of water at this place. Then we'd dig right there, dig that place a little. At that time the water would be muddy, it would be muddy, we'd wait a little for the water, we'd sit down and rest, and then when the water became clear, it would be clear water, we called it clear, then we'd drink it, and its water had that goodness, it had a taste when we drank it, you understand, our...

brh: وخت وخت مسکہ ہراکہ چاء کرینہ ہمو دیرتان ننا کرو مسکہ کٹلی ہرادے پانہ کروبھی پانہ تہ چادانی پانہ تہ نن گڑا تینتو اسہ چادانیس ہرفینکہ گڑا اوٹی چاء کرینکہ سنگتاک توسنہ پیالہ آک مسرکہ ہیسنہ تینا پیالہ تے ٹی چاء کنگنکہ گڑاسیئو ارغس ہرفینکہ ہرا چرپ مسکہ خریش اٹ یا سی اٹ
en: Sometimes we would make tea with that water. We had a 'karo', a kettle; we call it karo and we also call it a teapot. We would take a teapot with us and make tea in it. The friends would sit down, there were cups, and we would pour the tea into our cups and drink it. Then we would take some bread that was greased with fine ghee or with butter.
en_old: ...times were those times. When we made tea, with that water, we had a kettle, which we call 'karo', also called a teapot. We would carry a teapot with us and make tea in it. The friends would sit, there were cups, we'd pour into our cups and drink tea, and we'd take some food, which would be greasy, with ghee or with oil.

brh: زبان نا تخرہ او تینا زبان تیٹ بھاز گچینی اٹ ہیت کیرہ او ننا اکثر پاکستان ٹی چائینیزاک بھاز بریرہ ننتو اوفتا زیاتر آمد و رفت ارے اوفت ننے ہندا تینا زبانے ہیل تننگ نا کوشش ئےکیرہ نن بھی تینا زبانے ہیل تین کہ براہوئی تینا چین ٹی نن ہمہ زندہ کرون تو اکثر ہرا گڑاس نوجواناک ایڑے خوانرہ اور تینا براہوئی زبان ئے ہمیڑے بھی کیرہ
en: ...take great care of their language, and they speak their own language very well. Chinese people often come to our Pakistan a lot, and they come and go with us a great deal. They try to teach us their own language, and we should teach them our language too, so that we keep Brahui alive there in China as well. And often some of the young people who study there also use their Brahui language there.
en_old: language... they speak their own languages very well. Chinese people often come to our Pakistan a lot; they come and go with us a lot; they try to teach us their language, and we also teach them our language, so that we keep Brahui alive in China too. Often some young people who study there also use their Brahui language there.

brh: گڑاس چینی تے ہیل تسنو بھی تینا براہوئی زبانے تو ہندن کہ افریقہ نا مریک زبان افریقی اے ہاں پین مختلف بھاز زبانو ہراکہ داسہ دا ننا پاکستان ٹی تو بھاز زبان اریر ہرافک کنے یادو ہراکہ بلوچی مریک پشتونے سندھی اے سرائیکی
en: They have also taught some Chinese people their Brahui language. So likewise, Africa's language is African, yes, and many other different languages. Now, here in our Pakistan there are many languages, the ones I remember: there is Balochi, Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki,
en_old: They have also taught some Chinese people their Brahui language. So likewise Africa's language is African; yes, and many other various languages. Now in our Pakistan there are many languages, the ones I remember: Balochi, Pashto, Sindhi, Saraiki,

brh: ڈومکی بریک ہاں لاسی بریک پنجابی ارے تو مختلف زبانکو ہرافتے گڑاس ای ہیت کننگ کیوہ لیکن اوخس زبان کنا readyافک تو ہنداخس کنا چائنداریک اسرہ اوداکا مستی ان شاء اللہ مزید مرو مہربانی
en: there is Domki, yes, there is Lasi, there is Punjabi. So there are various languages, some of which I can speak, but I don't have that many languages ready. So this much was my knowledge; beyond this, God willing, there will be more. Thank you.
en_old: Domki comes, yes, Lasi comes, Punjabi is there; so various languages, some of which I can speak, but not that many languages are ready for me. So this much was my knowledge; beyond that, God willing, there will be more. Thank you.

I will talk about the season for planting trees. Trees: there are many, many kinds of trees. Among them, in the mountains,

I'll talk about the season of planting trees. Trees: there are many, many kinds of trees; among these, in the mountains

brh: رخت یکہ بریک میدان تیا یکہ بریک دیر ئنا رخت بریک مختلف بھاز کہ ارے وڑئنارخت بریک رختاتے ٹی مش ٹی ہرا رختاک مریرہ او بھاز وڑ ئنا رخت ارے ہرافتے ٹی اسٹ ہم بریک ہم آن پدا ہرا خط بریک پیپل بریک
en: there are separate trees, in the plains there are separate ones, and there are trees of the water; there are many different kinds of trees. Among the trees, the trees that grow in the mountains are of many kinds, among which one is the 'ham'. After the ham comes the khat (wild olive), and the pipal.
en_old: there are trees, in the plains there are trees, there are trees by the water, many various kinds of trees. Among the trees, the trees that grow in the mountains are of many kinds, among which one is the 'ham'; after the ham comes the 'khat', and the pipal comes.

brh: اوکا چنکا بریرہ گؤن گؤنک بریک گؤنک آن پدا پیش بھی رخت ئس پاننگک اوٹی ہرا کول تہ بریک کول تہ بڑز مریک او رخت سے نا شکل ٹی ظاہر مریک پدا اوکا پر پک بھی مریک مش تے ٹی مریک پرپک میدانا بھی پرپک
en: After that come the small ones: the gwan and the gwanak. After the gwanak, the pish (dwarf palm) is also called a tree; in it grows what is called the 'kol', and the kol rises up and takes the form of a tree. Then after that there is also the parpuk; it grows in the mountains, and there is also a parpuk of the plains.
en_old: Its smaller ones come: the 'gwan' and 'gwanak'. After the gwanak, the 'pish' is also called a tree; in it the 'kol' grows, the kol rises up and appears in the shape of a tree. Then after that there is also the 'parpuk'; it grows in the mountains, and there is also the parpuk of the plains.

brh: مریک پرپک ہمو رختے ہرا پھل ئس پوشکنو کیک تینا موسم ٹی اور پھل ٹی تہ دیر بریک اور دیرک کننگ بھی مریرہ دیرک کننگ نا ذائقس بھی جوانو ارے ٹی تہ اور پر پک نا پاٹے کمرہ نا انت نا گیڈ ئنا زیہا چھت کہ بھی استعمال مریک
en: is there. The parpuk is the tree that puts out a yellow flower in its season, and inside the flower there is liquid, and the liquid can be drunk too; drinking the liquid also has a good taste. And the parpuk's wood is also used for rooms, for, what is it, for the roofs over sheds.
en_old: The parpuk is the tree that puts out new flowers in its season, and inside the flower there is nectar, and people also eat the nectar; its taste is good too. And the wood of the parpuk is used for rooms, for the roofs of houses.

brh: اوڑان کرز بھی پیشتنگک اوڑان تیر بھی پیشتنگک اونا سختو پاٹ ئس مریک بھاز
en: Rafters are also made from it, and roof beams are also made from it; its wood is very hard.
en_old: Ploughs are also made from it, arrows are also made from it; its wood is very hard.

brh: اونا چھل کنا خیال پائے کھڑ کہ خوا بسنگ کہ بھی بریک چھل ئے تہ خلیسہ اونا چھل ئس بریک اونا چھل ئے خلیسہ او خوا کہ بھی بریک ایلو نرومب نرومب بھی اسہ رخت سے اونا بھی چھل مریک یا جند ئنا تہ ہراکہ مریک اودے بھی خوا ٹی شاغرہ و ولدا ہیٹ ئے تڑرہ اونا سل ئے کشرہ
en: Its bark, I think, is also used for hides and for curing water-skins. They strip off the bark; it has bark, and stripping off its bark they use it for water-skins too. Another one is the narumb; the narumb is also a tree, and it has bark too, or whatever is inside its trunk; they put that into the water-skin too, and then they butcher the goat and take off its skin.
en_old: Its bark, I think, is also used for tanning skins; they strip off the bark, its bark comes off, and stripping its bark they use it for the skins too. Another one, the 'narumb', is also a tree; it also has bark, or whatever is inside it, they put that in the skin too and then rub the hide and remove its hair.

brh: ہندا نرومباتے شاغرہ الرہ تہ تاکہ او نا تہہ او بسک بسک اوکا پدان دیر شاغا س تہ خوا ٹی گڑا دیرک تہ تام کپسہ مچہ منہ دے اسکا کیرہ اوکا پد تام کپسہ اوکا پدا پرپک آن پدا بریک دا جھگ بریک جھگ پانہ تہ جاگہ سے آ ٹالی بھی پارہ تہ جھگ ئنا بھلو رخت ئس مریک اونا پن ئس چنکو مریک رخت
en: They put these narumb in and leave them so that its inside gets cured; after that, if you pour water into the water-skin, then the water doesn't take on a taste. They keep doing this for a few days, after which it doesn't take on a taste. Then, after the parpuk, comes the jhag. We call it jhag, but in some places they also call it 'tali'. The jhag is a big tree; its leaves are small, but the tree
en_old: They put these narumb in and leave it so that it soaks inside; after that they put water in the skin, and then the water doesn't take on a taste; they keep it for a few days, after which it doesn't take on a taste. After the parpuk comes the 'jhag'; in some places they also call the jhag 'tali'. The jhag is a big tree; its name is small, but the tree

brh: ئس بھلو اخس عمر کے ہموخہ زیادہ بھلن مریک بھاز بھلو بھنڈس کشیک اونا شانکاک بھلن مریرہ اونا بھلو شاخ کشیک بھلو شولک خلیک جھگ نا اونا بھی ہندنو پاٹ ئس سختو مریک او بھی ہشنگ کہ کاریم کیک اودے ہراکہ مستی ہراکہ دیرہ تہ کمپنیک اوڑان پلک بھی جوڑ مریک اوڑان
en: is big: the older it gets, the bigger it becomes. It grows a very big trunk, its branches become big, it puts out big boughs and big limbs, the jhag. It also has that kind of hard wood, and it is also used for burning. Beyond that, the companies that take it also make beds from it;
en_old: is big; the older it gets, the bigger it becomes. It grows a very big trunk; its branches are big, it puts out big boughs and casts a big shade. The jhag's wood is also hard; it is also used for burning. Earlier, companies also made beds from it,

brh: الماری شوکیس داک بھی جوڑ مریرہ ٹی تہ جھگ آن علاوہ بریسہ واپس اسہ پین مش ئنا ہرا بریک پسی پسی بھی بھاز گچینو رخت سے او پت بھی مریک ٹی تہ اور اونا چنکو اسہ بھرم ئس مریک بھرم تہ پسی ہمودے ہراٹی کننگا مزہ اول کھٹک مریک
en: cupboards and showcases are also made from it. Besides the jhag, coming back to another mountain tree, there is the pissi. The pissi is also a very fine tree; it has thorns too, and it has a small fruit. The fruit of the pissi, when you eat it, tastes sour at first;
en_old: and cupboards and showcases are also made from it. Besides the jhag, coming back to another mountain tree, the 'pasi': the pasi is also a very fine tree, it also has leaves, and it has a small fruit. The fruit of the pasi, when you eat it, tastes sour at first;

brh: خرن مس اودے کھٹک پارہ اوکا بسس اودے پسی مریک پسی بھرم کیک اودے کنیسہ اونا چنکو اوٹی گڈس بھی ارے گڈ ئنا تہٹی پین ملیس بھی بریک
en: when it is green they call it 'khatak', and after that, when it ripens, it becomes pissi. The pissi bears fruit and people eat it; it is small, it has a stone inside, and inside the stone there is also a kernel.
en_old: when it ripens they call it 'khatak'; after that it becomes pasi. The pasi bears fruit, people eat it; it is small, it also has a seed, and inside the seed there is also a kernel.

brh: پسی ئے کنگس اونا مطلب ہراکہ اونا رختے او پتی اوس بریک ہرا پت ئنا تہ چنکو ٹکر ئس کشاس او ڈنگر ٹی پاننگک ڈنگر ڈنگر ٹی بریک ہرا کہ اونا پائے پاٹ استعمال مریک اونا پاٹ سے بھاز ڈڈو اودے تفر ئٹ پرغنگا بھی دم دریفک بندغے جوانو تفرس تیزو
en: Take the pissi, I mean its tree: it has thorns. If you break off a small piece of its thorny part, it is called a 'dangar', a branch; it grows in branches. Its wood is used. Its wood is very hard; even chopping it with an axe wears a person out. A good, sharp axe,
en_old: If you take the pasi (wild jujube), meaning its tree, it has small branches that it puts out, and in the ground — it grows in the ground — its wood is used. Its wood is very hard; even chopping it with an axe wears a person out. A good, sharp axe,

en: if there is one, can chop it; otherwise, an ordinary axe can't chop it. It has very hard wood too; the pissi is like that as well. After that, after the pissi, comes the tola angoor ('jackal grape'), which is also a tree. Like the pissi, it also bears some kind of fruit. The tola angoor tree, well, isn't used for anything else apart from burning. The edible part of the tola angoor, that fruit,

en: can be eaten. It is small, even smaller than the pissi. Its edible part is, what, the fruit, and it is also a beautiful tree. After that, coming to the fruit trees: there is the apricot, there is the apple, and the ber pissi too, which is a bigger breed of pissi.
