en_old: can be eaten. It is even smaller than the small pasi. Its edible part is the fruit, and it is a beautiful tree too. After that come the fruits: apricot, apple, and ber pasi. The ber pasi is a bigger breed of pasi. The pasi is small, the bigger one is the ber pasi, and its stone is a big one. It is also generally found almost

brh: جاگہ غا مریک بیر پسی آ اوکا گیت مریک گیت اکثر دیری آ جاگہ غا لگیک اور بھاز زو دا ٹرکیک اونا پاٹ ئے نی گڈے چنکا چنکا پاٹ ئے تہ خلک او سمجھو او تینا موسم ٹی ہرا ٹائم موسم تہ بس نی داسہ دا داسہ بھی موسم تہ بسنے دا ٹائماتا داسہ داکا پدا باغبر بوغبر نا موسم بریک
en: place. After the ber pissi comes the geet. The geet mostly grows in watery places and sprouts very quickly. If you cut its wood, cut it into small, small pieces and plant them, then, you see, it grows in its season, at the time when the season has come. Now, right now too, the season has come, these days. Now after this comes the spring season.
en_old: everywhere. After the ber pasi comes the geet (willow). Willow mostly grows in watery places and sprouts very quickly. You cut its wood into small pieces and plant them, you see, in its season, when the season comes. Right now the season has come too, these days. After this comes the spring season.

brh: داکا پدا داسہ نی خلنگ ئے شروع کریس تہ باغبر بوغبر آن پدا او تینٹ ٹرکینگ ئے شروع کیرہ پن کیرہ اوکا پدا روتہ خلیرہ او بھلن مریرہ بھاز
en: After this, if you start planting now, then after spring they start sprouting by themselves. They put out leaves, then they put down roots, and they grow very big.
en_old: Then, if you start planting now, after spring they start sprouting by themselves. They put out leaves, then branches, and grow very big.

brh: موسم نا حسابٹ بھلن مرسا کیرہ کیرہ اوفک پدان ہخس گڈسا کریر تا پین برسا کیرہ ہخس گڈسا کریس تا ہر موسم اٹ برسا کیک زیادہ مرسا کیک گیت مرے گیت آن پدا ٹرالی مس اوکا پد توت اسہ میوہ سے توت بھی اونا بھئی بھاز قسم مریک اسٹ ئس تو اونا مرغنو دانس تہ مریک اسٹ نا گونڈوس مریک اسٹ نا ہنینو مریک
en: They keep growing big according to the season. However much they keep cutting them back, they keep coming back again; however much you keep cutting it, it keeps coming back every season and keeps increasing. That is the geet. After the geet, that is done; after that comes the mulberry, a fruit. The mulberry also has many kinds: one has a long berry, one's is short, and one's is sweet.
en_old: They grow according to the season. However much you cut them back, they keep coming again. However much you cut them, they come back every season and keep increasing. That was the willow. After the willow, then the mulberry, a fruit. The mulberry has many kinds too: one has long fruit, one has short, round fruit, and one is sweet.

brh: موننگا توت بریک پیہنا توت بریک اوفتا بھی بھاز قسماک اریر توتے بارفنگہ ہر موسم ٹی بہا بھی مریک مونا قسم تے بھی بھاز ہنین مریک پیہنا قسم تے بھی بھاز ہنین مریک اونا بھلو ڈرختس مریک اونا بھی ہشنگ کہ کاریم تیک اونا بھنڈ بھی کاریم تیک بھنڈ بھلو خلیک عمرے بھی زیادہ کیک
en: There are black mulberries and white mulberries, and they too come in many kinds. Mulberries are dried, and they also sell in every season. The black kinds are very sweet, and the white kinds are very sweet too. It grows into a big tree. It is also useful for burning, and its trunk is useful too; it grows a big trunk, and it lives long as well.
en_old: There are white mulberries and black mulberries, and they come in many kinds. Mulberries sell well every season. The white kinds are very sweet, and the black kinds are very sweet too. It's a big tree. It's used for firewood, and its shade is useful too: it gives a lot of shade, and it lives a long time.

brh: توتان علاوہ پین سوف بریک سوف اسٹ ئس چنکا بریک اسٹ ئس بھلا بریک ہراکہ سوراب قلات اوفتے ٹی بھلا سوف اکثر بھاز مریک دا ننا ایریا ٹی دا ننا دا جہلاوان دا ئے انتاکو جاگہ غاکو دا پاسوئے داڑے کنا کنا خیال پائک کہ داڑے چنکا سوف مریک بھلا سوف داڑے ردینگ
en: Besides the mulberry there is also the apple. One kind of apple is small and one kind is big. In Surab and Kalat the big apples are mostly plentiful. Here in our area, our Jhalawan, these, what, places, these parts here, I think small apples grow here; big apples don't
en_old: Besides the mulberry there are apples. One kind is small and one kind is big. In Surab and Kalat big apples are mostly plentiful. Here in our area, Jhalawan, in these places around here, I think small apples grow. Big apples don't grow here.

brh: کپک اودے موسمک الیپسہ ردینگ گڑا چنکا سوف داڑے ردینگ کیک کننگ مریک اوکا علاوہ انجیر بھی مریک انجیر نا ڈرخت مریک او انجیر نا تو او بھی ہندنو ڈرخت سے اونا پن ئسے بھاز بھلو درخت تہ خو چنکوس مریک چنکی آن او شروع کیک بھرم کننگ اے پھل ئے تہ کس خنتنے ہندا گڑا نا پاریکہ اینو انجیر نا پھل ئے کس خنتنے
en: grow here; the climate doesn't let them grow. So the small apples can grow here and can be eaten. Besides that there is also the fig; there is the fig tree, and the fig is also that kind of tree. Its leaves are very big, but the tree is fairly small. It starts bearing fruit while it is small. As for its flower, nobody has seen it; that is why they say that to this day nobody has seen the fig's flower.
en_old: The climate doesn't let them grow, so small apples grow here and can be eaten. Besides that there's the fig. There's the fig tree, and it's that kind of tree too. Its leaves are big, and the tree is fairly small. It starts bearing fruit while it's young. Nobody has ever seen its flower. That's why it's said that to this day nobody has seen the fig's flower.

brh: بقایا ڈرخت ارے اونا ڈرخت ئس بھی اونا سورو ہندنو پاٹ سے اوخسان سرفنگان پنیک او بھی بھلو ڈرخت ئس کیک اور اونا ہراکہ پن سے پن تہ بھاز پرا مریک بھلن مریک
en: Otherwise, there is its tree. Its tree also has that kind of reddish wood; it grows from just that much shaking (?). It also becomes a big tree, and its leaves are very broad and big.
en_old: Then there's its tree. It also has reddish wood, it sprouts from a planted cutting, it becomes a big tree, and its leaves are very wide and large.

brh: انجیران پدا ؤ انجیر مس انجیران پدا پین سنجت بریک سنجت ارے او بھی میوہ سے سنجت ولا اونا بھیا سورو پاٹ سے بھاز سنجت ئے خلکس تہ مدان مدان ردیک لیکن اونا بھرم سے بھاز زیباؤ اونا اشکنو ہندنو دا پھینڈی نا دا کچوس چنکوس مریک انچ ئنا کچ مریک اونا
en: After the fig (so that was the fig), after the fig comes the sanjat (oleaster). There is the sanjat; it is also a fruit. The sanjat, well, also has reddish wood. If you plant the sanjat, it grows very slowly, but its fruit is very beautiful. It is slender, about the size of this finger, small; it is about an inch in size.
en_old: After the fig, so that was the fig, after the fig comes the sanjad (oleaster). It is a fruit too. The oleaster has reddish wood. If you plant oleaster it grows very slowly, but its fruit is very beautiful. It's small, about the size of this finger, about an inch.

brh: بھرم اور اول ٹی مریک خرم مریک پوشکن اوکا پدا خیسن مریک او بھی ہنین مریک بھاز رخت ئس تہ بڑزو بریک لیکن پن تہ بھی ہمون چنک اے اور بھرم تہ بھی بھاز چنک اے اور ہرا ٹائما دانا پھل مریک شامیکا دانا اگہ چنکو چرکس چھکا دانا پھل ئنا خوشبوس بھی بھاز گچینو بریک دا مس سنجت سنجت
en: The fruit is green at first, then yellow, and after that it turns red, and it is also sweet. The tree grows very tall, but its leaves are small too, and its fruit is very small as well. And when it flowers, in the evening, if even a slight breeze blows, the scent of its flowers is very lovely. That is the sanjat, the sanjat.
en_old: Its fruit is green at first, when it's new, then it turns yellow, and it's sweet too. The tree grows tall, but its leaves are small and its fruit is very small too. When it flowers, in the evening, if there's even a slight breeze, its flowers have a lovely fragrance. That was the oleaster.

brh: آن پدا برینہ دا ایلو اسہ ڈرختس ارے پھکاڑو دا تو پھکاڑو بھرم کیک کنوکس اف میوہ ئس افک ڈرخت سے پھکاڑو پارہ تہ داٹی دا ولا دانا بھی سورو پاٹ سے بھاز دادے خلکس زو بھلن مریک اور سیخاس گچینو بھاز کیک بھلن بھی مریک سیخاس دانا بھرم مسک دانا بھرم
en: After that we come to another tree, the phakaro. The phakaro bears fruit, but it isn't edible; it is not a fruit tree, it is a tree they call phakaro. It too, well, has reddish wood. If you plant it, it grows big quickly, and it gives very good shade; it grows big too, giving shade. Its fruit... its fruit
en_old: After the oleaster we come to another tree, the phakaro. It bears fruit, but the fruit isn't edible. It isn't a fruit tree; it's a tree called phakaro. It also has reddish wood. If you plant it, it grows quickly, makes very good sticks, and grows big too. Its fruit...

brh: نا ہرا غلہ غاک تہ اریر دا بھاز زررہ بھاز بھرم کیک زررہ بھی بھاز ہندا بھرماک گڑا دا صرف ہشنگ کہ کاریم تیک یا سیخا کہ بقایا پین کنا سوچ پائے کنا خیال پائے کہ پین ہچ کاریم ناس اف کہ داڑان کوئی دروازس جوڑ مرے داڑے کوئی شوکیس ئسے نا کاریمس ہلیر الماری سے نا پاٹ سے نا یا پلک سے نا
en: the seeds it has drop in large numbers; it bears a lot of fruit, and these fruits also drop a lot. So it is only useful for burning or for shade. Otherwise, to my mind, I think it has no other use, such as making a door from it, or using it for a showcase, or as wood for a cupboard, or for a bed.
en_old: the seeds it has fall in large numbers. It bears a lot of fruit and drops a lot of fruit. So it's only used for firewood or for sticks. Other than that, I think it has no use. You can't make a door out of it, or a showcase, or wood for a cupboard, or a bed.

brh: دہنو کنا خیال پائے دا کاریم چوف بقایا ایلو اسہ ڈرخت ئس ارے آرغ آرغ بریک او بھی اسہ قسم ئنا ڈرخت سے او بھی ہشنگ کہ کاریم تیک
en: That kind; I think it is of no use for this kind of work. Then there is another tree, the argh; the argh comes next. It is also a kind of tree, and it too is used for burning.
en_old: I think it's of no use for that kind of work. Then there's another tree, the argh. It's another kind of tree, and it's also used for firewood.

brh: اونا پن سے بھلو اوٹی پال بھی مریک اونا وری بھرم اسہ پین قسم ئنا وڑناس مریک ہندنو ہراکہ استان باروس مریک است نا شکل ٹی اونا بھرم مریک اونا بھرمے ہراٹائم بھرم کرے اودے ملاس تہ اونا تہٹی اسہ پین قسم ئنا بج ئس بریک ولا بجاک خلوکو ہندن زیبا زیبا اور ہراکہ اونا پال ئس بریک یا اونا ہراکہ دیرس بریک او کننگا
en: Its leaf is big, and it also has milky sap in it. Its fruit has a different kind of shape, like a heart: its fruit is heart-shaped. When it fruits and you break its fruit open, inside there is a different kind of seed, and the seeds are set so beautifully. And its milk, or the liquid that comes out of it, is, to eat,
en_old: Its leaves are big, and it has milky sap too. Its fruit has a different kind of shape, like a heart; its fruit is heart-shaped. When it fruits and you break the fruit open, inside there's a different kind of seed, beautifully arranged. And its milk, or its liquid, is harmful to eat.

brh: نقصاندہ اے بھاز نقصان نسخان تیک نے ہرا ٹائما دانا نی ہمو بھرم ئے یا دانا پن ئس کنگس یا دانا لٹ آتان ہرا پال تان کنگس یا اکثر دشمن داری ٹی مسنے دا میل تا کس سے نا ہنانو فصل ئے کنگنو میلک بھاز اودے کلکان کرینو اودے بھاز تنگ کرینو تو گڑا ا بندغ اکثر ننا
en: harmful; it does you a lot of harm and damage if you eat its fruit, or its leaves, or the milk from its stems. Or often it has happened in feuds: these livestock, someone's livestock went and ate someone else's crop and harassed him a lot, troubled him a lot, so then that man, often in our
en_old: It's very harmful to you. If you eat its fruit or its leaves, or the milk from its stems... Often, in feuds, when someone's livestock had eaten someone else's crops and harassed him a lot, that person in our

brh: سرغا تو اوٹی بروک لازم بریک اودے گڑا ہندا داسہ تو داک بھاز کم رہینگانو داسہ دافتے اینو پھگہ بس ہندا الماریک دافتے چٹفینو مست تو ہندا اسرہ اوفتے ٹی زیبائی ہمو اسکہ اوفتے ٹی ہمونا خوبصورتیک اسرکہ پڑچ ئنا گدان بریک پڑچ ئنائے منہ پارہ نہ پڑچ ئنا منہ بریک گدان پارہ پڑچ پارہ تہ
en: On top, in it, there is always the bedding stack (bruk). Now these have become very rare; nowadays the wardrobes have done away with them. In the past it was just these: the beauty was in them, their loveliness was in them. Then there is the mat tent: it is made of mats, and they call it a 'manna' (shelter), you see. There is the mat shelter; they call it a tent, they call it mat.
en_old: In it the bedding is always there. Very few of these are left now; today wardrobes have replaced them. In the past, that was where the beauty was. There was also the dwarf-palm hut. They call it the 'manh' of dwarf palm rather than a tent; they say dwarf palm…

brh: بشی پارہ ولدا مختلف اسہ قسم ئنا مریرہ
en: They call it bashi; and again, they come in different kinds.
en_old: They call it 'bashi', and there are various kinds of it.

brh: ہراکہ واپس شام ئنا ہراکہ کھریئا کائک تینا کھرے دیک مش آ خوافے ہراکہ دیر تس تہ گڑا او کبھی ہندنو مریک وانڈی کیک تینا کھرے وانڈی ہمودے کہ اسہ جاگہ اے ایریا کہ دا ایریا کہ اے ایریا ٹی دا جاگہ ٹی ڈکال مریک ہچ مفک بئے مفک پر مفک داڑے ڈکال
en: The one who comes back in the evening: the shepherd goes, takes his flock and grazes it on the mountain, and when he has watered them, then sometimes it happens like this: he takes his flock out on a vandi (a grazing camp away from home). Vandi is when in one place, that area, this area, in that area, in this place there is a drought: there is nothing, no grass, no rain. Here there is drought.
en_old: In the evening he comes back home, to his house in the mountains, and sleeps. When it rains, it sometimes happens that he moves his house. That happens when there is drought in one place or area: there is no grass, no wheat, no rain. There is drought here.

brh: مریک او دافتے ٹی مال تے کہ ہچس خنپک تو ہرک کہ مال کنا لنگڑی آن کہیرہ گڑا بنک بھئی فلان جاگہ غا آبادی مسنے مش تے ٹی خرسی ارے ہنداکا دریکہ تینا مالے ہمیڑے گڑا مش تے ٹی وانڈی کریکہ تینکہ گڑا ہنداکا برنچ مچہ ہرفیکہ انت دریکہ گڑا اونا خاسن گڑا ہموکا خاص ہمو
en: (Drought) happens, and among these, the livestock: when he sees there is nothing, so when he sees that the livestock are dying of hunger, then he hears, 'Well, at such-and-such place there has been greenery; there is green grass in the mountains.' He would take his livestock right there, to that very place, and then he would camp out (vandi) in the mountains for himself. Then right there he would carry a little rice, whatever he took along, then his buttermilk, then right there, especially that...
en_old: Maybe in these, for the livestock that see nothing, whoever's livestock went away from my flock, then they would say, well, in such-and-such place there has been cultivation, there is greenery in the mountains, he would take his livestock right there, then he would graze them in the mountains for himself, then right there he would gather rice, whatever he took, then his food, then that particular one.

brh: میل تان گڑا گڑا اوٹی تو ئس وانڈی ٹی لگاکہ تہ کبھی کس سے دہ دے لگاکہ کبھی بیس دے مش سے نا ہناکہ ہمے ٹوٹ آ گڑا میلک ہموڑے دشت ئنا مش تا زیہا دشت مریک پٹ ہندنو مریک پڑ میدان مریک گڑا دریکہ دا ہموڑے تینا خاخر لگفیکہ تینا میل تے ہموڑے ہیٹک اسرہ گڑا
en: ...of the sheep. Then, then on the vandi it would sometimes take him a month; sometimes it would take someone ten days, sometimes twenty days. He would go to a mountain, to that same spot, and then the sheep there: on the dasht above the mountains, there is a plain, it is flat ground like that, it is an open field. Then he would take them there, light his fire there, and keep his sheep there; there were goats too.
en_old: Then with the sheep, in grazing it took a while, sometimes it took someone ten days, sometimes twenty days, he went to a mountain, then on that slope the sheep, there over the plain of the desert, there is a flat area like that, a field, then he would take them there and set up his camp, his sheep and goats were there.

brh: سانبسا سانبسا ہندنو مسکہ اوڑے ہینسرہ ہیٹک دغرے ہیسرکہ اوفتے اڑفیکہ اوفتے پژ تسکہ اوفتے ٹی ہمو ہراکہ تینا لمہ ئے چائک میل تے تو اوار کریکہ تہ تینا لمہ تو یا ہیٹس مسکہ اوفتے پژ تسکہ گڑا اوفتے ہندا حسابٹ دغر تے بھلن کرسا اڑفسا اڑفسا گڑا
en: Tending them, tending them, it would go like this: there they would give birth; the goats would give birth to kids. They would make them suckle, they would put them to the teat (?). Among them, the one that knows its mother, they would put it together with the sheep, with its own mother; or if it was a goat, they would put them to the teat. Then in that same way they raised the kids, making them suckle, making them suckle, then...
en_old: In spring, spring, it would be like that, they would bring the kids there, they would separate the lambs and feed them, they would give them to suckle, among them, the one who knew its mother among the sheep, they would put it together with its own mother, or with a goat, they would let them suckle, then in that same way they would raise the lambs, separating and separating them, then.

brh: ہراکہ آبادی نا ٹائم ئس مسکہ وختس مسکہ او تینا آبادی نا وخت اسکا اوفتے ہموڑے توریکہ وانڈی کریکہ
en: Whatever the green season was, whatever period it was, until his green season was over he would keep them there and graze them on the vandi.
en_old: Whatever the time of cultivation was, when it was, until their time of cultivation they would keep them there and graze them.

brh: گڑا اکثر دیر ئنا تو کمی مسکہ گڑا او امر کریکہ ہندا میل تا پال تے بیڑاکہ ہیٹ ئنا پال ئنا ہموفتے ٹی برنجے کریکہ دانا جوانو پنس بریک کنا ذہنا بفک بھاز گچینو دانا ذائقس مریک ہمو ہراکہ وری اودے ہمر کیک کرے تہ انت
en: Then water was often short, so what would he do? He would milk these same sheep, the goat's milk, and put rice in it. There is a good name for this, it doesn't come to my mind. It has a very fine taste. The way he makes it, how does he make it, what was it...
en_old: Then often there was a shortage of water, so what he would do was milk these same sheep, the goat's milk, and cook the rice in it; there's a good name for this, it doesn't come to my mind, it has a very fine taste, the one who eats it, what would he do then.

brh: پلیٹ تو اوڑتو مفک تالی وٹی مفک او ٹائما تا بھڈ کننگ کپک یا مفک گڑا ہمر کریکہ ہندا برنج نا ہراکہ بے دیرےبرنجے ہندا ڈال ئے انت کریکہ پال تے ٹی ارغے کریکہ اوکا پدا خلاساکہ کنگکہ تا خلاسسا کننگ ناتا ولدا پین مزہ ئس بریک گڑا اوکا اٹ وخت
en: There were no plates with them, no trays; at that time they could not make pots, or there were none. So what would he do with this rice, the rice without water, this sweet dish? He would put bread into the milk; after that he would chew it and eat it, and eating it while chewing has yet another taste. Then at that time...
en_old: There were no plates with them, nor any dishes, they didn't have pots at that time, or there weren't any, then what he would do was take the rice without water, and the dal, he would put them into the milk, after that he would cook it, eat it, and when eating it there's another flavour to it, then at that time.

brh: مسکہ وانڈی آن پد یا وانڈی متوکہ او شام ئنا واپس مسکہ گڑا داڑے گودی توارے بنگکہ چڑینگاتا کہ کھر بننگ ٹی اے گڑااو ہنداکا اسیکا زہ ئے ملتوکہ ہخسو تینکہ بیڑارکہ تینا شام ئنا چاء ئکہ یا تینا خاسن کے یا تینا ملفنگ کے یا تینا پورنگ کہ بیڑارکہ تینکہ ہڑسارہ اوکا پدا یلہ کریرہ
en: ...would happen. After the vandi, or if there was no vandi, he would come back in the evening. Then here the lady of the house would hear the sound of them calling, that the flock was coming in. Then right there they would not let the kids out at once; they would milk as much as they needed for themselves: for their evening tea, or for their buttermilk, or for their [unclear], or for their churning. They would milk for themselves and hold the kids back, and after that they would let them go.
en_old: After grazing, or if there was no grazing, he would come back in the evening, then here a voice would come from the herd, from the bleating, that they are coming into the pen, then right there he wouldn't release the kids at once, so much for himself, he would milk for his evening tea, or for his food, or for his churning, or for his curd, he would milk for himself, after that they would release them.

brh: زہ ئے گڑا زہ ئے گڑا زہ ئس کبھی بیست خوڑدہ نا مسکہ یا کبھی سی ئنا مسکہ زہ یلہ کریرکہ ہناکہ اوکا گڑا بسرہ ہر کس تینا زہ ہناکہ تینا چاہسکہ لمہ ئے اڑاکہ اوکا پدا گڑا دا تینا شام ئنا ہمو خاسن نا اسہ وار خاسن کیرہ تا چاء ئنا اسر چاء کریرہ تا گڑا کبھی کس ئتو چاء متوکہ گڑ شاغارکہ تا بورہ
en: The kids, then the kids: sometimes a flock of kids would be twenty lambs, or sometimes thirty. They would let the kids go and they would go off; then they came, and each one's kid would go, recognise its mother and suckle. After that they would have their evening buttermilk once, and those who had tea would make tea. Then sometimes someone had no tea, they would put in jaggery, their sugar...
en_old: The kids, then the kids, sometimes there were twenty-five or thirty kids, they would release the kids, they would go, then each one would come, each kid would go and find its own mother, then after that they would have their evening food once, have tea at their tea time, then sometimes if someone had no tea, they would put in jaggery, their sugar.

brh: نا بورہ متوکہ گڑ شاغارہ پن اوفتا ہندا اسرہ پین تو بھلو الوکہ
en: ...if there was no sugar, they would put in jaggery. Those were their names (for these things); there was nothing much else.
en_old: If there was no sugar, they would put jaggery; their names were like that, there was nothing else big.

brh: زہ آن پدا گڑا او تینا ہرا خاسن نا اسرکہ ہراکہ خسیک اسرکہ ہراکہ پورنگ اسرکہ مدر کہ ؤ خسی خسی آن خاسن آن مدر مریک دا تو گڑاس ہیت مسک دافتا زیہا او ہیت ہیت کننگ است خواہک ہیت کیوہ دافتا زیہا اوکا پدا ولدانا اوفتا ڈیلی نا ہر دے ئنا ہنا
en: After the kids, then his dairy things that there were: what was butter, what was churning, the madar and the butter. From butter, from buttermilk, madar is made. These were some things; my heart wants to talk about them, and I will talk about them. After that, again, their daily, every day's...
en_old: After the kids, then whatever food of his there was, whatever was butter, whatever was curd, the buttermilk, and butter, from butter and food, the buttermilk is made; these were some things that happened, about these I want to talk, I will talk about them, after that, again, their daily, every day's...

brh: مسرکہ کہ تینا زہ ئے ہمو حسابٹ یلہ کننگ ہمو حسابٹ اوفتے اڑفنگ ہمو حسابٹ تخنگ دافتے ٹی میل تے ٹی کہ ہر وڑ ئنا بسکہ بیماری بیماری چالڑی بننگ کیک دافتے ٹی ریخنگ مننگ کیک پیہی بننگ کیک بھاز
en: ...would happen: letting their kids out in that way, making them suckle in that way, keeping them in that way. Among these, among the sheep, every kind of disease would come. Disease: chalri can come, there can be shedding (?) among them, and a lot of pehi (unclear) can come.
en_old: It happened that releasing their kids in that way, separating them in that way, keeping them in that way, among these sheep, that all kinds of disease came, disease, scabies can come, among them there can be shedding, lice can come, a lot.

brh: وڑ ئنا میل تے ٹی بیماری بریک چالڑی ہندنوس مسکہ او ہلککہ ہرا ٹائم تہ اسہ کھرے اسہ ہیٹ ئے ہلککہ اوڑان گڑا کلے ہیٹ تے ہلککہ گڑا بندغاک دافتے بہا کریرکہ یا دافتے اسہ کھرے ہرا کہ چائس بھئی اینو دا خلق ٹی بسنے چالڑی ہیٹ تا میل تا گڑا دافتے ایلوفک تینافتے نرفیرہ دافتے کہ ہراٹائم دافتے تڑیرکہ اوفتا
en: ...all kinds of disease come among the sheep. There was something like chalri, and it would catch them: whenever it caught one flock, one goat, from it it would then catch all the goats. Then people would sell them. Or a flock that people knew about ('well, today this has come into this camp, chalri of the goats and sheep'): then the others would drive their own away from these, so that whenever they slaughtered these, their...
en_old: Kinds of disease come among the sheep, scabies and the like, it would catch, at what time it would catch a pen, a goat, from that it would then catch all the goats, then people would sell them, or a pen, which they knew, well, today this has come among the people, scabies of the goats and sheep, then the others would keep theirs away from them, that whenever they died, their...

brh: سوتے بی خستوسکہ کہ میل سے پین گند برو اودے بھی ہندا چالڑی ہلو گڑا ہندا وجہ غان دافتے ہراتم تھڑیرہ تا یا کھڈ کریرہ تا بھازی آن اسٹ تو کھڈ کریرہ تا کھڈ کتوسہ دافتے بسیرہ کنگرہ تاکہ بھئی دافتا گند یا دافتا ہڈ ئنا گند ایلو میل تے لگپ کہ ایفتے چالڑی ہلو داگڑا نا بھاز خوف مسکہ یا وختس ڈکال مسکہ دا میل کھسکرہ ڈکال آن دافک
en: ...they would not throw out the remains (?), so that the smell would not reach another sheep and it too catch the same chalri. For that reason, whenever they slaughtered them, they would bury them; mostly they would bury them. If they had not buried them, they would cook them and eat them, so that their smell, or the smell of their bones, would not reach the other sheep and these catch chalri. There was great fear of this. Or at times there was a drought and these sheep would die; from the drought these...
en_old: They didn't burn them, so that the smell wouldn't go to another sheep and that one catch the same scabies too; for that reason, whenever they died, either they would bury them, mostly they would bury them, if not buried they would burn them so that their smell or the smell of their bones wouldn't reach the other sheep and these catch scabies; there was great fear of this, or when there was drought these sheep would die, from drought these...

brh: بھاز بیماری ہلککہ تا گڑا ہراکہ دا بریک آبادی یاد مسکہ آبادی ہتم مسکہ ہتم بھاز زیادہ مسکہ ہتم کننگ آن گڑا دافک
en: A lot of disease would catch them. Then, when it comes, the green season, I remember: when there was greenery it was spring, and the spring was very abundant. From spending the spring, then these...
en_old: Many diseases would catch them, then when it comes, cultivation was remembered, cultivation, there was dry fodder, there was a great deal of fodder, from making fodder, then these...

brh: پدام ہلکرہ ٹخارکہ آبادی تے ٹی دا ولدا ہتم ہتم تو پیٹرک بریک خورومب بریک پیملک ٹرکیک پین قسم ئنا بھاز دہنو بریرہ ہرا مشیئا مش ئنا پلاک بریرہ مطلب میوہ غاک بریرہ اوفتے ٹی پیٹرک بریک خورومب بریک پیملک بریک
en: ...they would swell up and fatten in the green pastures. Then again, spring: in spring the petrak comes, the khorumb comes, the pimalak sprouts (?), and many other kinds like this come, which are the mountain's, the mountain's fruits. I mean fruits come; among them the petrak comes, the khorumb comes, the pimalak comes.
en_old: Later they would catch and fatten them in the cultivated lands, again fodder, fodder, wild fruits come, khorumb comes, wild onion sprouts, many other kinds like that come, which are fruits of the mountain, meaning fruits come, among them wild berries come, khorumb comes, wild onion comes.

brh: پیملک پیمازان بارو چنکو سے او بھی بھاز گچینوس مریک ہندنو مزئیوس مریک او بھی بریک ہندا مش تے ٹی مریک آغوت بریک باہوشنک بریک گربست بریک گربست تو بوڑ مریک
en: The pimalak is a bit smaller than an onion; it is very good too, it is tasty like that. It too comes; it grows in these same mountains. The aghut comes, the bahoshank comes, the garbast comes; as for the garbast, it is a 'bor' (unclear).
en_old: Wild onion, smaller than an onion, that too is very fine, it is tasty like that, that too comes, in these same mountains there are, wild mushrooms come, bahoshank comes, wild pistachio comes, wild pistachio is a tree.

brh: داسہ ای گڑاس زبان تا زیہا ہیت کیوہ ہراکہ تینا علاقہ تے ٹی ہرافتے ننے زبان تے کہ ہیت کیرہ زبانٹ تینا ہندن کہ ننا بلوچستان ٹی ننا جہلاوان بیلٹ بریک ساروان بیلٹ بریک ہر جاگہ غا براہوئی نا بندغ ملیک ننے دا ٹائما خضدار ٹی براہوئی تقریبا اکثریت براہوئی نائے خضداران ہلیس مونی
en: Now I will talk a little about languages, the languages that people speak in their own regions, in their own language. For example, in our Balochistan there is our Jhalawan belt and the Sarawan belt; everywhere we find Brahui people. At present in Khuzdar, Brahui is roughly the majority; it belongs to Brahui. Going on from Khuzdar...
en_old: Now I'll talk a little about languages, which in their regions, the languages that we speak, in our own language, like in our Balochistan there comes our Jhalawan belt, there comes the Sarawan belt, everywhere Brahui people are found; at this time in Khuzdar Brahui is roughly the majority, Brahui; going on from Khuzdar...

brh: وڈھ وڈھ آن بیلہ تو ظاہرے کم بریک خیر اوڑے بیلہ تا لاسی تا زبان بریک لاسی اٹ ہیت کیرہ نی واپس بڑزائی بریسہ بڑزائی ہراکہ سوراب او بھی براہوئی اٹے اوکان مستی قلات کوئٹہ غا کاسہ اوڑے تو زبانک مکس مریرہ اوڑے پشتون بریک
en: Wadh; from Wadh to Bela it obviously becomes less. Anyway, there in Bela it is the Lasis' language; they speak Lasi. If you come back up north, up north there is Surab, and that too is Brahui. Beyond that, when you go to Kalat and Quetta, the languages there are mixed; there Pashtun comes in.
en_old: Wadh, from Wadh to Bela of course it comes less; anyway, there in Bela the language of the Lasis comes, they speak Lasi; you come back up, up there, Surab, that too is Brahui; beyond that, as you go to Kalat and Quetta, there the languages are mixed, there Pashtun comes.

brh: پٹھانی یکہ بریک افغانی مختلف اوفتا بھی زبان تے ٹی فرق امر کہ اکثر نیمہ براہوئی ہیت کیرہ نیمہ پٹھانی ہیت کیرہ اور اوکا پدا ننا کہ آواران بیلٹ اے او ایریا تے ٹی تقریبا او جاگہ غاک اوڑے تو بلوچی ٹی ہیت مریک خاران مرے آواران مرے تربت مرے گوادر
en: Pathani, that is Afghani, comes in, and there are differences in their languages too, since mostly they speak half Brahui and half Pathani. And after that there is our Awaran belt: in those areas, roughly those places, people speak Balochi there, be it Kharan, Awaran, Turbat or Gwadar.
en_old: Pathani, one comes, Afghani, different ones, there are also differences in their languages, because mostly they speak half Brahui and half Pathani, and after that our Awaran belt, in those areas, roughly those places, there they speak in Balochi, be it Kharan, Awaran, Turbat, Gwadar.

brh: مرے داڑے زیاتر کنا خیال پائک بلوچی ٹی ہیت مریک ہندن کہ اوکا پدا بریسہ صوبہ سندھ ئنا زیہا صوبہ سندھ ٹی سندھی زبان مریک اوٹی باگڑی زبان مریک اوٹی گڑاس تھر ئنا سیڈا بریک اوفتا تینا زبانس مریک گڑاس بگٹی تا بریرہ بگٹی نا یکہ او زبانس مریک مری نا یکہ او زبانس مریک
en: Here, mostly, I think, Balochi is spoken. Likewise, after that you come to Sindh province: in Sindh province there is the Sindhi language, and in it there is the Bagri language. On the Thar side some people come who have their own language. Some Bugtis come; the Bugtis have a separate language, and the Marris have a separate language.
en_old: Be it, here mostly, I think, Balochi is spoken, and likewise after that you come to Sindh province; in Sindh province there is the Sindhi language, there is the Bagri language in it, in it some people of Thar come, they have their own language, some Bugtis come, the Bugtis have their own language, the Marris have their own language.

brh: اوفتا گڑاس ہراکہ دا سیڈا ولا بریسہ بگٹی سیڈا مری سیڈا اوفتا تینا زبان سے بگٹی اٹ مریک زبان اوفتا
en: Some of theirs, which on this side, again, as you come to the Bugti side and the Marri side, they have their own language: it is in Bugti, their language.
en_old: Some of theirs, like this, then coming to the Bugti, and likewise the Marri; likewise they have their own language in Bugti, their language.

brh: بھاز فرق زبان تے ٹی ارے تقریبا فرق ارے ٹی تا تو ہندن اوکا پدا بریسہ اردو تو ایہن ہر جاگہ غا مریک مادری زبانے پاکستان نا اردو نا تو ہر جاگہ غا ہیت مریک کسس ہر بندغ اردو ئے تقریبا ہیت کننگ کیک اردو اٹ تو زیاتر کنا خیال پائک کہ پنجاب سیڈا کاسہ اوڑے پنجابی
en: There is a lot of difference among languages; there is roughly a difference in them. So likewise, after that you come to Urdu: Urdu is like this, it is everywhere; it is Pakistan's mother tongue. Urdu is spoken everywhere; anyone, every person, can more or less speak Urdu. In Urdu mostly, I think, if you go to the Punjab side, there Punjabi...
en_old: There is a lot of difference between languages, there is roughly a difference. So after that, coming to Urdu, it's used everywhere; it's the mother tongue of Pakistan. Urdu is spoken everywhere; almost every person can speak Urdu. In Urdu mostly, in my view, likewise Punjab, there Punjabi...

brh: ارےپنجاب نا پنجابی زبان اٹ او اردو ٹی بھی ہیت کننگ کیرہ اور پنجابی اوفتا زبانے تینا مادری زبانے تا ہندن کہ اوڑے سرائیکی بھی بریک سرائیکی نا بھی تینا ہموفتا مادری زبانے او بھی تینا زبان نا بھاز خیالداری ئے کیرہ تینا زبان ٹی ہیت کیرہ ہندن کہ اوکا پدا بریک فارسی آن پدا بھاز زباناک اریر ہندن کہ
en: ...is there, the Punjabi language of Punjab: they speak in it, and they can also speak in Urdu. And Punjabi is their language, their own mother tongue. Likewise, Saraiki also comes in there; Saraiki too is their own mother tongue. They also take great care of their language and speak in their own language. Likewise, after that comes Persian; after Persian there are many languages, like...
en_old: There is the Punjabi language of Punjab; they can also speak in Urdu, and Punjabi is their language, their own mother tongue. Likewise Saraiki also comes there; Saraiki is also their own mother tongue. They also take great care of their language and speak in their own language. Likewise after that comes Persian; after Persian there are many languages, like...

brh: ایرانا کاسہ ایران ٹی فارسی بریک فارسی ٹی بھی بھلو اوفتا بھلو حد سے کا اوفتا جند نا زبانٹ ہیت مریک اوفتا پوران ایران ٹی فارسی ٹی ہیت مریک ہندن اوکا پدا عربی بریک عرب خلیج ملکاتے ٹی ہندن کہ اومان اے مسقط یا امارات تو پارہ امارات ٹی تو ہفت انت بریک
en: If you go to Iran, in Iran there is Persian. In Persian too, to a large extent, they speak in their own language; all over their Iran, Persian is spoken. Likewise, after that comes Arabic, in the Arab Gulf countries, such as Oman, that is Muscat, or the Emirates. They say in the Emirates there are seven what-d'you-call-them...
en_old: Iran's... in Iran there is Persian; in Persian too, to a great extent, they speak in their own language; all over Iran Persian is spoken. Likewise after that comes Arabic, in the Gulf Arab countries, like Oman, Muscat or the Emirates; they say in the Emirates there are seven, what are they called...

brh: ملک امارات ٹی امارات نا ہفت او اوٹی دبئی بریک ابو ظہبی بریک اوٹی مختلف مسقط بریک ہفت تقریبا شمال انت ٹی اوکا پدا خلیج ملکاتے ٹی سعودی بریک سعودی بھی عربی زبان ٹی اونا زبان عربی اے اوکاپدا قطر بریک بحرین بریک
en: ...countries in the Emirates: the seven of the Emirates, and among them Dubai comes, Abu Dhabi comes, various ones, Muscat comes; roughly seven are included in the what-d'you-call-it. After that, among the Gulf countries Saudi comes; Saudi too is in the Arabic language, its language is Arabic. After that Qatar comes, Bahrain comes,
en_old: countries: in the Emirates, the seven Emirates, and among them come Dubai, Abu Dhabi, various ones, Muscat comes, roughly seven in the north. After that among the Gulf countries comes Saudi Arabia; Saudi Arabia is also in the Arabic language, its language is Arabic. After that come Qatar and Bahrain,

brh: یمن بریک ہندن کہ اوکا پدا افریقہ بریک افریقہ نا افریقی زبانے تینا
en: Yemen comes. Likewise, after that Africa comes; Africa has its own African language.
en_old: and Yemen comes. Likewise after that comes Africa; Africa has its own African language.

brh: اور ہراکہ یونائیٹڈ اسٹیٹ ؤ ہراکہ ہراکہ یو کے بریک اونا تینا زبانے انگریزی ہراکہ یو اے ای بریک او تو مسک امارات یو ایس بریک اونا تینا زبانے انگلش اے اوکا پدا چائینیزے چائنیز نا یکہ او اسہ زبان سے او چینی اٹ ہیت کیرہ تینا زبانے او بھاز خیالے تینا
en: And the United States, and the UK: the UK comes, and its own language is English. The UAE comes, but that has been covered, the Emirates. The US comes; its own language is English. After that there is Chinese: Chinese is a separate language; they speak in Chinese, it is their own language, and they take a lot of care of their own...
en_old: And the United States and the UK come; their own language is English. The UAE comes, that's the Emirates; the US comes, its own language is English. After that is Chinese; Chinese is one language, they speak in Chinese, their own language, they take great care of their

brh: بسینہ تہ اودے کنگنکہ اوکا پدا ہرفیسہ بسنکہ داڑے تینا اراٹی باریمے بٹینکہ اچے درینہ تینا جاگہ غا تفینکہ اونا آخر مسکہ اونا آخر ٹی نن بئے ہیسنکہ شاغانہ بئیک مختلف قسم نا مریرہ اسہ مطلب ہر وخت ئنا اسہ تینا فصل ئس مریک مکئی نا ٹائم ٹی مسکہ مکئی ایسرکہ جواری نا ٹائم ٹی جواری اسکہ او متوکہ پھگ مسکہ
en: We would bake it and eat it. After that we would pick up and come back here to our house, drop the load, take the camel and tie it in its place. Then that would come to an end, and at the end of it we would bring seed and sow it. The seeds were of different kinds; I mean, each season has its own crop: in maize time it would be maize, they would bring maize; in sorghum time there was sorghum; and otherwise there would be straw.
en_old: We would bring it and eat it, and after that we'd pick up and come back here to our home, unload the load, take the camel and tie it in its place. Then at the end of it, at the end, we would bring seeds and sow them. The seeds were of different kinds, meaning every time had its own crop: in maize season there was maize, in sorghum season there was sorghum, and if not, there would be the grain heads.

brh: ہراکہ خولمے گوبٹ کیسہ پرغٹ مریک ہمیشہ اون ہراتم نی ڈرنزتیسہ اونا پھگ یکہ مریک اونا پرغٹ آن پدا اونا غلہ تہ یکہ پیشتنگک جوان نا
en: When you thresh the wheat there is always a re-threshing (pargat). When you winnow it, its chaff comes apart, and after the re-threshing its grain also comes out separately, nicely.
en_old: ...the ones you shake in a sieve, there is always chaff. When you thresh it, its grain heads get separated, and after the chaff its grain is taken out separately, nicely.

brh: او پھگ پچاکہ پھگے گڑا ہنانہ ہندن اچا ٹرنگڑ ٹی واپس شاغانہ تہ بغیر رختان اودے تخانہ اچ ئنا زیہارخت مسکہ تو ٹہتوکہ بغیر رختان گڑا جوان اودے پر کرینکہ تفینہ تہ مرغنو اسہ قسم سیٹ مسکہ وڑسیٹ ہراکہ باریم مسکہ اچ ئنا مرغنو وڑ ئسے اٹ مسکہ ڈرندو وارڈر اٹ تفینہ تہ دانگان اینگان گڑاس چا وخت پٹوس شاغانہ تہٹی تہ یا
en: The chaff that was left over, that chaff, we would then go and put back like that into the camel's carrying net (trangar). We put it on without the saddle: if there was a saddle on the camel's back it would not fit, so without the saddle we would fill it well and tie it. It would be a long kind, a sort of shape: whatever the load was, on the camel it took a long shape. We would tie it with a strong rope, and here and there we would sometimes put a sheet inside it, or
en_old: We would gather the grain heads, then we'd go and put them back like that in the camel's saddle frame. We'd put it on without a load; when there was a load on top of the camel it wouldn't fit, so without a load we'd fill it well and tie it, a kind of long set, a set, whatever the load was would be of a long kind on the camel. We'd tie it with a strong rope, and here and there we'd put some dried leaves inside, or...

brh: وختس پڑچس شاغانہ تہٹی تہ کہ پھگاک زرپس ایہان تہ تو گڑا اچا اودے باریم کرینہ ہیسنکہ ننا اسہ انت مسکہ کوم ئس مسکہ کوم نن مرغن مسکہ تہٹی کھڈ خلکنہ تہ تاکہ بھاز پھگ جاگہ ہلے ٹی تہ گڑا وختس کس ئنا بیس گوالہ مسکہ ملک ئس بیس گوالہ نا سمجھو بھلو جوہان ئس مسکہ اونا بھلو پھگ ئس مسکہ گڑا اشری
en: sometimes we would put a mat inside it so that the chaff would not spill out. Then we would load it onto the camel and bring it. We had a, what was it, a 'kom' (straw store). Our kom was long, and we would dig a pit inside it so that a lot of chaff would fit in it. Then sometimes someone's harvest would be twenty gwalas (grain sacks); say a landowner had a big threshing heap of twenty gwalas, then he would have a big pile of chaff. Then an ashri (communal work party)
en_old: Sometimes they would put the sheaves into the threshing floor so that the stalks would get dry, and then the donkeys would carry them and bring them. We had a, what was it, a pile; we would make a big pile and dig a hole in it so that lots of sheaves would fit in. Then sometimes someone's harvest was twenty sacks, a landowner's was twenty sacks; you could say it was a big threshing floor, and there would be a big pile of sheaves. Then the threshing

Here the threshing floor is a flat area, a level threshing ground, and it is clean too,

en: and in the heap, then, our people of the past, as we ourselves saw, would place a 'daz', a stone; they called it 'daz'. en: sacks go into it. They would measure it, and then they would start: they would look at the daz, so to speak. en: they would take out the zakat right there on the threshing heap; however much grain their heap had, they would take out (their share) right there. Then people from far away would come: someone coming from Sindh, someone coming from Gaj, the poor, crowds of very poor people. They would come and stay and wait, knowing that generous people would take out their zakat, and these people would take out their zakat.
en_old: that they would take out the zakat from that threshing floor; however much grain the threshing floor had, they would take out their share there. Then people coming from outside, someone coming from Sindh, someone coming from Gaj, the poor, crowds of poor people, they would come and stay and wait, watching for the generous people to take out their zakat, so that they could take their zakat.

brh: اوفتے گڑاسے پنچ من تسرہ پنچ من تسرہ گڑاسے دو من تسرہ گڑاسے سئے من چار من ہندن ہندن گڑا او تینا زکوۃ ئے کشسا کریرکہ
en: To some of them they would give five maunds, five maunds; to some two maunds, to some three maunds, four maunds, and so on. That is how they would go on taking out their zakat.
en_old: They would give some of them five maunds, five maunds, some two maunds, some three or four maunds, and so on, and that is how they would take out their zakat.

en: Then whatever of theirs they had measured, they would load onto the camels. On the good, strong camels they would load two tangs and put a gwala on top as well, and the weak camel that had no strength would get one tang, which they put on top. Then they would bring these

brh: کہ ایڑے اراٹی سر کرسا گڑا اوڑے گڑاس نا ہرا بندغ نا اللہ تسس تہ بھاز حیثیت اوفتے بھاز اوفتے غلہ بسکہ تو خرم ئس ختارک اوفک voice خرم ہمو گڑائے اوزمین ٹی اودے کھڈ مریک تقریبا بھلوس مریک اوٹی دہ گوالہ اوٹی یست گوالہ بریک خرم ہمودے اونا یام ٹی چنکو دکوس مریک
en: here to the house, delivering them. Then there, any person to whom God had given a lot of means, who got a lot of grain, would dig a kharam (grain pit). A kharam is that thing in the ground: it is a pit, fairly big; ten gwalas, twenty gwalas fit in it. The kharam has a small opening in its middle.
en_old: to here, to the house. And there, whichever person God had given much wealth, who got a lot of grain, they would dig a kharam (grain pit). A kharam is that thing in the ground, a pit, quite big; ten sacks fit in it, twenty sacks fit in it. The kharam has a small opening in its middle.

brh: ہمودے دکو آ نی دڑنگسہ اونا باآ خلس تفسہ مست ئنا تو ایمانداریئا وختاک اسرہ او ٹائما دزی نا ہچڑا خلیس الوکہ خرم ٹی شاغارہ غلہ غان پر کریرہ تہ خرم نا تہہ ئے ہشارکہ تاکہ غلہ غاک خراب مفس اوٹی کوئی خرئس بف بژونگ ئس بف ٹی تہ غلہ غاتے نقصان کپ ایلو سولک بف غلہ غاتے
en: You go down through that opening, then you put a stone on its mouth and close it. In the past the times were times of honesty; in those days there was no fear of theft at all. They would put it in the kharam and fill it with grain. They would burn the inside of the kharam so that the grain would not spoil, so that no bugs or insects would get into it and damage the grain, and no worms would get at the grain
en_old: Over that opening you would climb in and close its mouth. In the past, the times were of honesty; in those times there was no fear of theft. They would put the grain into the kharam and fill it, and they would line the bottom of the kharam so that the grain wouldn't go bad, so that no insects or ants would get in it to damage the grain, and no weevils would get into the grain

brh: نقصان گڑا اوفتے خرم ٹی شاغارکہ غلہ غاتے پر کریرہ تہ بائے تہ خل سے اٹ بند کریرکہ تفیرہ خل سے اٹ بائے تہ لچغ کریرکہ او اسکا او تینا اسہ ولا پین ہم بسکہ پڑچ ئنا جوڑارکہ اسہ پلی نن پلی پانہ تہ پڑچ ئنا جوڑارہ اودے ارانا مونا تخارہ تہ اودے اوٹی بھی گوالس ارٹ بسکہ اونا زی ئے کریرہ لچغ
en: and damage it. Then they would put them in the kharam, fill it with grain, and close and seal its lid with a stone; they would cover the lid with a stone and plaster it with mud. That was that. They also had another thing: they would make one out of matting, a 'pali', we call it a pali. They made it out of matting and placed it in front of the house; one or two gwalas would fit in it too. They would plaster its top with mud.
en_old: to damage it. Then they would put it in the kharam, fill it with grain, and close its mouth with a stone; they would seal its mouth with a stone and plaster it with mud. That was it. And then there was also another thing: they would make one out of mud, which we call a 'pali'; they made it of mud and placed it in front of the house, and one or two sacks would also fit in it. They would plaster its top.

brh: پلی ئے پر کریرہ خولم آن پر کریرہ تہ غلہ غان اودے لچغ کریرہ زی ئے تہ اونا گڑا کیرغان وختس یا جوڑارکہ ترتیب اس
en: They would fill the pali, fill it with wheat, with grain, and plaster its top with mud. Then sometimes they would make a 'kiraghan'; it was an arrangement of its own.
en_old: They would fill the pali, fill it with wheat, and plaster its top over the grain. Then sometimes they would make a kirghan, it was arranged like that.

brh: کیرغان کڑک ئس چنکو کریرہ تہ گڑا غلہ کشوئی مسکہ تا گڑا غلہ کٹفیرہ غلہ ئے گڑا ہموکا کڑک آن ملارہ کڑک ئے تہ غلہ غاک تمسا تمسا او تنگ ٹی ہخس شاغارہ تینا نکان کہ وختس یا گوالہ نسفیرہ غلہ نت کننگ کہ دریرکہ نسفنگ کہ وختسے آ ارا گوالہ وختسے آ نیم گوالس دریرکہ تو تینا کچ ئنا حسابا اوفک
en: In the kiraghan they would make a small hole, and then, when grain had to be taken out, they would draw out the grain: they would let the grain out through that hole. (They would open) the hole and the grain would keep falling into the sack, as much as they put in for their own needs. Sometimes they would grind a gwala; to make the grain into flour they would take it to grind, sometimes two gwalas, sometimes half a gwala, according to their own measure.
en_old: In the kirghan they would make a small hole, and then when grain was to be taken out, they would open it and take the grain out through that hole, and the grain would keep falling into the sack, as much as they put in for themselves. Sometimes they would grind a sack; to grind, to make flour, they would take some to grind, sometimes two sacks, sometimes half a sack, according to their own needs.

brh: تیکہ غلہ دریرکہ انتا چکی آ تو دا چکی آ بھی ہندنو اچ سے نا زیہا دریرہ تہ یا بیش ئنا زیہا دریرہ غلہ غاتے نسفنگ کہ اوکا توران والا تنگان ولا تورومسکہ تورو ہمود اسکہ پیہنو رنگ سے اٹ مسکہ او کنا خیال پائے کہ میل ئنا کھاس اٹ مسکہ میل ئنا کھاس اٹ مسکہ
en: When they took the grain, to what? to the mill, to the mill too they would carry it like that on a camel, or on a donkey, to grind the grain. Then, besides the sack, there was also the 'toro'. The toro was whitish in color, and I think it was made of sheep's wool, made of sheep's wool.
en_old: When they put the grain, on what millstone? On this millstone too they would put it on top of a stone, or on top of the spindle, to grind the grains. Then there was a sack with a strap. The sack was whitish in colour, and I think it was made of goat hair, made of goat hair.

brh: تورو ٹی نتاتے شاغارہ تورو ہمو گڑائے کہ اودے وس سے کا نہ بژونگ ئس نقصان تیک نسخان تننگ کیک نئے اودے سولک ئس نسخان تننگ کیک اور او بھلن مسکہ اور گڑا اودے ہرا ٹائما اچا دریرہ تخارہ داکا ہورک دریرہ تہ چکی آ ایکا غلہ غاک نت مسرکہ اوکا ولا شاغارہ تا تورہ ٹی تورہ ئے گڑا ہفیرہ امپیرہ اچ ئنا زیہا و
en: They would put the flour into the toro. The toro is a thing that bugs cannot harm, nothing can damage it, and worms cannot damage it either. And it was big. Then whenever they took it, they would put it on the camel; from here they would take it empty to the mill, there the grain would become flour, and then they would put it back into the toro. Then they would lift the toro and load it onto the camel, and
en_old: They would put the flour into the sack. The sack is the kind of thing that no rain can harm, and no damp or insects can harm it either, and it was big. Then whenever they put it on the stone, they would put the hand-stone on the millstone. When the grains had turned to flour, they would put it back into the sack, then take it and bring it and put it on top of the stone.

brh: تنگ ئے تخارہ اچ ئنا زیہا ایسرہ داڑے بٹیرہ تہ گڑا او ہراکہ ننا پانہ کہ نن تو راوتی پانہ راوتی پانہ تہ رواتی ٹی تخارہ انت تے تینا یا کوئی جوانو اسہ تینا گیڈ ئسیٹ تخارہ تاکہ ہمو ٹائم ہر وخت سے آ اوکان نن نت
en: they would put the sack on the camel, bring it, and set it down here. Then there was what we call, we call it a 'rawati'. They would keep their, what, in the rawati, or they would keep it in some good container of their own, so that at any time we could take flour from it
en_old: They would set the tray on top of the stone, bring it here and sit down. Then there was what we call, we call it a 'rawati'. They would keep it in a rawati, or in some good bag of their own, so that at any time we could take flour from it.

brh: کشن نت کشنگ کہ گڑا تال ئس مسکہ تال ئے کچ ئنا مطابق ہخس ہخسو خاندان ئس ہخسو اراٹی رہینگوکو لشکرس مسکہ اوفتا کچا گڑا نت کشارہ تال ٹی
en: and take it out. To take out flour there was a tray. According to the measure of the tray: however big a family was, however big the household living in the house was, they would take out flour into the tray according to their size.
en_old: To take out the flour there was a tray. It depended on the size of the tray: however big a family was, however big the household living in the house was, they would take out that much flour into the tray.

en: They would take the tray, and then the lady of the house would knead the flour. There was a fireplace, and in the fireplace they would set up the stove; on top of the stove was the tafu, the tafu that is made of stone. Then they would heat it with firewood, and then shape the breads: on it she would make small, small pieces from the tray, make them round, about this big, and after that
en_old: They would set out the tray and then knead the flour. The lady of the house had a hearth, and in the hearth they would set the fire-pit. On top of the fire-pit there was a griddle, the griddle that is made of stone. They would heat it with wood, then shape the breads: from the tray they would pinch off small pieces, make them about this round, and then after that…

brh: آن با ولدا اوفتے دو آ تینا خساکہ خساکہ او بھلن مسکہ ارغ نا شکل ٹی بسکہ اودے گڑا شاغاکہ تافو نا زیہا اودے بسسا بسسا تافو داسہ تو پاٹ ئنا کمی مسنے بھاز تافو آ ارغ کننگ بھاز مشکلےمالو نا تو ہراکہ مش تے ٹی پاٹک اسرکہ اچاتا زیہا بھی دا تافو ئے نن پجانکہ گڑا تافو نا زیہا ارغ مسکہ
en: again she would toss them on her hands, toss them, and it would get bigger and take the shape of bread. Then she would put it on the tafu and bake it, bake it. In the old days, when there was firewood in the mountains, we would also carry this tafu on the camels, and the bread was made on the tafu.
en_old: …they would spread them out again by hand, spread them, and they got bigger and took the shape of bread. Then they would put it on the griddle and bake it, bake it. Nowadays there is a shortage of wood, and it is very hard to make bread on a griddle. In the past, when there was wood in the mountains, we also knew this griddle set on top of stones, and the bread was made on the griddle.

Patkim is this: when you knead the flour, the flour is wet at that point, and when you pat it and roll it, obviously it sticks to your hand.

en: Likewise, kashum is one of the plants, or you could call it a tree; you can call it a tree. Camels also eat kashum when it is young. When it has grown big, it makes a fruit, which they call 'bhol'. When this kashum drops its flower, its fruit, then understand that it is that time: the time for Nari has come. So kashum also signals a season.
en_old: Kashim is like a plant, or you could call it a tree. Camels eat it too. When it grows big it bears a fruit, which they call a flower. When this kashim's flower or fruit bursts open, you know it's time to move down to Nari. So kashim also tells us a season is coming.

en: Besides that, there is the donkey. The donkey has various jobs. It also carries loads, but it can carry small ones and cannot carry big ones. One person leads it along like that. For the mats, you go with the donkey, and after that you put the palm leaves back onto the skewers. They call this a 'targhan pacho'.
en_old: Besides that, there is the spindle. The spindle has various tasks and it also carries a load, but it can carry a small one, not a big one. One person handles it like that. For the rope, they would cut the palm leaves and then put them on the skewer again; the palm leaves, they call it 'targhan pacho'.

Then on the spindle you can put two skewers, three skewers, four, depending on how strong the spindle was.

en: ...it was. Then they would come to their own place and sit down. There was a gathering, and there was tea, parched grain and dates.
en_old: Then they would come to their place and sit down. There was a gathering, and there was tea and roasted grain there, the ladies…

brh: کسس شڑدی کریکہ کس ئکہ است خواہی آ شڑدی مسکہ اوکا علاوہ اوکا گڈ شڑدی آن سلیمانی چاء مسکہ پالیئو چاء مسکہ گڑا میل تے بیڑارکہ تینا مست ئنا بھلو خر میل اسرکہ ہراکہ میژداراک اسرکہ اوفتا مالک بھلن اسرکہ اوفتے ٹی اوفک
en: Someone would make pastry, and someone would have as much pastry as she wanted. Besides that, after the pastry there was Sulaimani (black) tea and milk tea. Then they would milk the sheep. In their past there were big flocks of sheep; the sheep owners were wealthy people, and among them they...
en_old: Someone would make buttermilk, and someone had buttermilk if she wanted. Besides that, after the buttermilk there was Sulaimani tea and milk tea. Then they would tend the goats. In the past there were big black goats; the livestock owners were wealthy, and among them they…

brh: مختلف قسم نا فائدہ ہرفیرہ آن تا گڑا نیاڑی پڑچے گوافارہ چٹفیرکہ اوپڑچا پدان گڑا پڑچ گیڈ ئنا زیہا بننگ کیک لیو کننگ کیسہ او ہنداکہ پختہ مریک تیر سے تیر ئنا زیہا کرزاک بریرہ کرزان پدا مچھ ئنا ہراکہ پاٹک بریرہ اونا زیہا پڑچے تخسہ پڑچ ئے اول نی کہ ایڑے پن کیسہ پن آن پدا اونا زیہا بریک لیو لیو کیسہ تہ گڑمالہ
en: ...they got many different kinds of use out of them. Then the women would weave the mats and finish them. Once there is a mat, it can go on top of a hut and you can plaster it with mud, and that is how it becomes solid. There is a beam, and on the beam go the rafters; after the rafters go the pieces of palm wood; on top of that you put the mat. First you spread the mat there, and after spreading it the plaster goes on top. You plaster it, and then the 'garmala'...
en_old: They got many different kinds of use out of it. The women would bring dwarf palm and weave it. After the dwarf palm, the palm mat can go on top and be plastered with mud, and that makes it solid. Beam upon beam, then the rafters go on, and after the rafters the palm wood. On top of that you put the dwarf palm. First you lay the leaves here, and after the leaves the mud goes on top. You plaster it with mud, and then it is done.

brh: پارہ تہ لیو پارہ تہ گڑا اوٹی مازو اردو ٹی پارہ تہ چرو نن پانہ تہ چرو خلیسہ کیرہ دیر پر ئنا بریک او وہے پیشتنگے تو ولدا ہراکہ لچغے ہراکہ لیو والا اوٹی پھگ شاغارکہ بھاز کہ تاکہ او گڑا او دیر ئنا ہراکہ سٹ ئس ارے اودے تورے کہ تاکہ اودے دیر کنپ تہ او زو زو چٹیفپ
en: ...as they call it; they call it 'lew' (plaster). Then in it, what in Urdu they call 'mazo' and we call 'charo', they keep applying charo. When rain water comes and seeps through, they would put a lot of chaff into the mud, the plastering mud, so that it holds back whatever water gets in, so that the water does not eat it away and it does not leak so quickly.
en_old: They call it 'leo' (mud plaster); in Urdu they call it something else, and we call it 'charo'. They apply it so that when water comes, the dirt comes out. Then whoever smears the mud puts a lot of straw in it, so that the cracks in it are sealed and the water doesn't get through. And they weave it quickly.

brh: چٹیفیکہ گڑا اودے ولدا لچغ کریرکہ دا پڑچ ئنا فائدک اسرکہ گیڈی شاغارہ تہ نمازی بھی جوڑ مریک آن تہ ہراکہ مسلہ پارہ تہ نمازی جوڑ مریک آ تہ مسجداتے ٹی او بھی بریک مسیتاتے ٹی شاغنگ پڑچ ئنا دا فائدہ غاک اسرکہ اوکاپدا پڑچان پدا بریسہ دا ہراکہ ننا اچ ئنا اسکہ بیش ئنا مس باریم تا
en: When it leaked, they would plaster it with mud again. These were the uses of the mat: they would lay it on huts, and prayer mats are also made from it, what they call musalla; prayer mats are made from it. It is also used in mosques, for spreading in mosques. These were the uses of the mat. After the mats, you come to what we had for our camels and donkeys, their loads...
en_old: They would weave it and then plaster it again. These were the uses of the dwarf palm. They laid down mats, and prayer mats were made from it too. Mats are also put in mosques. These were the uses of the dwarf palm. After the dwarf palm came the things that were part of our…

brh: مسر اوکا پدا کھر ئنا اسکہ ہیٹ تا میل تا ہراکہ رسماک اسرہ اوفتان رسماتان جھلک کریرکہ
en: ...there were. After that came the flock: the goats and the sheep. From the goat hair they had, they would spin on the spinning wheel.
en_old: …there were. After that came the household things made of goat hair, the ropes that existed. From those ropes they would make things.

brh: تنگ جوڑ مسکہ ہموڑان تورہ جوڑ مریکک میل ئنا کھاس آن او لیپ بھی جوڑ مریک میل ئنا کھاس آن لیپ ہمو نیاڑی تا اشر مسکہ گڑا لیپ ئنا گڑا اسہ لیلم نا پچ مریک کنا خیال لیلم نا آہا پین پچ ئس بریک اوٹی گڑا ہندا کھاس تے اسیکہ سلک کھاس تے ولا گڑا جھلک اٹ اوفتے درسا جوڑسا اوفتے
en: Girths were made, and from that sacks are made. From sheep's wool, quilts are also made; quilts are made from sheep's wool. The quilt was the women's communal work. For a quilt there is a piece of 'lilam' cloth, I think lilam, yes, another cloth goes in it. Then they would [prepare] these wools again, take them to the spinning wheel and make them up.
en_old: Girths were made, and sacks were made from goat-hair fibre. The lep (felt rug) is also made from goat-hair fibre, and the women did that. A lep is made from a piece of cloth; I think it is a piece of cloth. Then they would twist these fibres and make them into it.

brh: شیپانک اٹ شیپانک ہمودے کہ لٹ ئس ہشکنو مریک ہراکہ بھاز اور لٹ ئس ڈڈو مریک پنپک دہن ایہن اور شیپانک اٹ دافتے کٹارکہ اسیکہ جوان دافتے خلکرہ یلہ یلہ کل تا تین پہ تین آ پیشتنگارکہ بھاز مسرکہ بھاز مسرکہ گڑا اوفتے ٹی ہندا لیپ ٹی شاغسا گنڈساشاغاگنڈسا
en: With a shipank. A shipank is a dry stick, a hard stick that doesn't break this way or that. With the shipank they would beat the wool well, beating it until it was loose and all separated from each other and there was a lot of it. Then they would put it into this quilt and stitch it, put it in and stitch it.
en_old: With a shipank: a shipank is a dry stick, quite a long stick. They would beat the fibres well with the shipank until they were loose and all separated from each other, and there was a lot of it. Then they would put it into the lep and weave it.

brh: گڑا برامی کہ پوسکن برام تیکہ گڑا لیپ گنڈارکہ گڑا ہخسوس مسکہ لیپاتا کسسے نا ارا گز ئنا مسرکہ اسہ مطلب مسہ چھار گز ئنا مسکہ رلی بھی مسکہ ہندافتے ٹی جوڑارکہ لیپ ہندنو دانا فائدہ سے کہ اسیکا شاغاس تہ پدین مریک زیہاتینا پدا مچہ اوکا پدا باسس
en: Then for brides, for new weddings, they would stitch quilts. The quilts came in different sizes: someone's were two yards, another's three or four yards. There were ralli quilts too, and they made them the same way. The benefit of a quilt like that is that once you lay it down it is cool on top, then a little later it gets warm.
en_old: Then at weddings, for new brides, they would weave a lep. They were special. Each lep was about two yards, or three or four yards. There were quilts (rali) too, and they made those the same way. The good thing about a lep is that once you lay it down and then sit on it…

brh: گڑا باسنگ ئس گچینو کیک گڑا نے یخ اوخس اثر کپک نا زیہا اوخہ نے یخ لگپک تو میل ئنا ہندا فائدہ کو پین بھی میل ئنا کھاس ئنا بھاز مستی دا اینو پھگہ دا پچ بھی ہندافتان بھلو مست ئنا تو ہمو لیپاک اسرکہ جوڑ مسرکہ اوفتا توپین اوہنو بھلو انت الو کہ او مشینری ئے تینا فائدہ ہرفر دا گڑاتان
en: Then it gives a fine warmth, and the cold doesn't affect you much; on top of it you don't feel the cold that much. So these are the uses of the sheep. Sheep's wool was also used a lot in the past; nowadays even this cloth comes from these. In the past those quilts were made because they had nothing else so big, no machinery to use; they got their benefit from these things.
en_old: …it makes a fine seat, and the cold doesn't affect you much; on top of it you don't feel cold. So these are the uses of goat hair. In the past goat-hair fibre was used a lot; today even cloth like this comes from it. So those leps that were made: back then they had no machinery to make these things with.

brh: دو ئنا ہخسوس مسکہ گڑا او گنڈارہ سیلہ غٹ اشر مسکہ اوتینا ہندافتا فائدہ ہرفیرہ کہ
en: Everything was handmade. They stitched it with a needle; it was all communal work. They got the benefit of these things themselves.
en_old: It was handmade; they wove it themselves. All of it was done by the women, and they made use of these things.

brh: لیپان کھاس ئنا اوکا رسم بریک رسم نا ہمو تنگ اسکہ تور اسکہ چٹ بھی جوڑ مریک رسم نا اوبھی بھاز ٹرند مریک اور بھلو وخت خراب دے آن بھی مفک او رسم نا ہراچٹ مریک یا ہراتنگ مریک ہرا کھونٹ کھونٹی پارہ ہرا گدانک جوڑ مریرہ ہرافتے تنگاتان اوتو بھلو وختس خلیرہ اوفتا کنا خیال پائے چٹفپسہ بھی
en: After the wool quilts comes goat hair. From goat hair the girth was made and the sack, and cord is also made from goat hair. It is very strong too, and for a long time it doesn't wear out, even in harsh sun. Goat-hair cord or girth strips, what they call khont or khonti, are used to make tents, and those last a long time. I think they don't leak either...
en_old: After the goat-hair lep comes the rope. From rope you make the girth and the sack, and a rug (chat) is also made from rope. It is very strong and doesn't wear out for a long time, even in bad weather. The rope rug or the girth strips, called khonṭ or khonṭi, are used to make tent panels. Tents made from these girth strips last a long time, and I think water doesn't leak through them…

brh: دیرکہ پر آن چٹفپسہ بھی اسٹ ارٹمیکو اوفتے دے بھی دہن کنپک اینو پھگہ تو بھاز کمے گدان تو کھونٹی والو بھاز ملیک مست ئنا گڑا ہرانا شاہد کھونٹی ٹی گڑا دا ٹیوری ئے خلکرکہ گلیم پاریرکہ گلیم بٹیک مسرہ بٹی تے سرارکہ بٹی نا مون ٹی گڑا اسیکہ گلیم خلکرہ گلیم ئنا داڑا ہنداڑٹ
en: ...rain water doesn't leak through them either. And second, the sun doesn't wear them down like that either. Nowadays there are very few tents left, though khonti tents were found a lot in the past. Then, perhaps in the khonti tent, they had this practice: they called it the gilim. There were bedding stacks; they would arrange the stacks, and in front of the stack they would put a gilim. The gilim's place was here, like this...
en_old: …rain doesn't leak through them, not once or twice. Today very few of these tents are left, though khonṭi tents used to be very common. In the past, in the khonṭi, they did it this way. There was what they called the gilim. The gilim went with the bedding stack: they would stack up the bedding and put the gilim in front of the stack.

brh: مسکہ رسم اٹ ہیٹ ئنا اوٹی گڑا زیہا تہ بٹیس ہرا سرارکہ لیپ ئنا مسکہ چائے کمبل نا مسکہ صورت اونا زیہا بٹی تا زیہا سرارکہ ہنا کمبل ئے او لیپاتے اونا مون ٹی تفوک بسکہ تفوک بھی ہندا اسہ اوٹی شیشہ خلیسہ خوبصورتی کہ چٹ اٹ تفیرہ تہ مون ٹی چٹ نا وا تفوکاتے خلکرکہ
en: It was made of goat hair, from goats. Then on top in it was the stack they arranged, made of quilts or of blankets, whatever form it took. On top of the stacks they would arrange the blankets and the quilts, and in front of it came the stitched work. In the stitched work they would also set mirrors; for beauty they stitched it with thread, and at the front they would put the thread-stitched pieces.
en_old: It was made of goat-hair rope. On top was the stack they arranged, made of leps or blankets. On top of the stack they arranged the blanket and the leps, and the front of it was embroidered. For beauty they embroidered it with mirrors set in, and they put the embroidered pieces at the front…

brh: تاکہ گڑا خنوکا بندغ خنہ کہ دا مطلب چٹ ئٹ تفوک اونا مون ٹی تفوک مسکہ تفوک وا پشم نا چھٹ ئس بریک دسک پشم نا ہموڑے شیشہ نا خش تیٹ پشم خلکرکہ اوٹی چنکو چنکو ستارہ بریک اوفتے خلکرکہ گڑا مطلب گڑا ہموخہ خوبصورت اونا زیبا مسکہ ہراکہ گوفت تفوک مسکہ او زیبا مسکہ گڑا
en: ...so that whoever saw it would see that it was stitched with thread; there was stitching at its front. For the stitching, a woollen thread is used, wool thread; there, along with the bits of mirror, they would add wool, and little stars go in it too, they would add those. So that is how beautiful it was; whatever was woven and stitched was beautiful.
en_old: …so that anyone who looked would see that it was embroidered at the front. The embroidery was done with coloured wool thread. They set mirror pieces with the wool and added small stars, so it became very beautiful. Whatever was stitched and embroidered was beautiful.

brh: خنوکا بندغ خناکہ واقعی دا گودی سے نا بٹی اے اوتینا بٹی اے ہمہ زیبا کرینے
en: Whoever saw it would see that this was truly a lady's bedding stack, and that she had made her stack so beautiful.
en_old: Anyone who looked would see that this was truly a bride's stack, and that she had made her stack so beautiful.

brh: شیف آ ہرا بروک نا شیفا ہرا گلیم بریک مون ٹی بروک نا شیفا چنکو چنکو جاگہ جوڑاکہ تینا گڑاسیکہ تخنگ کہ مطلب تینا نسخل ئس مسکہ چائے تینا او چوریس مسکہ بتیس مسکہ کاریمان پدا تخاکہ تا تینا تینس تافوس چائے چھناسے نا پچ ئس
en: Below, under the part where the gilim comes down in front, she would make small spaces to keep her things: her hand mill, or her bangles, a lamp. After work she would put away her things there: a baking plate, a griddle stone, or a child's clothes...
en_old: Below the bedding, in front where the gilim hangs, they made small spaces to keep their things, meaning their belongings: maybe her shawl, her sandals and so on. After work she would put away her things, such as a piece of sieve cloth…

brh: تینا پین اسہ اوفتا پچ ئس مسکہ تینا بینوکو انتس مسکہ اوفتے ہمو بٹی نازیہا تخاکہ او گلیم ئے زیہاتہ یلہ کریکہ گلیم اودے اندر کریکہ او گلیما گڑا شیشہ خلککہ اوڑا کاریم کریکہ زیبا زیباؤ اوڑا ہندا پشم اٹ جوڑاکہ پھل اٹ اوڑے کیرغان تے گڑاہندا پھل لاڑو کریکہ
en: ...another cloth of hers, whatever she wore, she would keep on top of that stack. She would let the gilim hang loose from above, and the gilim would cover it in. On the gilim mirrors were set, and she would do work on it, very beautiful work. With this wool she would make flowers on it along the bottom, and then she would decorate it with these flowers.
en_old: …another cloth of hers, whatever she wore, and she kept it all on that stack. She let the gilim hang down from above and tucked it in. The gilim had mirror work and beautiful work on it. With that wool they made flowers along the edges, and they made the flowers red.

brh: کیرغانتہ ہندا انتٹ رسم اٹ چٹ چنکو گوفاکہ گڑا شیفان پھل جوڑاکہ اوفتے رنگ کریرکہ رسم نا یکہ او رنگس بریک رنگ کریرکہ اوٹی پوشکنو رنگ بریک اوٹی خیسنو اوٹی پیہنو رنگ مختلف رنگ بریک ٹی تہ تو دا اسہ گدان ٹی مننگ کیک اور گیڈ ٹی مننگ کیک ہر گڑاٹی ہراٹی بٹی تہ
en: Along the bottom, with this, what's it called, with goat hair, she would weave a small cord, and then she would make flowers along the lower edge. They would dye them. Goat hair comes in a color and they would dye it: there is yellow in it, red, white, many different colors go into it. So this can be in a tent, and it can be in a hut, anywhere there is a bedding stack.
en_old: Along the edges they stitched it with fine rope, and below they made flowers and coloured them. The rope came in colours: green, red, white and many others. This could be in a tent or in a mat hut, anywhere there is a bedding stack.

brh: نے ٹی کن ٹی حساب کتاب دہنو مون اف ہم اور دہنو ہیت ہم افک کہ بھئی نن کان میڈیا نا ایڑے سر مرین حساب کتاب کین کہ بھئی دا ہیت ننا بسنے داڑے حساب کتاب کرینے ای نی دہن رمب ہم کننگ کپنہ دہنو کسر ہم پٹنگ کپنہ کہ کان او جاگہ غاتے آ سر مرین ہرا جاگہ غاتے آ کہ میڈیا ننا ہیتے دیک سر کیکک
en: Neither you nor I have that kind of standing, nor that kind of clout, brother, that we could go and reach the media and get things sorted out, saying, brother, this matter of ours has come up, this has been done here. You and I can't run around like that either, nor can we find that kind of path to go and reach those places, the places the media takes our words to and gets them heard.
en_old: Neither you nor I have such a face, nor such standing, brother, that we could reach out somewhere other than through the media, that, brother, this matter of ours has come, has happened here; you and I can't make such an effort, nor find such a way to reach those places where the media delivers our words.

brh: تو باقی بھازو جوانو گڑاسے اور میڈیا آن ہندا کہ ننا اسہ انتے کہ بھئی نی ننا توار ہم مرک حق ئنا ہرا حساب کتابے نی خننگ ٹی اس کس سے تون نا انصافی مننگ ٹی اے نا جائز اوتو مننگ ٹی ای دہن مروئی الو تہ دہن مننگ ٹی اے تو نی اونا توار مرک اونا ہراکہ دا ٹائما انتے حساب کتابے نی
en: So otherwise it is a very good thing, and from the media we ask this, um, that, brother, you be our voice too. In matters of rights, whatever you see, if injustice is being done to someone, if something wrongful is being done to them, if it shouldn't be like this but it is happening like this, then you become their voice, their, um, at this time, the, um, you...
en_old: So the rest is a very good thing. And from the media we ask this, brother, that you also be our voice, for the right; whatever you see, if injustice is happening to someone, something wrongful is happening to them, if it shouldn't be like this but it is happening like this, then be their voice, at this time

brh: اونا توار مرک اونا ایلم مرک اوتو نی ہن سنگت مرک نی اونا توارے ہم سر کرک اونا کمک جوڑمرک
en: Become their voice, become their brother, go along with them and be their friend, make their voice heard too, become their helper.
en_old: be their voice, be their brother, go and be their friend, make their voice heard too, become their helper.

en_old: and joking all over the place here, so that I... But I said, hey, this guy told me don't joke around, keep quiet, so he's scolding me. I said, okay, enough, let it be. Then here he told Muzaffar bhai, hey, you did wrong, you shouldn't have said that to him. I said, hey, we come here to have fun

brh: ہراتم میٹرک اسکا بریک۔ میٹرک ئے ہم انت برحالی اٹ خوانک، خواننگ پد ولدا ہچ اودے دا گڑا اف کہ ای تینا یانزدہ دوانزدہ جماعت ئے، سینزدہ ئے چانڑدہ ئے ای امہ خوانو، ای مونا ہمہ پیش تمو۔
en: When he gets as far as matric — and even matric he studies in such hardship — after studying, again he has no means, so (he wonders) how will I study my eleventh, twelfth grade, thirteenth, fourteenth, how will I go further ahead?
en_old: When he reaches matric, he studies even matric in a bad state, and after studying he again has no means to say, "I will study my eleventh, twelfth, thirteenth, fourteenth grade like this and go ahead like that."

brh: تو لائخی کریٹہ، اسٹ تو ننا علاقہ نا ٹھکری، نواب، میر، معتبر دا گڑا ئے دا گڑائے پو مفک کہ دا چنا کائہہ مونا خوانہ۔ ولدا ہموعلاقہ نا ہراکہ انتظامیہ اے اونا زیا دا گڑا مریک کہ دافتے سہولت ایتہ، دافتے بجلی نا مرے، دافتے سکول ئس مرے، دافتے کولج ئس مرے، دافتا علاقہ تے ٹی یونیورسٹیس مرے۔
en: So I would be capable. First, the clan heads (takris), nawabs, mirs and notables of our area do not understand (accept) this, this thing, that this child should go ahead and study. Then, as for the administration of that area, its responsibility is this: that it should give them facilities, that they should have electricity, that they should have a school, a college, that there should be a university in their areas.
en_old: So it should be like this: first, the tribal chiefs of our area, the nawabs, mirs and notables, don't want these children to move forward through education. Then there is the administration of that area, which has the responsibility to provide them facilities, to give them electricity, schools and colleges, and universities in their areas.

brh: داسا داخس بھلو بلوچستان ئس اے۔ داٹی کوئٹہ ٹی یونیورسٹیس اے، خضدارٹے اسہ یونیورسٹیس اے۔ تو دا چناک ہرانگ کار۔ اوکان علاوہ کالج نا داسا ای نمے اسہ مثالس ایتوہ کہ ننا علاقہاتے ٹی اینو اسکا ہچو ڈاکٹرئسے نا سہولت اف اور ہچو دہنو پروفیسر، لیکچرر ہراقابلومریر ہنا چنات ئے خوانفر، ہنا چنات ئے مونی راہی کیر، مونی کیر۔
en: Now, Balochistan is such a big (province). In it there is a university in Quetta, and there is one university in Khuzdar. So where should these children go? Apart from that, about colleges — now let me give you an example: in our areas, to this day, there is no facility of any doctor, and there are no such professors or lecturers who are capable, who would teach our children, send our children forward, take them forward.
en_old: Now, Balochistan is this big. There is a university in Quetta and one university in Khuzdar. So where are these children supposed to go? Besides colleges, let me give you an example: in our areas, to this day, there is no doctor available, and there are no professors or lecturers capable enough to teach our children, guide them forward and help them progress.

brh: ننا علاقہ ٹی اسہ وار اگہ اللہ کپ کس نیاڑیسے دا نیاڑی بے جان اے، دانا چنا خننگ نا ٹیم بریکک تو دابریک تینا خلق ان بریک شہر ئٹی، شہر ئٹی بس داڑے بس پارہ تہ کہ ہچو لیڈی ڈاکٹر ئس اف۔ ببا داسا دادئے ارانگ دین۔
en: In our area, once, if — God forbid — someone's woman, this woman is weak and ill, and the time comes for her to give birth, then she comes from her village to the city, and in the city they just tell her here that there is no lady doctor at all. Brother, now where do we take her?
en_old: In our area, if God forbid a woman is ill and it's time for her to give birth, she comes from her village to the city, and in the city they just tell her there's no lady doctor here. Now, brother, take her somewhere.

brh: ببا دادے نی قلات ان کراچی آ دریا کوئٹہ غا در یا خضدارآ دتہ۔
en: Brother, you take her from Kalat to Karachi, or take her to Quetta, or take her to Khuzdar.
en_old: Brother, take her from Kalat to Karachi, or Quetta, or Khuzdar.

brh: او ہندنو ٹیم ئسے ہراکہ اودوران دا خضدارے سر مرے یا کراچی ئے سر مرے یا قلات ئے ہناڑے کہک۔ تو دا مقصد داداے کہ اگہ اینو تعلیم مسکہ، شعور مسکہ علاقہ نا ہر نوجوان ڈاکٹر جوڑ مسرہ، ہر نوجوان پروفیسر، لیکچرار جوڑ مسرہ۔
en: And it takes such a long time that in the meantime, whether she reaches Khuzdar, or reaches Karachi, or Kalat, she dies there. So the point is this: if today there had been education, if there had been awareness, every young person of the area would have become a doctor, every young person would have become a professor, a lecturer.
en_old: That takes so long that by the time she reaches Khuzdar, Karachi or Kalat, she dies along the way. So the point is that if there were education and awareness today, every young person in the area would become a doctor, every young person would become a professor or a lecturer.

brh: بھاز بھلو بد قسمتی نا ہیت داد اے کہ پیشن نا ملک ئنا مخلوق ہرا کہ جوانو خوانندہ ؤ بھلو افسرئس اے، ہراکہ جوانو اسہ ادارہ سے ٹی سر مسنے ہمودے اسکالرشپ آ خوائفک، پیسہ ایتک کہ کنا مخلوق ئےشعور برے کن،ا مخلوق ئے خوانفبو، کنا مخلوق مونا برے۔
en: The very great misfortune is this: in foreign countries, whoever among the people is well educated and a big officer, whoever has reached a good position in an institution, he gets others educated on scholarships, gives money, so that my people gain awareness — let's educate my people, so that my people come forward.
en_old: The very unfortunate thing is that in foreign countries, people who are well educated and senior officers, who have reached good positions in an institution, educate others on scholarships, and give money saying: bring awareness to my people, educate my people, let my people move forward.

brh: اور ننے اسکا بھاز بھلو ہنا بدقسمتیس اے کہ نن تینا علاقہ نا اینواسکا ننے اسکا نئے ڈاکٹر ارے او نہ ننے اسکان نئے لیکچراریا پروفیسر ارے۔ داسا نی ہنا پا کہ ننا ہراکہ پروفیسراو، ننا لیکچراراک او، ننا چنا داسا برے لاہور آ یا داڑے برے اسلام آباد آ او اراکا افورڈ کننگ کیک داخہ اوڑتو اراخہ ارے پیسہ۔
en: And it is such a great misfortune for us that in our own area, to this day, we have neither a doctor nor a lecturer or professor. Now look at it this way: to have our own professors, our own lecturers, our child now has to come to Lahore, or come here to Islamabad. Who can afford that much? How much money does he have?
en_old: And it is a great misfortune for us that in our area, to this day, we have neither doctors nor lecturers or professors. Now consider this: our professors, our lecturers, our children now go to Lahore or to Islamabad. Who can afford that? Who has that kind of money?

brh: ہرا مزدورئس اے بیچارہ مچا دے تینا کائک، د-دیہاڑی ئے تینا خلیک اونا داخسو ہچو حیثیت ئس مننگ کپک کہ او تینا چنا ئے خوانفہ۔ تینا بھازبھلو ایڑے غریب اے نرینہ نیاڑی۔ جذبہس بھلو ارے بدقسمتی داد اے کہ چنا اسکا سہولت ئس اف۔
en: A laborer, a poor man, who goes out all day and earns his daily wage — he can never have such means that he could educate his child. They are very, very poor there, husband and wife. The desire is great; the misfortune is that the child still has no facilities.
en_old: A poor laborer who works all day and earns a daily wage can never afford to educate his children. Both husband and wife are very poor. The passion is great, but the misfortune is that there are no facilities for the children.

brh: ہراتم کہ علاقہ ٹی کل ان مست نا سکول جوڑ مرور، نا علاقہ ٹی نا یونیورسٹیک جوڑ مرور، نا علاقہ ٹی ادارہ غاک جوڑ مرور۔
en: When, first of all, your schools are built in the area, your universities are built in your area, institutions are built in your area,
en_old: When first of all schools are built in your area, universities are built in your area, institutions are built in your area.

brh: نئے کہ ارا بھازبھلو فائدہس مرو۔ داسا نی ہمو علاقہ نا کل ان مست تینا یونیورسٹی نا، تیناکولج نا، تینا ہاسپٹل نا نی کوشش ئے کیسہ، کل ان مست رکاوٹہ ہمو جاگہ نا مخلوق مریک، کل ان مست انتئے کہ ہرکہ ٹھکری اے، نواب ئے سڑدارئے، میر معتبراے، اون چناک پیشن نا ملک ئٹی خواننگ او۔
en: then it will be of very great benefit to you. Now, when you first of all make an effort for your own university, your own college, your own hospital in that area, the first obstacle is the people of that very place — first of all because whoever is a clan head (takri), a nawab, a sardar, a mir or a notable, their children are studying in foreign countries.
en_old: That will be of great benefit. Now, when you try to get a university, a college, a hospital in that area first, the first obstacle is the people of that very place, because the tribal chiefs, nawabs, sardars, mirs and notables have their children studying abroad.

brh: اونا ہرا زالکار اے پیشن نا ملک ئٹین او۔ اوفتے ہچو پرواہس اف کہ غریب، اوتے ہچو پرواہس اف کہ غریب خوانہ مونا کائہہ۔
en: Their womenfolk are in foreign countries. They have no concern that the poor — they have no concern whether the poor study and go forward.
en_old: Their families live abroad. They don't care at all about the poor; they don't care whether the poor get educated and move forward.
